text: WHen the Emperour of Turkie, forſaking Conſtantinople, ſetteth forewarde vnto anye warre, he taketh with him two tentes, called Satorlar, that one this day, may be pitched at the next place of taryinge, when the daye folowing, he purpoſeth to be receyued.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: OReanes ſecōd Emperour of the Turkes, was ſubtil & wittye, he inuented ſondrye ſortes of inſtrumentes and Enginnes of warre, and gouerned the Empire two & twentie yeares.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: Whether, after the contine wance of certaine monethes, he iorneyed, his mother him accūpanying, at what time, through his floriſhinge in youthelye yeares and vertue, he was thoughte, in ye opinion, & iudgement of al men, by ſome heauenly prouidence, to be geuen and ſente vnto their countrye.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: And the names of lordes of the meaner condition are Spahalar, Sauſlar, Eminler, Behram, Memmi Mehē met, Alli, Ahmat, Tcielebi, Paiazith, Chatſun, Hutſcref.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: Beſydes the infinite riches geuē to the buildinge of that princely vvoorke, commonly called the Burſe, vvhich already declareth, and in Lōdon is openly to be ſēne. vvhat commodity generaly, it vvill bringe to the Citiſens therof.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: Howbeit by the lawes, he hym ſelfe is bounde, after euery thrée yeares, to take a voiage into the chriſtian realmes, eyther for amplifyinge or defence of his kyngedome and dominion.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: But as manye as come vnto the prayer Church, ought firſt to waſhe their handes, féete, and pryuy partes: after ye thriſe they ſprincle water vpon their beades, rehearſinge theſe wordes: Elhemdu Lillahi, wiche is, glorie be to my God.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: And whereby the better to conceale and clooke this matter, ſhée fitelye prouided all thinges to be attempted by Ruſtanus, whiche continually hadde the charge of weightie affaires about ye king neither were ther anye craftye meanes priuy vnto him, whiche he applied not for the deſtruction and accuſemēt of the young men.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: Certaine laborers do make way for the Armie to paſſe, placing heapes of ſtones, or piles of woode, on euery ſyde, as tokens of the waye, in ſomuch that in the darke, they can ſcarſe ſtraye out of the waye.
author: Georgijević, Bartolomej, d. ca. 1566.
title: The ofspring of the house of Ottomanno and officers pertaining to the greate Turkes court. Whereunto is added Bartholomeus Georgieuiz Epitome, of the customes rytes, ceremonies, and religion of the Tu

text: But this haue I sayde hytherto agayne Crassus, let hym loke vpō this mater how he maye be an emperour. where as reason and trueth in dede cō uinceth hym that he is no gentyl man nor free harted man.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: But he brought to passe by breue and lytle questiōs (and as a man wolde say) by sharpe poyntes the thing that he purposed.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: Nor I wyll not say yt a man hath loste his goodes / if he haue lost his cattell / or his householde stuffe.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: This prouerbe notable is vsed of well lerned men, whose authoryte I wolde not vse yf I shulde make this oracion before some rude persons.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: I Haue many tymes notedde and marked / my famylyare Brutus, Marcus Cato, thy vncle / whan he shewed his mynde in the Senate / entrate of matters of grauite taken out of phylosophy / far distant fro this exercise of oratory in the iudiciall place & touchyng the cōmon welthe.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: For where it ys sayde of syngler lerned men / that no man is a free man except he be wyse.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: And callest thou me a banisshed mā aft thi name? where as all mē iudged yt ye comē welthe was banisshed bi mi deꝑtīg thēs? wil thou neuer loke about ye thou starke mad man? will thou neuer considre what thou doest? or what thou saist?
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: For a certente, to lyue well and welthyly / is nothyng els, but to lyfe honest lye and iustly.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: I haue sene Caius Mariꝰ whiche semed to me in tyme of ꝓsperite / one of the foriunate men, and in aduersite / one of very excellent men.
author: Cicero, Marcus Tullius.
title: [The paradox of Marcus Tullius Cicero, latelye translated out of the laten tonge by R. whitinton.]

text: Let no man thinke that ſuch things do come by chance or fortune, but that they are appointed to be meſſengers of enſuing plagues which are like to fall vpon vs, except with repenting harts we turne vn to our Godand forſake our wicked waies.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: For you ſhall vnderſtand that after the former perill was paſt, newe panges began to ariſe vpon the ſorrowful woman in ſuch ſort that it cauſed a lamentation among all the wiues.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: I make bould with you, but if it like you to doe mee this fauour, you ſhall command mee any thing that lieth in my power to performe.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: At Outthorne in Holderneſſe the 12. of Februarie laſt paſt, by the meanes of wind and weather a wonderfull huge fiſh was driuen on the ſandes, of ſuch hugeneſſe as hath not been ſeene, being a fiſh of an vnknowne name.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: The people of the countrey came in great aboundance to behold this ſtraunge fiſh, marueling thereat, not knowing what to ſaye or iudge therof, but onely reſolueth them ſelues that it was ſent of God to ſome great purpoſe.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: SUch is the mercifullneſſe of our God that he wil neuer puniſh any people or nation without warning firſt ſent vnto them.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: This fiſh was in length 19. yeardes and three quarters, and in thickneſſe at the middle 10. yeardes good meaſure.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: Alſo a cowe being carried into the temple for ſacrifice, calued a Lambe in ſight of al the people.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: The Lord be mercifull to this our Countrey of England, vnto whom our moſt louing God hathe giuen many warninges, yea as many as euer Ieruſalem had, and yet we continue in our former ſinnes.
author: Duncalfe, V.
title: A most certaine report of a monster borne at Oteringham in Holdernesse, the 9. of Aprill last past. 1595. Also of a most strange and huge fish, which was driuen on the sand at Outhorn in Holdernesse i

text: Their both bodies dead (moſt fearfull ſpestacle) Moſes cauſeth be men in readines To be caſt out, fare frome the tabernacle, For ſo to be an exempell ſport les.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: Dauid willeth not, auenge him of his kinge, Allthought it laieth in his power vtterlie: Onlie on him the great daunger hanging, Of him in care, sheweth him faithfullie.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: Of treaſon sheweth the falſe talking coured Achitophel, that Dauid innocent Abſalon taketh, but all is diſcoured: Wherfor for fear, ſtraight to hange himſelf went.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: Iacob leauing Laban ſoon cometh awai, Rachel ſoftlie her idole taketh with her: Laban after goeth and cerche them that dai: But findeth nothing wherfor kiſſeth them both ther.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: The kinges daughter fonde him in great pitie The ruſshes amonge, wiche to him fauourable, As god did pleaſe, him to ſaue thought worthie, His owne mother giuing him for nource able.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: Of all iowels Pharaon abonding, To be clothed Ioſeph cauſeth and araied, Him of the worlde ſauiour be name calling, Maketh him of his to be woorshipped and praied.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: The quene cometh frome Saba, for to heare Salomon kinge, and his diuin conning: Wiche being hard, wonderfull did apeare: Preſentes therfor riche mad, him fauouring.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: In wildernes Helie ſeeth an Aungell, Water, and bread shewing him, in that whill: Be whoſe vertue, after he hath eate well, Cometh to the top of Oreb goddis hill.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: Abraham then Agar without faintiſe Knoweth in deed, be Saras owne counſaill: Great that she is here mastreſſe doeth dispiſe: Wherfor greate ſo muſt flie with muche trauaill.
author: Paradin, Claude, 16th cent.
title: A true and lyuely historyke purtreatures of the vvoll Bible

text: After he ſaw this incontynēt by certayn marchaūt men whych were wonte to be cōuerſant in Inde with the Portyngales, whyche he before hadde made hys frendes, he wrote ſecretely vnto the capytayne Alfonſus Dalbuberque, certifyeng hym as diligētly as he could how it ſtode with him.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: For yf ſo be yt there be any ſo obſtynate a perſone that he careth not for the curſe, but that not wythſtandynge he leueth not from the cryme for whych he ſo was accurſed: his meate and drynke ſhall be taken from hym, and he ſo compelled to dye for famyne.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: Now after I was fully acquaynted wyth thys Roderyke Ferdynāde, & eche had ſhewed a nother others beſineſſe I happened to ſpeke of his legacy into Germany, chaūſed vs alſo to fall in cōmunycacyon of Inde.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: The fyrſte, in all thoſe regyons (as great as they be) from the ſee of Araby, to the water of Gange, there be but two languages, that is to wit, Perſyke and Arabyke. whyche languages who ſo perfytely knoweth, may eaſely paſſe thorough all thoſe prouynces.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: But after we had mych debated this mater, your holynes putte wel in mynde of the high emperour of Inde preſter Iohn̄.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: Two yere after I hadde done the kynges grace ſeruyce in that offyce, I was by at all this as other of the court were, and both harde ſaw and vnderſtode all, as myche at leſte ways as my yonge and tender age wolde gyue me leue.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: I toke theym, and as well as I could, haue tranſlated them out of the Portyngale tonge into latyne.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: Ieſu Cryſte be your ayde, helpe, & ſuccour, for the thynges that ye haue done in Inde / be ſurely more by goddes myght then mannis.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: Dauid kynge of kynges, kynge of the Ebeſſins, preſter Iohn̄, kynge of kynges vnto the Ebeſſyns and of all his prouynces, both nexte and alſo at the ende of the ſees.
author: Góis, Damião de, 1502-1574.
title: The legacye or embassate of the great emperour of Inde prester Iohn, vnto Emanuell kynge of Portyngale, in the yere of our lorde M. v.C.xiii. Of the fayth of the Indyans, ceremonyes, relygyons []c. Of

text: Not the les seyng the miserie so greit apperyng, and the calamitie sa neir approching, I thoght it les fault, to incur the crime of surmounting my priuate estate, then the blame of neglecting the publik danger.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: Thairfoir I chesid rather to vnderly the opinion of presumptioun in speiking, thē of treson in silence, and specially of sic thingis as euin seme presently to redound to the perpetuall schame of your Lordschippes, distructioun of this royall estaite, and ruyne of the hole cōmoun welth of Scotland.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: IT may seme to your Lordschippis, that I melling with heigh materis of gouerning of common welthis do pas mine estait, being of sa meane qualitie, and forgettis my dewtie, geuing counsall to the wisest of this Realme.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: And albeit that Schir Iames to make him self clene of that suspitioun, soght many diueris wayis to the distructioun of the Erle of Arrane hys brother, yit he could neuer cōqueis the Kingis fauour, vntill finallie he was executid for tresoun, and tooke ane miserabill end conforme to his vngodly lyfe.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: And seing he durst not at sic a time put tham downe by tyrannie, he offerit tham to the sword of the enemy to be slaine by tham.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: In the begynnyng of hys gouernement the Quene and hir mother wer keipit by hym, rather lyke presoneris then Princessis, but yit that incommoditie was caus of preseruyng of the Quenis lyfe, he beleifing to mary hir on his sone.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: For the king was yong, lusty, and redy to auenture his persoun to all hasardis, baith by sea and land, in down putting of theifis, and vpsetting of Iustice.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: Maist like thinking, as if they honourit not the doar, thay should nat be knawin as counsallouris of the deid, and wald tyne the glorie of that nobill acte.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: Thay do schaw also how crueltie & auarice haue blindit tham that thay cā not se in bringyng a tyranne to haue power ouer thame, seyng thay pretending neyrest clame to the crowne, should be neirest the danger.
author: Buchanan, George, 1506-1582.
title: Ane admonition direct to the trew Lordis mantenaris of the Kingis graces authoritie. M.G.B.

text: Ye ſhal alſo keep the Queenes peace in your owne perſons, ye ſhall know no gatheringes, conuenticles nor conſpiracies, made againſt the Queenes peace, but ye ſhal warne the Maior thereof or let it to your power.
author: City of London (England).
title: The othe of every free man, of the cittie of London

text: Ye ſhal be contributorie to all manner of charges within this Citie, as ſummons, watches contributions, taskes, tallages, lot and ſcot, and al other charges, bearing your part as a free man ought to do.
author: City of London (England).
title: The othe of every free man, of the cittie of London

text: Ye ſhal colour no forreines goods, vnder or in your name, whereby the Queene or this Citie, might or may looſe their cuſtomes or aduantages.
author: City of London (England).
title: The othe of every free man, of the cittie of London

text: The Franchiſes and cuſtomes thereof ye ſhall maintain, and this Citie keep harmeles in that that in you is.
author: City of London (England).
title: The othe of every free man, of the cittie of London

text: All theſe pointes and Articles yee ſhall well and truelie keepe, according to the lawes and cuſtomes of this Citie, to your power.
author: City of London (England).
title: The othe of every free man, of the cittie of London

text: And not when he doth delyte to here ydle speche / fables / tales or lyes or fylthy comunynge / or any euyll of his neyghbour.
author: Goodale, John, attributed name. aut
title: [Here begynneth a lytell treatyse called, the (myrrour or lokynge glasse of lyfe) for co[m]fortyng of the soule]

text: And wyllyngly he offred his moste precyous bo dy on the crosse / vnto the deth for vs / whtche at that tyme was the moste shamphullest deth that myght be deuysed.
author: Goodale, John, attributed name. aut
title: [Here begynneth a lytell treatyse called, the (myrrour or lokynge glasse of lyfe) for co[m]fortyng of the soule]

text: And not when he tasteth meates or drynkes and taketh therof vnmesurably / where throughe he is the worse to serue god / and the more nedy to enclyne to vyce or synne.
author: Goodale, John, attributed name. aut
title: [Here begynneth a lytell treatyse called, the (myrrour or lokynge glasse of lyfe) for co[m]fortyng of the soule]

text: O lorde what deedly and intollerable deth is hangynge ouer the heedes of the ryche / whiche shal not auoyde that charge: wherof god taketh so great vnkyndnes.
author: Goodale, John, attributed name. aut
title: [Here begynneth a lytell treatyse called, the (myrrour or lokynge glasse of lyfe) for co[m]fortyng of the soule]

text: And so wylfully wyll auoyde it selfe from all trewth / lyght and vertue / and foloweth the dampnable pleasure of his carnall body / and ouerdryn keth hym selfe of the bytter deth perpetuall.
author: Goodale, John, attributed name. aut
title: [Here begynneth a lytell treatyse called, the (myrrour or lokynge glasse of lyfe) for co[m]fortyng of the soule]

text: Also be the place neuer so holy / and the pyc ture or ymage / appere neuer so gloryous or curyous in syght / be you well ware of any truste or confydence in them: for in so doynge you dyshonoure god / as apperyth exodi. (32. chapitre.

text: No wyſe man entreth into a gardeyne, but he ſone eſpieth good herbes from nettils, and treadeth the nettils vnder his feete, whiles he gadreth good herbes: wherby he taketh no damage.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: But yf men wolde nowe applye the fyrſte parte of their youthe, that is to ſaye from ſeuen yeres to twentie, effectually in the ſcyences liberall, and knowlege of hyſtoryes, they ſhoulde reuiue the aunciente fourme as welle of daunſynge, as of other exerciſes.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: And that haue we in dayly experience. for the pannes and pottes, garnyſſhe well the ketchyn, and yet ſhuld they be to the chā bre none ornamente.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: Wherfore vndoutedly, the beſt and the moſt ſure gouernāce, is by one King or Prince, whiche ruleth onely for the weale of his people: and that maner of guernaunce is beſte approued, and hath longeſt continued, and is moſte auncient.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: NOwe wil I ſpeke of CONTINENCS, whiche is ſpecially in refraynynge or forbearynge the acte of carnall pleaſure, whervnto a man is feruently meued, or is at libertie to haue it.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: And whan the Oratour wolde haue hadde Phocions ſonne, to haue taken the money, Phocion anſwered, If his ſonne wolde be lyke vnto him, he ſhuld haue no nede, neyther of that money, nor of none other.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.

text: Themiſtocles, one of the princis of Athenes, a moche noble capitayne, ſayde vnto the people, that he had aduyſed hym ſelfe of an excellente counſayle, where vnto if fortune inclyned, nothynge mought more augment the power of the Athenienſis.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.
title: The boke named the Gouernour, deuysed by syr Thomas Elyot knight

text: To the ruynous towre all moſte cometh none, Of emotes innumerable vneth thou findeſt one In emty barnes, and where fayleth ſubſtaunce Hapneth no frende, in whom is aſſuraunce.
author: Elyot, Thomas, Sir, 1490?-1546.

text: The riche man wold not once vouchſafe, to take hym into his houſe, to releue hym, but god doth vouchſafe to take hym, to ſuche a place, where is euerlaſtyng felicitie & glory.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.

text: Let vs conſider, vs (I ſay) whiche either bee, or oughte to bee very Chriſtians, lette vs marke well, and depely conſider, what thynges bee taught in this parable for our inſtructions and lerninges, and let vs beleue the doctrines of theſame to bee moſte true.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.

text: We ſhall perceiue that al the goodes and ſubſtance that is on the earth, is the Lordes and not ours, and that we be but balliefes and Stuardes of theſame, to beſtowe them after his wyll and not after our owne wyll, & that on payne of damnacion.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.

text: Here wee bee taught alſo to be merciful to the pore in diſtributyng & miniſtring to theym thoſe gods goodes lent vs for theſame purpoſe.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.

text: What ye haue receiued at goddes handes, & how that ye vſe ſuch thynges ſo receiued, ye muſte remember alſo, that he that dothe receiue muche at his lordes handes, muſte geue a compte of muche.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.
title: A funerall sermon that was prepared to haue b[i]ne preached, by Robert King doctour in diuinit[y] for a cert[e]in honourable lady then almoste deade, but afterward recouered, to who[m] in writing this

text: They maye well bee called the riche of this worlde, for they ſhalbe poore beggers in the other worlde, forthey make no preparacion here, that they may be riche there.
author: King, Robert, d. 1557.

text: This obiection is anſwered to partely before, but heareafter it ſhalbe anſwered fully, that neither the gooddes that thou haſte in thy poſſeſſyon, are thy gooddes, but goddes gooddes, and are not geuen the to be beſtowed at thy pleaſure, but at goddes pleaſure.

text: Wherfore my thynke it is inough to proue to a Christened man, that the welthy state of this worlde is vayne and ieoperdous, by cause Christe so teacheth and preacheth, and surely a greater profe by reason for this matter with you I wyll not vse atte this tyme.

text: For money maketh all, and ruleth as a god, Wiche ought not to be, for Chriſte it forbod, And bad, that we ſhoulde take nothyng in hande, But for the lordes loue and welthe of the lande.
title: A compendious dittie wherin the state of mans lyfe is briefely touchid.

text: For moneie is cauſe of murder and thefte, Of batayle and bloudſhed, whiche wold god wer left, Of rauine, of wronge, of falſe wytueſſe bearyng, Of treaſon conſpired, and eke of forſwearyng.

text: I would his mother had not knowne, His father Priam, or that she, So foule a firebrand had not borne, As he to Troy is like to be: Would she had dreamed of his death, Or wisely she had stopt his breath.

text: My tongue doth tremble for to tell, The villanie that they inuent, My heart (alas) with griefe doth swell, To see braue men so beastly bent, From this their wicked trechery, The Lord aboue deliuer me.

text: My father eke doth me accuse, And saies, I do my wooers wrong: And too too much my selfe abuse, Sith widdow-like I stay so long.

text: Ah when to Troy my true-loue wend, He left me shining maiden like, But when that he doth backward bend, He sure shal find-me beldam-like: But Ioue I thanke thy glorious grace, For this my wrinkling sorrowed face.

text: Now gif ȝe pleis Cummers I fall begin This ſame cauld nicht to tak ane of thame in, We knaw thame not (quod thay) hot tak ȝe ane We muſt not leif the vther bird alane.

text: Away ſum ſayis to Veneis is he gone, Or to the Swiſches as thay do ſuppone, Quhair he is ſaif from danger, hurt, or ſkaith, Heir wald he deit of cauld and hounger baith, Thus am I left as wedow in diſtres, For commoun weill, my bairnis left Fatherles.

text: It ſuld be ȝe Mother, it ſuld be ȝe To quhome the pepill ſuld giue eir and Ee, It ſuld be ȝe ſchortly I ſay no moir, That to all vertewis ſuld ȝow Indeuoir.

text: For the drift and ſcope of all his doinges, is to make vs keepe our eares ſhut, againſt that which the Lorde doeth ſpeake plainely vnto vs out of his woorde, that we may onely reuerence theſe rydles, that proceede from him ſelfe.
author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

text: And if they were ſo ſtrengthleſſe, as they be ſuppoſed: yet the ſwarmes of them ſhoulde cauſe men to bee waking, vnleſſe they haue forgotten, that neither all the wiſedome nor power of Egypt, was able to reſiſte the armie of Lice, which the Lorde ſente againſte them.
author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

text: And like as wee haue no ſtay for our ſelues, no more haue me any good weapon, wherwith either to beare of an aduerſary, or to make an aſſault againſt a deadly and ſworne enimie.
author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

author: Knewstubs, John, 1544-1624.

text: The thynges that are called, and in dede also are indifferent, howbeit a god ly mā may vse them frely and in euery place and at all tymes, yet not withstandynge he shulde vse them with knowlage and of charitie to the glory of God trewly, and the edificaciō of the churche and congregacion.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And yf any man wyll attempte to corrupte the trewe meanynge of this oure confession he shall heare bothe a confession and a defēce of the veritie & truth.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And so confyrmeth and stablissheth it, so it belōgeth to the magistrate to se that it be worthely bothe begonne and worshypped, and not broken but for a iust cause.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And these so godly benifites with the very sanctificacion of the holy spirite, do we optayne by fayth, the very trewe gyfte of God, and not throughe any other power or strength of oure selues or merytes.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And therfore we make it free for all men to vse theyr owne sorte of speaking as they shall perceyue moste profitable for theyr churches, and we shall vse the same libertie.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And that by the holy supper of thā kes, called howselynge, the faithe of the godly be ofte exersysed, and that they shulde be contynually in prayer for all men, and for the necessities of all men.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: Also do we acknowlage and confesse hym onely to be our attonement and raunsome, satisfaction, expiacion, or wysdome, our defence, and our onely deliuerer, refusyng vtterly all other meane of lyfe and saluacion, excepte thus by Chryst onely.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And therfore in the whole doctryne of the euangelystes anūnciat and shew to be the fyrste, and chefely to be inculcated and taught that we are safe onely by the marcie of God, and merite of our sauiour Christ.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: And as he onely is oure mediatour, and entercessour, hoste and sacrifice, bysshop, lorde, and our kynge.
author: Schweizerischer Evangerlischer Kirchenbund.
title: The confescion of the fayth of the Sweserla[n]des

text: For the Almicantares begin frō the Horizon & thēce grow leſſe & leſſe til they come to nothing at the Zenith, as the parallells grow frō thequinoctiall to the pole, where they end at 90, ſo that euer the Horizō circle is the firſt or 0 Almicātare.

text: As to the example before mentioned, where according to the altit. of the ☉ taken 25 degree high by the Zenitfer prepared to that 25 altit. and the pointer applyed on the Sun his place at K, his nooneline ſhewed in the howercircle 10 of clock.

text: The Third difficultie and materiall matter is as it ſeemeth for any latitvde aſſigned to prepare the Zenitfer to any Altitude taken, taught in the 13 Cap. thereby to knowe what hower of the day or night it is and ſuch like queſtions.
author: Blagrave, John, d. 1611.
title: An apollogie confirmation explanation and addition to the Vranicall astrolabe by the author.

text: And your Curſor thus planted at D C and the poynter diſtaunt from C according to the quantitye C Q ſo is your Zenitfer prepared for that 25 altitude in this 52 latitude.

title: An apollogie confirmation explanation and addition to the Vranicall astrolabe by the author.

text: All which this my Ʋranicall Aſtrolabe ſo effectually, ſo plauſibly, ſo pleaſingly, ſo eaſily, and ſo ſuffitiently performeth.
author: Blagrave, John, d. 1611.
title: An apollogie confirmation explanation and addition to the Vranicall astrolabe by the author.

text: Then for the Azimuth work in all reſpects as is done laſt before, and you ſhall find the meeting of the pearle and pointer at G. will fall out in the centre line L. M. extended.

title: An apollogie confirmation explanation and addition to the Vranicall astrolabe by the author.
