author: Fisher, John, of Chester.
title: The copy of a letter describing the wonderful woorke of God in deliuering a mayden within the city of Chester, from an horrible kinde of torment and sicknes 16. of february 1564

text: At the last Maister Lane called for viniger, wherat the stāders by marueiled, saying, that yt thing with muche more had bene often tymes attempted, but to no purpose.
author: Fisher, John, of Chester.
title: The copy of a letter describing the wonderful woorke of God in deliuering a mayden within the city of Chester, from an horrible kinde of torment and sicknes 16. of february 1564

text: Neyther did eate during the time of her sycknes, but once in ech xxiiii. houres, and then most commonly a litle quantitye of breade and cheese, which notwithstāding was done with wonderfull snatching and rashnes.
author: Fisher, John, of Chester.
title: The copy of a letter describing the wonderful woorke of God in deliuering a mayden within the city of Chester, from an horrible kinde of torment and sicknes 16. of february 1564

text: The next day following, mayster Lane preached at saynt Maries within the sayde Citye, before John Chrogmarton Esquier, the Quenes maiesties high Justice in the Countye of Chester, at whych sermon the late recouered Maiden was present.
author: Fisher, John, of Chester.
title: The copy of a letter describing the wonderful woorke of God in deliuering a mayden within the city of Chester, from an horrible kinde of torment and sicknes 16. of february 1564

text: And in this sort beholding her, almost during the fourth part of an houre, her bellye began to moue, swelling vp & down, somtime beneath her chest, sometyme vp to the throte, in suche vehemenry, that a man would haue thought she would haue burst.
author: Fisher, John, of Chester.
title: The copy of a letter describing the wonderful woorke of God in deliuering a mayden within the city of Chester, from an horrible kinde of torment and sicknes 16. of february 1564

text: Thys verse is alwayes vnseperably adioyned vnto the Hexameter, and serueth especially to the handling of loue and dalliances, whereof it taketh the name.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: The auncient Authors of Comedies, were Eupolis, Cratinus, and Aristophanes, of the middle sorte, Plato Comicus, of the last kinde Menander, which continued and was accounted the most famous.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: YE dainty Nymphcs that in this blessed brooke, doo bathe your brest: Forsake your watry bowres and hether looke, at my request: And onely you Uirgins that on Parnass dwell.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: O Amarill, vvherefore, to thy Gods (very much did I meruaile) Heauilie thou didst praie: ripe fruites vngathered all still: Tityrus is not at home: these Pyne trees Tityre mist thee.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: He which wyll not slatter and is of ability to iudge, let him endeuour to nothing so much, as to the correction of that which is wrytten, and that let be doone with earnest and exquisite iudgment.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: The great company of famous verses of thys sort, which Master Haruey made, is not vnknowne to any and are to be viewed at all times.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: The seauenth sorte is a verie tragicall mournefull measure, wherein he bewayleth the death of some fréend vnder the person of Dydo.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: A foote of two sillables, is eyther simple or mixt, that is, of like time or of diuers.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: In making choise of such fréendes as should tell vs the trueth, and correct our wrytinges, héedefull iudgment must bee vsed: least eyther we choose vnskylfull folke, or flatterers, or dissemblers.
author: Webbe, William.
title: A discourse of English poetrie Together, with the authors iudgment, touching the reformation of our English verse. By VVilliam VVebbe. Craduate [sic].

text: But tell me now, you haue hard my mynde all this whyle, whether goe you? and what countreyman are you?
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: NOwe lette vs ryſe and goe to comforte the friendes of this our Brother, that they doe not much ſorrow and lament for the departure of this our moſt deare brother, which now reſteth in ioyfull peace.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: A faythful ſeruant is greatly to be commended, but hee that maketh much haſte to ſlouthfulneſſe, ſhall not be vnguiltye.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: Better it is to haue a little with the feare of God, then great and vnmeaſurable-treaſures otherwyſe.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: That is moſt true, for I remēber ſometyme when I ſhould keepe the Crowes out of the fieldes, I was ſo ſlouthfull, that although the wether was colde, yet was I aſleepe.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: Thou ſhalt not luſt after thy neighbours wife, neyther whoremongers, nor worſhippers of Images, nor brekers of wedlock, nor wekelinges, neyther abuſers of them ſelues with mankynd, ſhall inherite the Kingdome of God.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: I tolde you before what commeth of eaſe and ydleneſſe, whereby you might vnderſtande that paynes muſt be taken, and the moſt parte of them doe fetch water in a Tanckarde on their ſhoulders.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: For dronkenneſſe is counted to be a Lady, and a good fellow, you cannot ſpeake with her, but by the ayde of Glotony, who is her Porter.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: And who taketh thy cloake, forbid him not thy coat, and whoſo taketh that is thyne, aſke it not agayne, and as yee woulde that men ſhoulde doe vnto you, euen ſo doe ye vnto them.
author: Fit John, John.
title: A diamonde most precious, worthy to be marked instructing all maysters and seruauntes, how they ought to leade their lyues, in that uocation which is fruitfull, and necessary, as well for the maysters

text: And yf you wylle, the houſe of Guyſe and I wylle healpe and ſuccoure you, and wylle ſende you eyther into Lorayne or Sauoye.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: For in good logicke they bee thynges repugnaunt, to bee kepte agaynſte his wyll as a pryſoner in a toune, and to deſerue to be proclaimed a rebell bicauſe he commeth not thence.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Men knowe alſo that ſhe her ſelfe perſuadyng with teares the naughtye aire and other reaſonable cauſes of her refuſall, dydde a greate whyle wythſtande the departyng from the ſaid fountainebleau: declaring vnto theim there was no cauſe why they ſhoulde geue the kyng ſuche an alarm.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Thoſe that are aboute the kyng waſte his good, and ſucke out the ſmall remnant that was in his treaſure to ſatiſfie theyr creditoures: The noble menne that are at Orleaunce, are there vpon their owne coſtes and charges, yea almoſte euery gentylman that there is.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Yf it bee for religion, I wyll take order for it as I ſhall ware elder: In the meane ſeaſon why doe not menne obſerue the lawes?
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Yf the Prynce of Conde be withholden pryſoner, what rebuke haue they cauſed the kynge to receiue, and what iniuſtice haue they don, to declare the ſaid prince a rebell and culpable of treaſon, becauſe he came not to the courte nor laid doune weapon whanne they ſente to hym ſo to doe?
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: The morowe after, the duke of Nemours departed, and came to take his leaue of the kyng. and in takynge leaue, ſayde vnto the Duke in his eare: bethynke you of that I haue ſayde, and tell no body therof.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: The Duke of Orleaunce anſwered that he would not leaue the king nor the quene his mother: The other yet replyed therto, ſaying, Aduiſe your ſelfe well of that I tell you.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Lette this ſhame and ignomie than whyche they haue doone to the maieſtie of the kyngs name be accompted for one mattier. but immediatly after ther folowed an other.
title: A discourse vpon the libertie or captivitie of the Kyng 1562.

text: Laſtly, the loue of God neuer commeth emptie, but as God is the fountain and full treaſure of all pleaſure, ſo he bringeth with him whither ſoeuer hee commeth, all good, pleaſure and happineſſe, by the which his loue and affection towardes any perſon is known and felt.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: Not that I doubt of this, or any other maine poynt of Chriſtian religion, but that I may knowe and hold that more firmly, which I doo alreadie both beleeue, and alſo know in part.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: Hee was alwaies, as hee will bee euermore, neuer beginning, nor euer ending, but alwaies being.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: So then, if we adde this difference of infinitneſſe to the Angelicall nature, there will come forth a diuine nature, which may not vnfitly be deſcribed an angelical nature euery way infinit: and ſo God be defined an infinit Angell, as an Angell may be ſaid to be a ſpiritual man.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: NExt to the eternitie of GOD, commeth to bee conſidered his vbiquitie which concerneth the ſtature and greatneſſe of GOD, as the other did his age and continuance.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: I did not thinke it to haue beene a matter requiring either long time, or any greate labour, and then I am ſure you would not haue ſtucke with me, but I pray you hold on your courſe, ſeeing you will not bee intreated to digreſſe.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: Not ſo ſir: but without queſtion, the company of men of your profeſſion, is both pleaſant and profitable, & much to be deſired for the attaining of knowledge & wiſdome.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: me thinks, that humilitie doth not well agree with the nature of God, and that there is ſmall vſe of humiliation in his doings.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: Otherwiſe, by giuing God a body, we take from him his infinitneſſe, & ſo his diuine nature, making him locall, mutable and mooueable.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: A treatise of the nature of God

text: That is: A soule refourmed to ye lyknes of god fyghtyth ayēst yt flesshly styrynges of this ymage of synne / & also this ymage of synne stryueth ayenst the wyll of the spyryte.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: I pray ye norysshe this fyer. this fyer is not elles but loue & charyte. this hath he sent in to ye erthe as he sayth ī ye gospel / Ignē veni mittere ī terrā & ad quid nisi vt ardeat.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: Thenne semyth it that there is no thynge that so lyghtly may be had as charyte. and therfore the nedeth for to be moche adradde Be meke & haue it.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: I coueyte nought but one / Thou shalt haue ye meanyng of thyse wordes ī thyn entent & in habyt of thy soule lastyngly though thou haue hem not euer specyally in thy thought. for yt nedeth not.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: ANd therfore it is a grete maystry a man to cun loue his euen crysten in charyte / Al this sayeng may be openly proued by saynt poules wordes thus.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: There is noo creature soo vnmyghty as he is. and therfore it is a grete cowardnes se that men dreden hym so moche.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: For they wote well that yf they sholde be good men they must nedes forbere the grete lykynge & the luste of this worlde that they haue in erthly thynges / & yt wol they not.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: LO thyse are fayre newe felynges in a clene soule. & yf a sowle were fulfylled with suche it myȝe be layd.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: Loue ye & prayse our lorde. for he is good. & by suche other as he is styred to say.
author: Hilton, Walter, d. 1396.
title: Scala perfectionis

text: Thoſe thinges that doe not concerne vs, let vs not contend about them, wee haue no ſuch cuſtome, neither the Church of God.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: Aſſure your ſelues beloued our ſpirituall landes are turned into temporalles, hundreds by the yeare, are not ſufficient to maitaine them, this is ſcandalous to the eie of the multitude, and their diſordered liues are laied as heauy burdens vpon the backes of their aged parents.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: Timot. 3. ſhee is ſaied to bee vniuerſalis, becauſe ſhee is not onely reſident in one place, but is extended to the confines of the whole earth.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: I neede not to tel you what he did his ſchoole at my back can tel you, he hath ſent forth frō thēce heretofore many a famous ſcholler, that haue proued neceſſary & profitable mē in the church of god.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: Men and brethren, I haue beene ſomewhat long in theſe points, I will leaue them to your good conſideration: in the meane time, let vs be aſſured of this, that God permitteth this cockle and darnell to grow among vs, vntill in due time he flingeth them into the fire.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: That man ſaieth Bernarde, is not onelie ſaied to bee idle, that doeth nothing, but hee likewiſe that alvvaies turmoyleth, and reapeth nothing.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: The Apoſtle Saint Peter in theſe three verſes propoundeth vnto vs, three ſeuerall partes to be obſerued: The firſt a propheticall prediction of the future calamities incident vnto the Church of Chriſt by falſe teachers conteined in theſe words: There were falſe Prophetes among the people ſo likewiſe their ſhalbe falſe teachers among you.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: This ſay they ſhall haue an aduouſion of ſome cōpetent perſonage, the other ſhall attend vpon my Lord Biſhop, vt ditetur de bonis domini ne in noſtros liberos noſtra diuidatur haereditas.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: Here the quarrell beginneth, a diſputation is intended, and thereof proceedeth malice and rancour, and one enuying the other, one in the ende conſumeth another.
author: Barne, Thomas.
title: A sermon preached at Pauls Crosse the thirteenth of Iune, the second Sunday in trinitie tearme 1591 by Thomas Barne ...

text: Tel me, I pray thee, what thing more ſweeter, and of greter conſolation may any man deſire, that hath not wholly loſt his taſte, then to meditate, diſcourſe, and think vpon the wordes, workes, examples, and life of our Sauiour Ieſus Chriſte?
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: See, O thou miſerable and wicked man, ſee what God a moſt righteous and merciful man hath ſuffred for thy iuſtification; procure thou therfore to be grateful to ſuch a benefactour, and not to renewe his griefes with thy newe ſinnes.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: Conſider alſo what the good olde father Simeon felt, at ſuch time, as (being inſtructed of the holy Ghoſt) he ſawe and knewe that to be come to paſſe, which he ſo long time had wiſhed for, and ſo oft had craued at Gods handes with continual teares and praiers.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: O glorious Ladye, what tongue can poſsiblye declare the ioye thou felteſt, ſeing thy ſelfe thus highly honoured, and thus embraced betwixt thoſe ſacred armes of thy dere ſonne.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: AS TOVCHING the ſecond point thou haſt a plentiful ſubiect to warm thy ſoule with, entertaining thy ſelfe in meditating the comming of the holy Ghoſt.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: Behold him chaſtiſed, in ſuch wiſe, that hardly can he be taken for a man, ſo farre is he from being reputed a king.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: Seing the ſame our Lorde aſſureth vs him-ſelfe therof, ſaying: If anye enter in by me he shal-be ſaued, and shal finde moſt ſweete feedings.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: O howe much more ſugred wordes maye we thinke he ſpake to her, howe much more ſinguler fauours he did her, and howe much more amiably he embraced her.
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: What is he therfore that wil-be ſo ſenſeleſſe, and of ſo corrupt a taſte, as wil not be delighted therwith, and feele a ſinguler ſweetnes in meditating of this ſo holie a life?
author: Loarte, Gaspar de, 1498-1578.
title: Instructions and aduertisements, how to meditate the misteries of the rosarie of the most holy Virgin Mary. Written in Italian by the Reuerend Father Gaspar Loarte D. of Diuinite of the Societie of Ie

text: Thus we haue briefelye ſhowed what thinges are to be wiſhed and obſerued in all elections, now I will as breefely in few wordes touch what thinges are to be auoyded and taken heede of.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: Finally the ſignes are diuided into foure quarters, that is to ſay, into the Spring tyme, the Somer, the Autumne or harueſt, and the Winter: the which contain the ſignes which make thoſe partes of the yeare, as followeth.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: The ſecond ſort is, when as a planet going to the Coniunction of another more waightie then he, and the ſame do behold another planet that is more waightie, before the firſt be ioyned vnto him.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: In like ſorte doth it happen betweene Iupiter and Mars, for Iupiter is exalted in the xv. degree of the Crabbe, and abaſed in the lyke degree of Capricorne, and Mars is exalted in the 28 degree of Capricorne, and abaſed in the lyke degree of the Crabbe.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: But if the ſignificators in the natiuitie doe promiſe in any matter ſome good or ſome ill, a good election ſhall helpe the good and let the euill, or at the leaſt diminiſh or make the euill the leſſe.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: Wherefore ſetting downe one only queſtion vpon euery houſe, eaſie iudgemente maye bee giuen of the reſt, ſo that which is ſpoken before, bee well vnderſtoode and perceyued.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: The dignitie or aduauncement of the children is gathered from it becauſe it is the tenth from the fift houſe, it ſignifieth alſo the friends and eſtate of fathers being the eleuenth from the fourth houſe.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: NOw that we haue ſhowed the diuiſion of the houſes, wee will alſo intreate of the ſignifications of the fame, for euery houſe hath his owne proper ſignification, as there be alſo proper Lords of the triplicitie of the houſes.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: The Mone is likewiſe cold and moyſt: and albeit ſhee doe heate a little, yet ſhe doth moyſten more, ſhe doth chaunge her nature and qualitie according to the quarters, like as the Sunne doth thorowout the ſignes of the Zodiack, & the quarters and parts of the yeare.
author: Dariot, Claude, 1533-1594.
title: A breefe and most easie introduction to the astrologicall iudgement of the starres VVhereby euerye man maye with finall labour giue aunswere to any question demaunded. Written by Claudius Dariot Phisi

text: After that I had long looked for thee (O Lorde) at the last thou diddest attende vnto me, and heardest my crie.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: O Lorde God, whiche art riche in mercie, and of thyne especiall loue towardes vs, euen when wee were thyne enemies by sinne, didst sende into the worlde thyne onely begottē sonne Iesus Christ: that whosoeuer beleueth duly in hym, shall not perishe, but haue euerlastyng life.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: The ropes of hell bee tied rounde aboute me: and I am wrapped in ye snares of death and whiche waie so euer I goe.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: Thou hast taken me out of the lake of miserie: and sette my feete vppon a rocke, and made my steppes sure.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: But thou haste heard my praiers: and according to thy greate mercie, hast taken me againe into thy fauour.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: I tary and looke for helpe from thee (O lorde) blessed is the mā that trusteth in thée.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: Wherefore goe not farre awaie from me: for daunger is euen now at hande, and I so no man that will help me.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: For albeit no man is able to beare the punishemente, whiche thou dooest threaten against sinners, yet the mercie, whiche thou hast promised, is greate & vnsearchable.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: Thei reioyce and bee glad of my fall & declination: thei be assēbled together against me: thei strike to kille me in the waie, before I maie beware of them.
author: Fisher, John, Saint, 1469-1535.
title: [Psalmes or prayers] [taken out of Holy Scripture].

text: Therfore beleue me louynge frēde, the folyſhe eſtate, that procedeth of vnlaufull wynnynge, gyueth ſmall ſuretie and leſſe good name to the perſone.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: I wyll tel you one thynge, I wolde rather my doughters, in myne abſence, ſhulde be diſciples to vertues, than to be mayſtreſſes in lewdeneſſe in my preſence.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: And therfore the beſt is, that ſuche people, whan they be warned by their ſeruantes, and reproued by their parentes, and deſired by their frendes, that they make not excuſe & ſay, howe they be not amorous, but in mockerye.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: Thou knoweſt well, that we loue togyther, and of a longe ſeaſon thyn amitie hath truſted in me.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: Therfore, if you be vertuous, with drawe theyr iapynge trifles as nowe, for them that ſhall be vertuous.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: I ſe well, that mine eies the ladders of my hope, are ſet on ſoo hie a walle, that no leſſe is the doubte of my fall, than the daunger of the clymmynge vppe.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: And thou Retoria knoweſt wel, that in thy yonge dayes, two yeres thou were appoynted on the ſee with a Pyrate, ſo that he ſhulde take no moo to ſatisfie a. C. men of warre in the galey.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: As the mayſter of Nero ſayde: As moche as the ſhame of ſynne oughte to be fledde of them, that be good, ſo moche prayſe, is the infamye of the yll.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: And therfore I wolde wytte of you, wherof you can praiſe this your kynſeman, that there be no contraritie betwene his werkes and your wordes.
author: Guevara, Antonio de, Bp., d. 1545?
title: The golden boke of Marcus Aurelius Emperour and eloquent oratour

text: But as Chriſt doth ſaye, ſoch ſlayghtes are in the ſectes As wolde in maner, deceyue the verye electes.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: Paule worketh ſedicion, and is no treaſon ſpeakar ye do the myſchefe, and yet ye make no fraye The ſame foxe that lurketh, the ſame foxe take the praye Oh trollynge gnato, ye thynke ye be not ſeaue yet by your trollynges, perceyue men what ye meane.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: Agaynſt aftrawe ye ſtumble And at a blocke ye fumble Ye fare lyke hym that tumble For nought ye do but bumble.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: Whych wyll not from them wauer and is in ſo great fauer Beynge the kynges ſeruaunt So wyttye and ſo pregnaunt He that ſhall with hym ſcole Wyll fynde hym no ſmall fole.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: Nowe maye we tythes home trolle and care but for the bolle We maye let the goſpell goo For he is our mortall foo We are fortunate thys tyde To haue ſmythe on our ſyde.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: The ſcrybe on hys ſkyrtes, doth goddes commaundementes ſet The dcuyll reſembleth, the maſſenger of lyght Who deſtroyeth lawes? who doth good order let?
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: The knaues ſhall nomore checke Nor agaynſt vs popyſtes becke With hym they dare not dallye For feare of Putiphars vallye or els for Daniels deane But now ſynge in a meane.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: Compoſed by Thomas ſmy the / ſeruaunt to the kynges Royall mageſte / And clarke of the Quenes graces, ounſell (though moſt vnworthye.)
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: But thoſe pharyſees, that chryſten peple ſpyght Sendynge ſoche prophetes, as the daye change to the nyght All them that abhorre, ther olde pylde popetrye For the worde of God, they accuſe of hereſye.
title: A brefe apologye or answere to a certen craftye cloynar, or popyshe parasyte, called Thomas smythe [sic].

text: The world is full inough of fooleries: though the humor be not feaſted with ſuch luxurious, and riotous Pamphlets.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: Here lies the man, whome miſtriſſe Iſam crown'd with bayes; Shee, ſhee, that ioyde to heare, her Nightingales ſweete layes.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: Oh, ſolace thy miraculous ſelfe, and cheere the Muſes in cheering thy daintie ſoule, ſweetelie drunken with their delitious Helicon, and the reſtoratiue Nectar of the Gods.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: But I pray God, they haue not done more harme by corruption of manners, then good by quickening of witte: and I would, ſome Buyers had either more Reaſon to diſcerne, or leſſe Appetite to deſire ſuch Nouels.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: The wildeſt Colte is ſoone tamed: and be like neither Death, nor Shame, nor Miſery are affraid of them, that vaunt themſelues, Like vnto Death, and Will Sommer, in ſparing none.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: Though the painted ſheath bee, as it is, (for it needeth no other Painter, to pourtray it ſelfe) yet neuer childe ſo delighted in his ratling baby; as ſome old Lads of the Caſtell, haue ſported themſelues with their rappinge bable.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: Surely it muſt needes bee current in matter, and autentical in forme, that had firſt ſuch a learned preſident: and is now pleaſantlie interlaced with diuers new-founde phraſes of the Tauerne: and patheticallie intermixt with ſundry dolefull pageantes of his own ruinous, & beggerlie experience.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: SOme Tales to tell, would I a Chaucer were: Yet would I not euen-now an Homer be: Though Spencer me hath often Homer term'd: And Monſieur Bodine vow'd as much as he.
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: Plutarch is grauely wiſe: & Macchiauell ſubtilly politike: but in either of them, what ſounder, or finer piece of cunning, then to reape commodity by him, that ſeeketh my diſpleaſure: & to play vpon the aduauntage of his detection of my infirmities?
author: Harvey, Gabriel, 1550?-1631.
title: Foure letters, and certaine sonnets especially touching Robert Greene, and other parties, by him abused: but incidently of diuers excellent persons, and some matters of note. To all courteous mindes,

text: And all thoſe peeces that haue three hundred weight in mettall, vnto one poūd weight of ſhot, doe require as muche Sarpentine pouder as the ſhotte wayeth, and one ninth parte more.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: And for that the lighte ſtandeth to the Seawards of the marke appointed, the ſhott muſt haue a time to come vnto the Ship, and the Ship goeth away in the meane time.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: Some alſo wyll take a priming yron, and put it into the tutchhole, and then lay it vnto the mouth of the peece, and looke what it commeth vnto more than the meaſure, they will take that for their diſpart: but that maye deceiue them, as it is generally falſe.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: And now the principal vſe of the quadrant, is to know what any peece will caſt at the mount of euerie Degree, and ſo from degree vnto degree, vnto the beſt of the Rander.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: The winde one the ſide, the peece caſteth beſide the marke: therefore you muſt weather the marke, according vnto the hardneſſe of the winde, and the diſtance vnto the marke.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: And alſo thoſe Faucons that doe ſhoote two pound and a half of Pouder at a ſhotte, then there is forty ſhottes in a hundred weight, ſo that there is, 960. ſhottes in a Laſt of Pouder.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: THe elder ſorte of whole Culuerings, called of ſome Norborow Culuerings, the heigth of the mouth of the peece fiue ynches and a halfe, the heigth of the ſhot. 5. ynches a quarter.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: As for example, a Morter peece, that ſhooteth a. 180. paces at the beſte of the Randare, ſhall ſhoote at the mountyng of euery degree foure pace ſhorter: and ſo from degree vnto degree, till that the mouth of the peece ſtandeth directly vprighte with your Zeneth.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: And I am of that opinion, and that no man can denie, but that the Arte of ſhooting in great Ordnaunce is neceſſarie to be aduaunced for the defence and mainteynance of a Kingdome, and countrey, and the common wealth thereof.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: The arte of shooting in great ordnaunce Contayning very necessary matters for all sortes of seruitoures eyther by sea or by lande. Written by William Bourne.

text: And to beginne, Firſt whan Romulus reigned, the Capitoll beyng already taken by the Sabines, and thei feightyng with baners diſplaied in the middeſt of the high ſtrete: was not the battaile ſtaied by the womens rennyng betweene both armies?
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: For he that woll charge his inferiours with any greuous impoſicion, and firſt practiſe it in hym ſelfe, ſhall finde theim the better diſpoſed to obey, eſteemyng theyr charge the leſſe, whan they ſee their betters freely take the greatter part of the burdein vpon them.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: So that the fyrſt part of the Conſules oracion ſeemeth a common defence of all lawes: and the other agaynſt ſuperfluitee, ſeemeth agreable to his ſeuere cuſtomes.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: Conſules, were two chiefe officers of the citee of Rome, whiche were choſen euery yere, and bare hygheſt authoritee in the common wealth.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: O, if we had no more but ſuche women now, as were than, I woulde thinke our worlde happie.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: After this, whan the Tribunes of the people, that had profeſſed alſo to interrupt this matter, had ſpoken ſomwhat to the ſame purpoſe, At the laſt Lucius Valerius, for the opteynyng of the contrarie (by hym ſette foorth before) ſpake on this wiſe.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: But as our libertee, by our owne weakeneſſe is ouercome of the women in our owne houſes: euen ſo here in the open ſtretes it is ouerthrowen and troden vnderfote.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: But becauſe I ſaw you matched with one as rough as Cato, who not contented with naturall reaſons, burdeined you ſo farre with ſcripture, that ye ſhuld not be allowed to weare any pleaſant apparaile: me thought I coulde no leſſe in conſcience, but take your part.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: And why ſhoulde other folkes pouertee bee hydde vnder the colour of this law? that wantyng the thynges they can not haue, it ſhoulde ſeme thei might haue them, if it were not prohibited.
author: Livy.
title: An argument wherin the apparaile of women is both reproued and defended

text: WHoſoeuer addict themſelues to honor thée (O moſte mightie God) wyth fayth and pure deuocion, are bound to render immortal thanks to thy glorious name, which they ought to paye vnto thée in all places, euery yere without ceaſſing, euery day, and euery houre.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Cauſe henceforth the puyſſaunt force and moſte ſharpe weapons of thy bleſſed worde to be preſent, whereby all the ſubtiltie of Sathan maye be confounded and brought to nought.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Thy ſure protection & moſt ſtrong defence hath béene alwayes merueilous readie to helpe thy elect ſeruaunts at what time they repoſed their whole truſt in thy vnſpeakable mercie, and when thou tookeſt vpon thée to be their ſtrong helper and mightie deliuerer, no man could in any wiſe hurt them.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Pardon vs (we humbly beſéeche thée) neyther ſuffer thou vs to repoſe our truſt in the force & power of any creature: but graunt that we hauing thy wonderfull mercye in experience, maye perfectly reioyce, and rightfully take pleaſure in ye ſame, through Ieſus Chriſt our Lorde.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Haue mercy out of hande (we humbly beſéech thée) of Sion, that is to ſay, thy bleſſed Church, for the time is now come that ſhe ſtandeth in great néede of thy readie helpe.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: All which matters, if we did beholde with a godly affection and well diſpoſed minde, our heart without doubt ſhould alwayes be kindled and inflamed with a feruent deſire it hath towards thée.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Wherefore our earneſt requeſt is, that thou wouldeſt ſpeedily lay to thy readie helping hand, not permitting hir neyther to be polluted with ſuperſticious and deuiliſhe errors, nor yet oppreſt by Sathan or force of the vngodlye, through Ieſus Chriſt our Lord.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Graunt therefore that the vertuous men which earneſtly loue thée, may well vnderſtande that thou mightily preſerueſt thy faithfull ſeruauntes, and doeſt greatly ſtrengthen ſuch as honor and reuerence thee with an vnfeyned heart, through Ieſus Chriſt our Lorde.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Let vs neuer ſo ouerſhoote our ſelues, (no though we be appoynted as ſhéepe to the ſlaughter) as to be forgetfull of thy glorious name, and to haue recourſe vnto deteſtable worſhipings.
author: Vermigli, Pietro Martire, 1499-1562.
title: Most godly prayers compiled out of Dauids Psalmes by D. Peter Martyr. Translated out of Latine into English by Charles Glemhan. G. Seene and allowed according to the order appointed

text: Or the conſideration of the benefits of God, and of his Diuine promiſes, for to ſtirre vs vp vnto his loue, and to the hatred of all that which is offenſiue to his Diuine goodneſſe.

text: Farre greater are my ſinnes than thoſe of MARY MAGDALEN: a more vgly Leper I am, than he which came vnto thee: and in my ſoule I ſuffer another manner of fluxe, and farre more dangerous than that Woman.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: If finding any thing he hath taken the ſame with mind to keepe it for himſelfe: the like of thoſe thinges which happen to come to his handes, which knowing that they belong to others, he hath not reſtored to whom he ought.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: If he haue borne carnall loue to any perſon, purſuing the ſame with deſire of ſinne, and how long time he hath perſeuered therein: and if by his occaſion ſuch perſon haue beene noted with any infamy: alſo diuers actes and ſinnes which happen between perſons which beare ſuch loue one to another.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: If he haue ſuffered himſelfe to be ouercome with choller: and if he haue donne, or cauſed any euill to others.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: Thoſe which are Parentes, or Rulers of Families, if they haue curſed or wiſhed any cuell to their Children, or others of the Family, or if they haue not reprehended them when it was conuenient, nor procured to make them Learne whatſoeuer a Chriſtian ought to knowe.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: If he haue ſinned by himſelfe, with any vncleauneſſe, and whether at that time he thought of any other perſon deſiring the ſame: for in that caſe there be two grieuous Mortall ſinnes.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: He therefore ſaide when he was amongeſt vs. Thoſe that are in health haue no need of the Phiſition, but thoſe which are ſicke.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.
title: A short treatise of the sacrament of penance with the maner of examination of conscience for a generall confession : wherunto is added another treatise of confession, for such spirituall or deuoute pe

text: If with his euell example, or counſaile, or with praiſing that which was euell, or reprehending that which was good, he hath bin cauſe that any man lefte any good worke which he had begunne: or if he haue induced him to any ſinne, or to perſeuerance therein.
author: Bruno, Vincenzo, 1532-1594.

text: The companie of euery ſhip, one euery morning at the breake of the day, according to the cuſtome, ſhall giue the good morrowe by the maine maſt, and at night the Aue Maria: and ſome dayes the Salue Regine: or at leaſt, the Saterdaies with a Lettenie.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: When that for any occaſion he ſhall ſtrike all Sayles, he ſhall ſhewe three lights, one in the toppe, an other in the Shrowdes, and the third in the Fore-caſtle: and the reſt ſhall ſhew it, with putting foorth a light each vpon his Poope.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: Euery afternoone they ſhal repayre to their Admirals to take the word, and to knowe if there be any thing to do.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: Being from the land a ſea borde, euery ſhip ſhall come to leyward, ſaluting the Admirall to know what he wil commaund: & demaund the word, without going a head the Admiral, either in the day or in the night, but to haue great care to his ſayling.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: And for that the moſt occaſions come by play, you ſhal publikly prohibit it, eſpecially the games that are forbidden: and that none do play in the night, by no meanes.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: And for that ſo many great Shippes, and ſo great may be, cannot come euery day without bording one another: to auoyde the daunger that may followe, the Generall of each Squadron ſhall haue particular care, to take the word in time, to giue it vnto the Shippes vnder their charge.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: All the aboue ſaid, we commaund to be manifeſted, and bee kept without any breach for the ſeruice of his Maieſtie, none to breake them or any parte thereof in no manner, vpon payne they ſhalbe ſeuerely puniſhed, euery one according to his eſtate and offence: all others reſerued to our diſcretion.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: If it happeneth ſome daies that winde wil not ſuffer to take the word of the Admirall or Admirals, they ſhall haue for euery day in the weeke the words following.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: In the night there ſhall be great vigilance for the Admiral, to ſee if ſhe change her courſe, or make about.
author: Medina Sidonia, Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, duque de, 1550-1619.
title: Orders, set dovvne by the Duke of Medina, Lord general of the Kings fleet, to be obserued in the voyage toward England. Translated out of Spanish into English by T.P.

text: He ſhall call on my name, and I wyll here him; & I wyll ſaye you are my people, and they ſhall ſaye the lorde is my God.
title: The foūtayne or well of lyfe, out of whiche doth sprynge mooste swete consolations, ryght necessarye for troubled conscyences to thyntente they shal not despayre in aduersitie and trouble..

text: But after that he hath called vpon the almyghty, which through his power doth breke the ſtrengthe of enemyes, they toke the citie.

text: O lorde god the creatour of all thynges / terrible, ſtronge, ryghtuous, & mercyfull, which onely art good, onely the excellent kynge / onely iuſte, almighty, and eternall, whyche delyueredſt Iſrael from all euyll.

text: The lord god wyll caſt downe deth for euer, and wyll take awaye the teares from euerye face, and the ſhame of his people out of all the world for the lord hath ſpokē and they ſhal ſay at that tyme.
title: The foūtayne or well of lyfe, out of whiche doth sprynge mooste swete consolations, ryght necessarye for troubled conscyences to thyntente they shal not despayre in aduersitie and trouble..

text: Haue mercye on me, o god haue mercye on me, for my ſoule truſteth in the, and I ſhal truſt in the ſhadowe of my wynges vntyll wyckednes be paſſed.
title: The foūtayne or well of lyfe, out of whiche doth sprynge mooste swete consolations, ryght necessarye for troubled conscyences to thyntente they shal not despayre in aduersitie and trouble..

text: Deliuer me from claye, leſt I ſtycke init, deliuer mefro them that hate me, and from the depenes of waters.

text: Bleſſed be all that truſt in him That man is curſed that truſteth in, man / and maketh fleſh his defence, whoſe hart ſwarueth from the lorde.
title: The foūtayne or well of lyfe, out of whiche doth sprynge mooste swete consolations, ryght necessarye for troubled conscyences to thyntente they shal not despayre in aduersitie and trouble..

text: No eye hathe ſene, O God without, The thynges That thou haſt prepared to ſuche as loke after the.
title: The foūtayne or well of lyfe, out of whiche doth sprynge mooste swete consolations, ryght necessarye for troubled conscyences to thyntente they shal not despayre in aduersitie and trouble..

text: Beleue in your lorde god and ye ſhall beſure / beleue his prophetes, and all thynges ſhall come to paſſe happely.

text: Yea and much-more a Lothsomnes / to receaue or inioy anything of any straunge Spirites / or of anyone which is a Straunger vnto the Familie of Loue.
author: Abia, Nazarenus.

text: Woe vnto you and your Presumption / yee false and seducing Spirites. yee sathanish Houndes and renting Wolues. yee Generations of Vypers and Cains Ministers.
author: Abia, Nazarenus.

text: To the Communialtie in the Loue, vnto whom wee wish in the Lorde / much Felicitie, Health, and Saluation.
author: Abia, Nazarenus.

text: FOr-that-cause looke now into your Abhominations / and marke how yee haue seperated yourselues with ye Goates / from the Sheep / with the which yee shall also (if so be that yee do not whollie turne you away therfrom / and repent) be constrained to beare your Sentence of Condemnation.
author: Abia, Nazarenus.

text: But verelie it shall not auaile you in this Daye of Loue / by the Faithfulones of the Familie of Loue / to spread-abrode your seducing Seedes any farder.

text: In this ſtate he dyeth, and hath his eyes alwayes faſtened vpon God, and ſo ſeeth, how indeede, the dead are bleſſed which dye in the Lord.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.

text: They bee vnder the couenant with vs. The ſobreſt waye is to ſpeake leaſt, and to leaue them to the iudgement and mercie of God.

text: God calleth to vs by the Prophet, Bring wood; & builde this houſe, & I will be fauourable in it.

title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: The dead bodies of thy ſeruants, haue they giuen to be meat vnto the foules of the heauen, & the fleſh of thy ſaints vnto the beaſts of the earth.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: Of hym alone, and onely of hym, hath it bene ſpoken, This is my well beloued Sonne in whom I am well pleaſed.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: Now to applie theſe wordes vnto this our preſent time, wherein vnder a moſt godly and gracious prince, the trueth of Chriſtes Goſpell is freely preached, Gods holy name therfore be prayſed for euer.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: He ſhewed vs in a Sacramēt bread & wine, after the order of Melchiſedec, to bee the likenes of the body and blood of Chriſt.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: Strabo writeth of the Smyrnians, that they builte a temple in the honour of Homer, and ioyned therto a library.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: Wee ſay, there is no other ſubſtantiall foode of our ſoules: and that hee is diuided among all the faithfull: and that hee is voyde of ſaluation, and the grace of Chriſt, whoſoeuer is not partaker of his body and blood.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: Certaine sermons preached before the Queenes Maiestie, and at Paules crosse, by the reuerend father Iohn Ievvel late Bishop of Salisburie. Whereunto is added a short treatise of the sacraments, gather

text: And therfore, if there ſhould be ſome of you that would not further to the vttermoſt this the weightieſt cauſe of a thouſand, concerning not onely our ſaluation, but more the glory of Chriſt.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: For al the whole land is at your commandement both of body and goods (with the conſent of our moſt gratious ſoueraign, who is full of mercy and compaſſion) to do as by law you ſhal preſcribe thē.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: To this plaineneſſe of teaching, there ought to be ioyned a continuaunce in the holy exerciſe of the word, as S. PAVL ſaith to TIMOTHIE: Take heed to thy ſelfe, and to doctrine, and continue therein.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: If it be ſayd the ſmall number of skilfull men canne not eaſilye be founde, a lamentable thing to be heard.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: Then wold your honorable counſell come about you, as SECHANIAH the ſonne of IEHIHEL came to ESDRAS, and ſaid, we haue treſpaſſed againſt God, by receiuing a ſtrange miniſtery; yet there is hope concerning this.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: But our caſe is to bee bewailed and pitied, becauſe the doctrine of ſaluation is not offred vs by the way of preaching, in ſo many ſeueral congregations, as hunger and thirſt after it.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: By whoſe meanes the people treſpaſſed grieuouſly againſt the Lord in negligence, or rather contempt of comming to the tabernacle to worſhip the Lord according to the law.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: Much more we find in holy Scripture concerning the office of Miniſters, tendyng to ſhew the excellencie of their function, and the wonderfull skill and knowledge that is required at their handes.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut
title: A lamentable complaint of the commonalty, by way of supplication to the high court of Parliament, for a learned ministery. In Anno. 1585

text: What belongeth to God, that is kept from him? euen that which appertaineth vnto his church, to wit, preſentations and impropriations.
author: Waldegrave, Robert, 1554-1604, attributed name. aut

text: From tope to toe, ſhe felt great payn as Lazerous, that bleſſed man whiche ſhe full meklye, did ſuſtayne although her frendes, forſoke her than with out all, mourmuration agenſte Gods ſweet, correction.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Well I doe hope, that ſhe ſhall onſe though lyne of lyfe, be now out raſte ryſe and reuyue, bothe fleſhe and bones and ſo in heuen, with Chriſt be plaſte thus leaue I her, in laſting Ioyes and for the ſame, geue God the praiſe.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Her harte was, infatigable throughe faith which ſhe: ſtaied vppon that nether welthe: nor paine was able her to remoue, from Sion ſtonne. but ſtyll in faithe, endured ſhe as one the, Inuyſyble ſee.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Abhore ſhe dyd, to haue exceſſe and porcyon, to eate alone but gaue ther of, the Fatherles as one fulll of, Compaſſion therfore the ſcriptures, doth witnes her ſoule ſhall neuer, feele darknes.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Thus is ſhe deade, to lyue agayne in that lyfe, that laſteth euer highe in the heuens, where is no payne amongeſt the holy, ſaynctes together happy therfore, was her good channce whome God of heuen, doth ſo aduaince.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Now when ye chriſte, in her laſt dayes dyd vyſyt her: with muche ſyknes and proued her fayth, ſunderye wayes to make her to, his owne lyknes ſhe paſt not then, for aney loſſe but meklye wt Chriſte: kyſte the croſſe.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Yf that Marie Choſe, the beſt parte which Chriſte bad kepe, in memorye ſeinge from the ſame, ſhe did not ſtarte her Fame therfore, ſhall neuer dye amongeſt the Bleſſed, Femynyne though the wicked, ther at repyne.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: As ſhe thus hath, played her parte and nowe reſteth in Gods owne hand ſo death wyll ſtryke vs, with his darte whoſe power no fleſhe, can with ſtand God garunt therfore: to eache degree ſo happye in lyfe, and death to be.
author: Newport, Frances.
title: An epytaphe, of the godlye constau[n]t, [and] counfortable co[n]fessor mystres (Darothye [sic] Wynnes) whiche slepte in Christ the yere of grace. M.D.LX. Made by, Frances Newport

text: Beautie is worne awaie, fresh bloud is turn'd to blacke: Wit is made dull, the memorie lost, and liuelinesse dooth lacke.

text: Quhairfoir I ſeing the ſamin to haue bene obſcure from the beginning to thir dayis, ȝit being ane ornament and ane publict vtilitie to the Realme & Burgh, thocht gude to mak the qualiteis and profeit thairof acknawledgeit to ſic perſoūis as be vexit with ſic diſeſis as it is good for.

text: Sic watter as be of the qualitie of Iryn geuis ſtrenth to the Interiour partis of mānis body, & keipis the ſtomak frō corruptioū, and promouis the haill faculteis quhilkis gouernis mānis body.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: Sic watter (ſayis he) quhilkis ar not abill to burding the ſtomak and ar of facill digeſtioun muſt neidis to be laxatiue, and procure paſſage of the womb be Medicinall het qualitie.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: Quhilk alſo approuis the minerall qualitie thairof, be reſſoun all naturall and pure ſweit watter is flaw in paſſage, difficill of concoctioun, flatuous & heuie in the ſtomak, and generis diſtillatiounis, as wrytis Aetius Tetrab. 1.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: To vtheris it is womatiue, quhilk alſo teſtifeis the het qualitie thairof, farther it geuis gude appetyte to thame quha at deſtitute thairof, and gif ony mā drink twentie pound wecht of this Fontaine he findis no charge nor burding of the ſtomak nor bellie be the watter.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: And in reſpect the countrie is of nature minerall, this watter being drunkin cuirand ſair Eyn, Catarris, ſair mouth, prolapſioū of the vult, and dolour of the Tonſallis, it muſt neidis ſpring from Braſſe, as teſtifeis Aetius Tetrab. 1.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: Ane greit fault I find in the vſe of this watter, that Ilk perſoun drinkis thairof at thair awin pleſure, nether hauing reſpect to the preſent diſeis, naturall cōſtitutioun of body, nor tyme of the ȝeir, quhair by the ſaid watter be the abuſaris thairof is rather vilipendit nor cōmendit.
author: Skeyne, Gilbert, 1522?-1599, attributed name.
title: Ane breif descriptioun of the qualiteis and effectis of the vvell of the vvoman hil besyde Abirdene

text: Ȝe brag mekle of richteouſnes on ȝour ſyde, bot will ȝe find me that impietie with thame quhilk is not in the lyke degre or rather greiter with ȝour ſelfis, and it is ſpokin that ȝour treſſoun aganis the King and countrie may matche thairis as ȝour practiſis with Ingland witneſsis.
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Cryit not Dauid (his pepill being chaſtoſit for his offenſis) it is I ô Lord, it is I, quhat hes thir Innocent ſcheip done?
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Bot albeit I ſeme to gang with ȝow thus far generallie, ȝit find I not thir circumſtances correſpondent to the depoſitioun of our Maiſtres.
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Attour the floriſching & beſt cōmoun welthis yat our Nobill predeceſſouris hes left mentionat in famous Cronicklis, teichis not onlie how inſolent Kingis hes bene comptrollit of thair Gouernament, bot ſum be mature deliberatioun of the counſall of Nobilitie cōdempnit to perpetuall preſoun and yair deceiſsit.
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Quhat ſpirite culd haue reuengit ane cuffe geuin to a man of his awin Surname with the ſlauchter of ane Innocent man, and reſſauit in his ſpeciall protectioun the murtheraris of that Nobill Prince his Maiſter, that was during his dayis the bandſtane of mekil quyetnes in yis Realme?
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: My conſcience beiris me record, that thair Nobilitie aucht to put ordour to thair inſolence, and that baith ye lawis of God and nature allowis the ſame.
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Dardanus King for his Murther and Tyrannie apprehendit be his Nobilitie and ſlane: and for the mair terrour of all Princes to gouerne be tyrannie, his body caſsin in his awin vyle cloiſſet. 5.
title: Ane Discourse tuiching the estait present in October anno Domini 1571

text: Thair appeiris na les, for his only ſtanding hes brocht Scotland to the miſerie ȝe ſe, and quhat it hes done in Ingland ma aig es nor ane will remē ber.

text: Pale hungry Death, thy greedy longings stop, Hope of long life is banefull to my mind: Yet hate not life, but lothe captiuitie, Where rests no trust to purchase victorie.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: They show him diuers gallant men of might, VVhose wounds not mortall, hope gaue of recuer, For their saks sue they to diuorce this night Of desperate chaunce, calld vnto Deaths black lure, Their lēgthned liues, their coūtries cares might right, And to their Prince they might good hopes assure.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: You powers of heauen, rayne honour on his hearse, And tune the Cherubins to sing his fame, Let Infants in the last age him rehearse, And let no more, honour be Honors name: Let him that will obtaine immortall vearse, Conquer the stile of Grinuile to the same.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: Say fiftie three strong shyps could not fulfill, Gainst one poore mayden vessell their foule teene, But that in spight of death, or miserie, She fought, and foyld, and scapt captiuitie.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: Then to the night she giues all soueraigne power, Th'eternall mourner for the dayes diuorce, Who drowned in her owne harts killing shower, Viewes others torments with a sad remorse.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: To him their Chieftaines mightines they tell, And how much valure on his soule doth feede, That if preuention, not his actions dim, Twill be too late to saue the shyp or him.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: Loe, on the great west-walling boistrous sea, VVhich doth imbrace thy gold-inclosing eyes, Of many sailes one man, of one poore Ile, That will my fame, and all thy faire defile.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: Th'ambrosian Nectar-filled banqueting, No more shall I communicate, or see, Triumphes in heauen, Ioues masks, and reuelling, Are cleene exempt, both from my ioyes and me.

title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: On eyther side him, still two Gallions lay, VVhich with continuall boardings nurst the fight, Two great Armados, howrelie plow'd their way, And by assault, made knowne repellesse might.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The most honorable tragedie of Sir Richard Grinuile, Knight

text: As the ſpirite bloweth where he liſt, ſo when he liſt; ſom muſt be called at one houre, ſom at an other: ceaſe we not in the meane time (hoping the beſt) to perſeuer in our embaſſage.

text: Strength vpon Strength, Pſal. 84, more and more annointed (as it were) to the euery fingers end: that is, to the ending of euery action.

text: She ſees the body but not the Head: She, therfore maketh ſuite, eye, chargeth the body (by reaſon of that dutie which is owing from member to member) to acquainte her beloued with this, namelie That ſhe vvas ſick of Loue.
author: Clapham, Henoch.
title: The sinners sleepe vvherein Christ willing her to arise receiueth but an vntoward answer. By Henoch Clapham.

text: The third goeth for life (Ezech. 12.18.) to the ſmoth tongued propheteſſes, who lay ſoft pillows vnder their ſore elbowes, that ſo rhey may ſleepe on peaceablie to the Deuil.

text: As he was gone paſt her feelinge, ſo immediately herevpon, ſhe remembreth his former ſpeaches kinde and reaſonable: the remembrance wherof, ſmiteth her to the heart, wherevpon ſhe ſoundeth & is ready to departe away in a qualme.
author: Clapham, Henoch.
title: The sinners sleepe vvherein Christ willing her to arise receiueth but an vntoward answer. By Henoch Clapham.

text: A confeſſion which fewe will bee brought vnto in theſe daies: for they rather will ſay, I am not more naked than others, more ignorant than ſuch.
author: Clapham, Henoch.
title: The sinners sleepe vvherein Christ willing her to arise receiueth but an vntoward answer. By Henoch Clapham.

text: Lot could not ſleepe quietlie in his Zoar, and thinks thou to reape holie contentment in thine vnholie choiſe?

text: Then ſhall they cal vpon her, but ſhe ſhal not anſwere: they ſhal ſeeke her early, but not find her, meaning, Not at all.

title: The sinners sleepe vvherein Christ willing her to arise receiueth but an vntoward answer. By Henoch Clapham.

text: But leauing this our Sinner heere ſleeping: or rather betweene Sleeping and vvaking, namely in a Slumber: I will in the next tractate (God permitting) take examination of her ſoul: by which time I exſpect her firſt Reſurrection.
author: Clapham, Henoch.
title: The sinners sleepe vvherein Christ willing her to arise receiueth but an vntoward answer. By Henoch Clapham.

text: VVhen intertaining to my bewties honor, The true instructions chastitie did teach me: Noting what hap, what heauen did wayt vpon her, VVhilst no dishonoring blemish did impeach me, By nature and desire to this disposed Soone had my will my thoughtes thereto imposed.
