title: Beawtie dishonoured vvritten vnder the title of Shores wife Chascun se plaist ou il se trouue mieux.

text: And infant younglings, sucking from their mother, Selfe-like-dregs, of vnwomanly surmises, Add boldnesse to the mallice enuies other, For euen the young begins as bewtie rises: And this peculier to their sexe did see.

title: Beawtie dishonoured vvritten vnder the title of Shores wife Chascun se plaist ou il se trouue mieux.

text: O if it be so, yet withall I finde, That hell's aboue the yearth as well as there And neuer could Philosophie approue, That there was one below but one aboue.
author: Chute, Anthony, d. 1595?
title: Beawtie dishonoured vvritten vnder the title of Shores wife Chascun se plaist ou il se trouue mieux.

text: For sooner had no motiues of desire, Taught me to exercise my witt, and bewtie; But my conceipt could set delight on fire And wanton lookes impriuiledge all dewtie And I grew fayrer and the oftner named As quainte conceipt me for delightfull famed.
author: Chute, Anthony, d. 1595?
title: Beawtie dishonoured vvritten vnder the title of Shores wife Chascun se plaist ou il se trouue mieux.

text: Cruell in what may harme in what may ill me But thrise more cruell that thou wouldst not kill me.
author: Chute, Anthony, d. 1595?
title: Beawtie dishonoured vvritten vnder the title of Shores wife Chascun se plaist ou il se trouue mieux.

text: But ô, why doe I thus wearie prolong, The wofull Tragedie of my pleasures wayne, Suffices that I knew to bide the wrong, And brooke with patience what I did sustaine, Idly we greeue when greeuingly we plaine vs, For that must be perform'd that needes constraine vs.
author: Chute, Anthony, d. 1595?

text: Nor be they pleas'd to giue vs all these vvounds, To make me languish as a dying liuer, But from her orbes they fling their fiarbronds, Thereby to quite consume both hart and lyuer: Pardon, drad povv'rs, pardon my rash offence, By heauens bright vaile, t'vvas gainst my cōscience.

text: If that by chaunce they fall most fortunate, Within those cruell hands that did enact it, Say but, alas he vvas too passionate, My doome is past, nor can be novv vnactit.

text: Were I but once resolued certainly, Soon should I knovv vvhich point my helme to stere, But she denies my sute most vvomanly, As hidden documents for vs to heare.

text: COurteous Reader, whereas I was fullie determined to haue concealed my Sonnets, as thinges priuie to my selfe, yet of courtesie hauing lent them to some, they were secretlie committed to the Presse, and almost finished, before it came to my knowledge.
author: Percy, William, 1575-1648.

text: Wherefore making, as they say, Vertue of necessitie, I did deeme it most conuenient to praepose mine Epistle, onely to beseech you to account of them as of toyes and amorous deuises, and ere long, I will impart vnto the world another Poeme which shall be both more fruitfull and ponderous.

title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: O that the rablement of brattes whych swarmde aboute the syde Of Niobe that scornefull dame who perysht by her pryde Had taken lyfe out of hys lymmes. o that the fates of heauen A fruytefull mother had me made of chyldren seuen and seuen.
author: Seneca, Lucius Annaeus, ca. 4 B.C.-65 A.D.
title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: An holye solempne sacryfyce to worship the we make, Imbrewed with a blooddye turphe the kindled torche doth take Thy sacred burning night fyre at the dampishe morie graue.
author: Seneca, Lucius Annaeus, ca. 4 B.C.-65 A.D.
title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: Tyme is it Phaeba to respecte the seruyce to thee made: To thee with cruell blooddye handes thes garlandes grene were twind Whych with hys foldyng circles nine the serpent rowgh dyd bynd.
author: Seneca, Lucius Annaeus, ca. 4 B.C.-65 A.D.
title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: This vengeaūce this doth lyke me wel good reason is their why The last attempt of yls, thou must with stomacke stout applie.

title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: With malyce bent agaynst the godes my wrath shall them assay: And rifling euerye thyng, both good, and bad, I wyll turmoyle.
author: Seneca, Lucius Annaeus, ca. 4 B.C.-65 A.D.
title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: Whose swellyng knobes of wondrous sise & boysteus bobbing bumpes Doth thumpe the great & lesser bear that fele his heauye lumpes.

title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: Yet was hys speache so pleasant and so milde, Hys tongue so fylde, hys promyses so fayre, Sweete was the fowlers songe that hath beguylde The selye byrde, brought to the lymed snare.
author: Seneca, Lucius Annaeus, ca. 4 B.C.-65 A.D.
title: The seuenth tragedie of Seneca, entituled Medea: translated out of Latin into English, by Iohn Studley, student in Trinitie Colledge in Cambridge

text: The heauenlye father inſpired me into their hartes, that I ſhoulde moue thē to attend vpon Ieſus his ſōne.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: And yet could not the vngracious & wycked people be ſtayed, but fell in murmuring, & began newe tumult and buſynes, but the wrath & plague of God fell vpon them, and they were conſumed with fier, to the numbre of xiiii. thouſande.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: But as God wold there was one good and vertuous mā, whoſe name was Noe, who euen as I was ſecretlye departinge from the earthe, founde me, & obtained of God, that I myght tarye with him, and God of hys goodnes was content that ſo I ſhould.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: And I wrought ſo that after this, Darius alſo the kynge of Perſes was fauourable to the Iewes, and confirmed the libertie of buildinge againe the temple, as Cyrus had done before.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: And all this would not helpe, ſtyll they continued murmuring when ſo euer their wāted the ſatiſfiyng of their carnal deſires, inſomuche that Moyſes was faine to get thē water out of the hard ſtone.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: And by his prudente pollicie and prouiſion bothe the people were quietlie pacified in tyme of the darthe, and the kynge enriched.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: After this whā Moyſes had brought the people into the wyldernes of Surria, I taughte him by his praier, to chaunge the bitter and ſower waters in to ſwetenes, wherby the murmuringe of the people was pacified.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: Howe happie then are thoſe princes and great men, which haue vertuous and honeſt men aboute thē, who wyll make no ſuggeſtions, but ſuch as ſhalbe cōmē dable & profitable to the world, honorable to their mayſter, and acceptable to God?
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: O would God I were as great in their heartes, as I am muche vſed in their ſtyles and tytles.
author: Redman, John, 1499-1551.
title: A compendious treatise called the co[m]plaint of grace compiled by the notable clerke mayster Ihon Redman Doctour in diuinitee deceassed, late mayster or president of Trinitie colledge in Cambridge, c

text: I wil not for this time enter into long disputation, but I would rather come to the crime, wherein I fell my selfe by you most accused.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.

text: Therefore, we charge and commaund, all and euerie of our Lordes, gouernors, magistrates, Iudges, Treasurers, Receauers, Consulles, Citizens, commons, and all in generall, diligently, and straitly, to obserue this our present commaund, that euerie one may be maintained according therevnto.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.

text: Therefore, in all extremities, I haue recourse to the iudgement of those which hath right intelligence and knowledge.

title: A declaration made by the Archbishop of Collen, vpon the deede of his mariage, sent to the states of his archbishoprike VVith the letter of Pope Gregorie the. 13 against the celebration of the same ma

text: Giuing me aduertisement of the great and manifold daungers, falling on those, which are desirous of nouelties, which folowing their disordinate lustes and affections, are drawne from the company of the Apostolique church.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.
title: A declaration made by the Archbishop of Collen, vpon the deede of his mariage, sent to the states of his archbishoprike VVith the letter of Pope Gregorie the. 13 against the celebration of the same ma

text: Which is, because I am purposed to marie, which S. Paule neuerthelesse affirmeth, to be honourable amōg all men: and which is also sette in the Romane church, among the number of the Sacramentes.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.

text: Forbidding them expresly, that they shall doo no wrong nor iniury to any in déede, or in wordes, to the ende that euerie one of them maye liue quietly and peaceably one with an other.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.
title: A declaration made by the Archbishop of Collen, vpon the deede of his mariage, sent to the states of his archbishoprike VVith the letter of Pope Gregorie the. 13 against the celebration of the same ma

text: Wherefore my duty is to accept of your charitable & holie admonitions, knowing that which is said by Salomon, that he which refuseth discipline, hath no regarde of his owne soule: but he that harkeneth to correction, shall obtaine knowledge.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.

text: In this submission most rightfull and iust, that by those which religiously feareth God the trueth alone is reuerenced, and to the same, all and euerie thing must be agréeing.
author: Gebhard, Truchsess von Waldburg, Archbishop and Elector of Cologne, 1547-1601.

text: Therefore am I determined to enter into mariage, not being mooued by any light or disobedient minde: but after long tryall made of my selfe, I haue knowne that it is not good for me to liue vnmaried.

text: That is to ſaye, a Rocke, euen as, Chriſt taketh not his name of a Chriſtian, but a Chriſtian of Chriſt, therfore the Lord ſayd, vpon this Rocke will I build my Church becauſe Peter ſayd, thou art Chriſt the ſonne of the liuing.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: This is our God, and there ſhall none other be compared vnto him, it is he that hath found out all wiſedome and hath giuen her vnto Iacob his ſeruaunt, and to Iſraell his beloued, afterward dyd he ſhew himſelfe vpon earth, & dwell among men.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: I will not that you ſhoulde be mine but with me, be with me, for we are all his which dyed for vs which was crucified for vs.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: I am he, before whom there was neuer any God, and their ſhalbe none after me, I am euen, I am the onely Lord and beſide me ther is no Sauiour.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: There is both in the olde Teſtament a letter that kylleth as alſo in the new Teſtament, if hit be not vnderſtande ſpiritually for if thou doſt followe the letter where as it is ſayd, vnleſſe you eate my fleſh and drinke my bloud.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: If he be ſuch one, he wyll not vniuſtlye binde vpon earth, neither without iudgemente vnloſe or make frée, but if there be any man, that I may ſo ſaye.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: Becauſe they haue turned the troth of God into a lye, and haue worſhipped and ſerued the creature, rather then ye Creator which is bleſſed for euer.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: But my people haue giuen ouer their hie glory for a thing that may not helpe them and much farther he ſayth in that Chapiter.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.
title: The fortresse of fayth defended both by the Scripture, and doctors / gathered by the learned German Bodonius ; and translated out of Latine into English by Edward Crane.

text: But it is we that muſt be helped and reliued, it is we that may be hurte or harmed of him and not he of vs.
author: Bodonius, Stephanus.

text: But where it ſtaied, there did the preeſt ſet down the ark: and then was Moſes woont to ſay; Return, O Lord, to the many thouſands of Iſrael; ſo (as it were) welcoming hom the Lord again.
author: Bunny, Edmund, 1540-1619.

text: And the better to advance the ſolemnitie of this feaſt (beſides the praeſence of the people, and thoſe loaves that they had to bring for themſelves and ther families) there was a ſpecial ſacrifice appointed on behalfe of the whole people for that pręſent day.
author: Bunny, Edmund, 1540-1619.
title: The scepter of Iudah: or, what maner of government it was, that unto the common-wealth or Church of Israel was by the law of God appointed. By Edm. Bunny

text: If a man had ſo unwarily kindeled a fire, that it had done any hurt to his neighbors corn, either in the ſtak, or ſtanding in the feeld, he was to make good the whole loſſe unto his neighbor.
author: Bunny, Edmund, 1540-1619.
title: The scepter of Iudah: or, what maner of government it was, that unto the common-wealth or Church of Israel was by the law of God appointed. By Edm. Bunny

text: Then that the Koathites followed in the midſt, betwixt the ſecond and the third armie, with the ſanctuarie, and the holie things.

text: Which in my judgement may beſt be done, if we ſhal ſort them al to be one of theſe two, either ordinarie, or extraordinarie.

text: So likewiſe, that if he ſhould promiſe hir to his ſon, and afterward repented: yet ſhould he do unto hir, as to one of his daughters.

text: Again, beſides thoſe tokens of aequitie in particular duties one with another, we ſee that divers of them that were utterly deſtitute of the word of God, had notwithſtanding excellent gifts in the way of government, and notably governed much people and mightie kingdoms.

text: Vnto thoſe inferior magiſtrates that were to be ordained in their cities, it was commanded that they ſhould judge uprightly, regarding no perſon, nor wreſting the law: that ſo they might proſper upon the earth.

text: Arise (said Mercurie) thou sluggish beast, That here liest senseles, like the corpse deceast, The whilste thy kingdome from thy head is rent, And thy throne royall with dishonour blent: Arise, and doo thy selfe redeeme from shame, And be aueng'd on those that breed thy blame.

text: For since the time that Phoebus foolish sonne Ythundered through Ioues auengefull wrath, For trauersing the charret of the Sunne Beyond the compasse of his pointed path, Of you his mournfull Sisters was lamented, Such mournfull tunes were neuer since inuented.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.
title: Complaints Containing sundrie small poemes of the worlds vanitie. VVhereof the next page maketh mention. By Ed. Sp.

text: O who shall powre into my swollen eyes A sea of teares that neuer may be dryde, A brasen voice that may with shrilling cryes Pierce the dull heauens and fill the ayer wide, And yron sides that sighing may endure, To waile the wretchednes of world impure?

text: The Paſſeouer was the ſame to the Iſraelites, that the holie ſupper is to vs: but becauſe our ſacrament is more excellent then theirs, great care muſt be had in preparing our ſelues.

text: This is cleere in both the ſacramēts: whē the miniſter hath added the word of inſtitutiō to the water, it is no more common water, but baptiſme, which is a Sacramēt of our Regeneratiō.

text: The new Sacraments inſtituted of Chriſt are plainer and clearer then the Sacramentes vnder the Lawe, as the Goſpell is playner and clearer then ye Lawe, but the thinges ſignified in and by their ſacramentes and ours, are not contayned more in our Sacramentes then in theirs.

text: Many grapes make one cuppe of wine, many cornes one loafe of bread, wee are members of one body, whereof Chriſt is the heade: therefore we muſt be at vnitie with Chriſt, by giuing great honour to him, and with our fellow members by doyng good vnto them.

text: If they ſinne which for the eaſe of their owne purſes ſuffer the Churche to bee charged, their ſinne is greater which do pull from the Churche, or take eyther mony or penſions of the Church men for preferring of them.

text: Plaine men of the countrie, doe marke onely thoſe ſheepe for their own, which they eyther knowe or at the leaſt doe take to be their owne.

text: In clothynge and in goinge haue with the symplenesse: in thy gate and in thy mouynge clennes, in thy bearynge sadnes, in thy walkyng honestie, nothing of vilany, nothynge of vncleannesse, nothynge of wyldenesse.
author: Isidore, of Seville, Saint, d. 636.
title: Here be the gathered counsailes of saynct Isodorie to informe man, howe he shuld flee vices and folowe vertues

text: A feythfull speche holdeth the place of a sacramente: as who sayth, a faythfull worde is as moche as all the swearynge of the worlde.
author: Isidore, of Seville, Saint, d. 636.
title: Here be the gathered counsailes of saynct Isodorie to informe man, howe he shuld flee vices and folowe vertues

text: Lerne at Christe manlynesse, take hede at Christe, and be not heuy: he suffrynge wronges lefte to vs ensaumple, he was bobbed and buffetted, spytte vpon, and scorned, nayled hande and foote, crowned with thornes, dampned to the crosse, and euer more helde his peace.
author: Isidore, of Seville, Saint, d. 636.
title: Here be the gathered counsailes of saynct Isodorie to informe man, howe he shuld flee vices and folowe vertues

text: Therfore suppose not thy selfe good, thoughe thou beholde good in other mens tonges, aske thyne owne conscience, deme thy selfe by thin own dome, and not bi other mens speche, but in thyn owne mynde inserche thy selfe.
author: Isidore, of Seville, Saint, d. 636.
title: Here be the gathered counsailes of saynct Isodorie to informe man, howe he shuld flee vices and folowe vertues

text: Fyre by castynge to of wodde, increaseth more and more, the more mattier is in the fyre, the more is the flame.

title: Here be the gathered counsailes of saynct Isodorie to informe man, howe he shuld flee vices and folowe vertues

text: Do away the occasion of Stryfe, Despyse stryfe, and lyue alwaye in peace, stryue not in any wyse.

text: And a man moche swearynge, shalbe fulfylled with wickednesse, & the plage shall not departe from his house.

text: And if he for any cauſe paſſe the bondes of the fielde, that then he beare openly a croſſe of ſaint George, vpon peyne to be impriſoned and punyſhed at the kinges pleaſure.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And alſo that euery of them obey, and duly kepe all ſuche proclamations ordinaunces and ſtatutes, as now be and hereafter ſhalbe, on the behalf of our ſaid ſoueraine lorde made and proclaymed, vppon the peynes within the ſayd proclamations ordynances & ſtatutes, or any of them comprehended.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And ouer that, euery man aforeſayd, the ſayd lieutenant onely except, be obeyſant vnto the marſhall of the armye, for the tyme being, vpon ſuche paynes as ſhall be lymytted by the lieutenant.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And that in lykewiſe no man come ne appere in or at any muſter vnder any capytaine, except he be (as afore is ſayd) retayned with hym for that voyage, vpon peyne of impriſonement at the kinges wylle.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And that no man bie no ſuche priſoners, vpon payne to loſe the money that he ſhal paye for him, and the priſoner to be arreſted to the capitain afore ſaide.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: Alſo that no man murdre or robbe any perſon, excepte he be the kynges ennemie, ne rauiſhe any woman, vppon peyne of death.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And that it be lefull to the mayſter of the ordynance, to ſend for pyoners into any countrey won or pacified, where he ſhall thinke neceſſary.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And if it be any other crime or offence capital then treaſon: that then the reſiſtour in ſuche caſe ſhal ſuffre like paynes and puniſhmētes as the principall adiudged ſhuld haue ſuſteyned and ſuffred.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: And that no man preſume to breake the kynges ſalueconducte, his lieutenauntes or his ſayd merſhall hauyng ſuche auctoritie, vppon peyne to be hanged and drawen, and his goodes and inheritaunces to be forfeyted to the kynge.
author: England and Wales. Sovereign (1509-1547 : Henry VIII)
title: Statutes and ordynances for the warre

text: So that no other contract is ſo certaine, and ſo preciſely bounded, or limited, as this of geuing to lone.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: To geue to lone by the law of al people and coūtries is, to delyuer preſently to another man ſuch ſtuffe as is ſpent with the firſt natural and proper vſe therof, with bond to haue him repay ſo much and ſo good againe of the ſame kind.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: By which teſtimonie the truth it ſelfe doth witneſſe, that euen our dayly ſinnes and inward vncleanneſſe, are made cleane by Almoſdedes.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: If then I lend a quart of old french wine, although I can not aſke the ſelfe ſame quart againe: yet the meaſure of a quart maketh it certaine, how much he muſt paye who boroweth the wine of me.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: And where he ſhould rather haue loſt ſomewhat of his owne for Gods ſake, there he increaſeth his owne, and taketh away another mās goods iniuriouſly: as it ſhal more plainly appeare, when the matter of geuīg to lone is fully declared.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: Now albeit a donation or free gift, whē it is really deliuered, is not properly a contract: yet becauſe many times a man bindeth him ſelfe by ſolemne promiſe afore hand, to geue a thing afterward, in this caſe there is a certain couenāt betwen them, which muſt be kept.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: For mony was inuented to make exchange withall: but vſurie (exchangeth not, but) increaſeth the pennie, wherof alſo it toke his name (in Greke) Now thoſe thinges which are begotten, are lyke to them by which they are begotten.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: The matter I ſpeake of, is vſurie, in defence whereof thus I haue heard diuerſe mē reaſon at ſeueral tymes.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: Secondly, that yt ought allwaies to be free: otherwiſe it is no lone at al, but a ſelling or ſetting to hyer.
author: Sander, Nicholas, 1530?-1581.
title: A briefe treatise of vsurie, made by Nicolas Sander D. of Diuinitie

text: And thynke on the inestymable ioye of the sayntes in heuen / the whiche our lorde hath promised you of ye lyue out of deedly synne / & loue hym aboue all thyng.

text: And whā thou dilygētly by thyselfe hast discussed & consydered all thynges: than go thou to the pest with grete reuerēce: & not as thou woldest tell a tale: & after the synne of the crosse made vpon ty brest say.
author: Catholic Church.
title: This prymer of Salysbury vse is set out a long wout ony serchyng with many prayers, and goodly pyctures in the kale[n]der, in the matyns of our lady, in the houres of the crosse in the. vii. psalmes,

text: So than neither for the weke perſons cauſe neither for their cauſe whiche are parfyte / is it neceſſarye to take awaye ymages.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: Beſydes this / there ar ſayd & done ſo many thinges / whiche do turne away our myndes frō chriſt which raigneth in heuen / vnto the worke of the preſt.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: Who ſo euer dothe this / ſhall be gyltye of that cryme / of whiche Paule accuſeth Peter / in the epyſtle to the Galatyans.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: I ſay / how fortuned it / if ymages be ſo ꝓfytable / that god for al this inſomoch dyd nothinge eſteme thē that he wold in no wiſe ſuffre them to be amonge his people.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: But if any man do ſomwhat dilygently conſyder & way the mater / he ſhall perceyue vndoutedly / that ymages ar fallē into a farre gretter abuſe amonge Chriſten men / than euer was amonge any heathen men.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: Maſſes moſt ſpecyally ar done for the belyes ſake: or els at ye leſtwiſe to purchaſe ſome merite afore god / which thīg euē it ſelfe alone / although al this buſynes were cōmaūded by god / ſhuld yet make it abhomynable to god.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: For there was no man at that tyme / which dyd ſo moche as ones dreme / that euer ſo gret a multytude of images ſhuld crepe into churches / as hath cropē in / for as moche as they knewe it to be forbydden with ſo open & euydent oracles & teſtymonyes of the ſcrypture.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: Images haue gyuen anſweres wt vs / they haue wepte / one of thē hath ben thoughte more holy and of more power than another.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

text: A chriſten man neuer eteth or drinketh / but forthwith he is put in remembrance that chriſt is the only and the very meate / which fedeth and nouryſſheth vs into eternall lyfe.
author: Bucer, Martin, 1491-1551.
title: [A treatise declaring and showing that images are not to be suffered in churches]

author: Hyperius, Andreas, 1511-1564.

text: The Philosophers say, it is because of the spirit labouring to passe thorow the long and small passage of her necke, makes a noise as if she did sing.
author: Vallans, William.

text: The last, and not the least motiue was my friendes request, whose importunate demaund without breach of amitie, I could not gainsay: to whom, as also to thy fauourable construction (curtcous and friendly reader) I commit the same.
author: Vallans, William.
title: A tale of tvvo swannes VVherein is comprehended the original and increase of the riuer Lee commonly called Ware-riuer: together, with the antiquitie of sundrie places and townes seated vpon the same.

text: From hence to Sapsford, and to Starford, cald The Bishops: then to Farnam and to Maundes, And so to Clauering, vvhere it riseth first, And then comes dovvne againe into the Lee.
author: Vallans, William.
title: A tale of tvvo swannes VVherein is comprehended the original and increase of the riuer Lee commonly called Ware-riuer: together, with the antiquitie of sundrie places and townes seated vpon the same.

text: The townesmen of late haue procured to themselues a new corporation, and haue on the Saterday a good market and euery yeare three faires.
author: Vallans, William.
title: A tale of tvvo swannes VVherein is comprehended the original and increase of the riuer Lee commonly called Ware-riuer: together, with the antiquitie of sundrie places and townes seated vpon the same.

text: Long liued these Swannes in Lee, with great increase Of honour, royaltie, and in high estate: Inricht with issue of the fayrest breede, That liues in Seuerne, Humber or in Trent, The chiefest floudes that water English ground.
author: Vallans, William.
title: A tale of tvvo swannes VVherein is comprehended the original and increase of the riuer Lee commonly called Ware-riuer: together, with the antiquitie of sundrie places and townes seated vpon the same.

text: Then looke hovv Cynthia vvith her siluer rayes, Exceedes the brightnesse of the lesser starres, When in her chiefest pompe she hasteth dovvne, To steale a kisse from drousie Endymion: So doe these princes farre excell in state, The Svvannes that breede vvithin Europaes boundes.
author: Vallans, William.
title: A tale of tvvo swannes VVherein is comprehended the original and increase of the riuer Lee commonly called Ware-riuer: together, with the antiquitie of sundrie places and townes seated vpon the same.

text: No sooner vvas this message knovvne abroad, But there resorted to their being place, Such troupes of milke-vvhite Svvannes, as vvell beseem'd The royall state of tvvo such princes great.

text: Viols and Virginals were heir, With Girthorns, maist iucundious, Trumpets and Tymbrels, maid gret beir, With instruments melodious: The Seistar and the Sumphion, With Clarche pipe and Clarion.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: I murne, I plene in anguisch and in baill, And not but caus to cares I do incline, Seeing no helpe of counsall can awaill, Vnto my persoun quhilk remains in pine.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Quhiles lesings helps as we may se our sell, And be that mene sum makes thair profit weill, Hurtful it is somtime the truth to tell, And in al things the veritie to reueile, Se that great gifts thou distribute and deale.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: O Edinburghe now will I sing, Thy prais quhilk the perteins of richt, Thou hes bene ay trewe to thy King, In doing seruice day and nicht: Quhen that his grace did haif ado, And in the fields ay formest to.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Thocht it be rid, and fellun fair of hew, Zit in the stalke, scharp pyks it hes anew.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: ANNA, our welbelouit Queene, Sat in hir goldin Coche so bricht, And efter sche, thir things had seene, Syne she beheld, ane heuinly sicht: Of Nymphs, quho supit NECTAR cauld, Quhois brauities, can scarce be tauld.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Vpoun the left wer likwais knit, Twa proper stains of valure hie, The Iasynth, and the Chessolit, Iewels maist excellent to se: Amangs the rest I saw athort, The Rubie of the rarest sort.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Quhy stay I now, and thairfore to be schort, My humble sute, gif gud atendence to, And I maist ernestlie, will you exhort, To tak in patience, that quhilk I will do.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Seing na ischew till eschew, My dolour daylie did renew, Sic madnes did me moue, Euin as ane persoun in dispair, My greif aggregis mair and mair, Without remorse or roue.
author: Burel, John.
title: [To the richt high, Lodvvik Duke of Lenox ... J. Burel, wisheth lang life]

text: Under trybute be cōteined taxes, fiftenth, subsides, and suche as be payed at sometymes to the Rulers, and be not continuall.

title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: But if thou do euyll, feare: for he beareth not the sweard wythout a cause, for he is the minister of God to auenge in wrath, hym that doeth euyl.

title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: Geue therefore vnto euery one dueties: tribute to whōe trybute is due, custome to whome custum is due, feare to whom feare is due, honoure to whom honoure is due.

title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: Another wyll say that he would bye a Lordshyppe of the kyng, for the loue that he hath to the tenauntes thereof, but assone as he hathe boughte it, by takynge of fynes, heyghnyng of rentes, and sellyng away of cōmodities, he maketh the same tenantes pay for it.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: But as there be dyuers members in dyuers places, hauyng dyuers duties, so to haue dyuers prouision in feedyng and clothyng.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: And so sinne & abhominacion destroyed by the repentaunce of man, this pleasaunte place of Englande, and good people shall be preserued and saued by thy mercy of God.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: What haste thou that thou hast not receyued: Yea thou as a seruaunte haste receyued of thy Lord, whych gyueth vnto hys seruauntes the Talentes of hys treasures.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: A hundred thousande of these enemies are landed at thy hauens, haue entred thy fortes, and do procede to spoyle, murther, and vtterly destroy: and yet for all this thou wretched Englande beleuest not gods worde, regardest not hys threatninge, callest not for mercye, ne feareste not gods vengeaunce.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A fruitfull sermon made in Poules churche at London in the shroudes, the seconde daye of February by Thomas Leuer

text: For as there is no power of authorithy but of god, so is there none put in subieccion vnder theym but by God.

text: Antichrist preacheth neuer, prateth oft, great and noble personages he flattereth although neuer so wicked and vngodlie, namely when he hopeth and looketh for gaine.

text: Beeyng found hee sweetely laide her vppon his shoulder, and tenderly brought her home againe with greate ioy and muche gladnesse: and callyng together his louers and neighbors, he said vnto them: Oh reioice with me: for I haue found my shepe, which was lost.

text: Christe as touchyng his deitie, is the true and naturall Sonne of the liuyng and immortall God: and as cōcernyng his humainitie, he is the true and naturall Soonne of Marie the Uirgine.

text: Yea, the basest among you all thei shall salute with Domine, that is to saie, Lorde, or Sir.

text: And that wicked Spirite occupieth their myndes also in these our daies, whiche againste all right, and againste their owne conscience, vnto their greate damnation, except thei shortly repent and amende, go forthe to kepe, hold, and possesse these liuyngs and gooddes of the poore Pastours?

text: And Moses exhorted the Israelites to teache the Lawe of God to their young children, and that they should haue it bounde as a signe in their handes, that it might be euer before their eyes: he caused them also to write it on the postes and doores of their houses.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.

text: Lette vs fill our selues with good Wine and Ointment, and let there no flower of the time goe by vs. Let vs crowne our selues with Roses, afore they be withered.

author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.

text: This is the article, that dyd byte you, for you can not bée content with the office of a byſhop, but you will bée alſo kynges.

text: To this I did aunſwere, that I reckened it more to the honour of God, and to the ſalnation of his ſoule, and alſo to the comfort of his poore brethren, that they were coyned, and giuē in almes.
author: Tyndale, William, d. 1536.

text: And now (Chriſten reader) to put thee cleane out of doubt, that Chriſtes body is not here preſent vnder the forme of bread (as the papiſtes haue mocked vs many a day) but in heauen, euen as he roſe and aſcēded.
author: Tyndale, William, d. 1536.
title: The vvhole workes of W. Tyndall, Iohn Frith, and Doct. Barnes, three worthy martyrs, and principall teachers of this Churche of England collected and compiled in one tome togither, beyng before scatte

text: Now wythout fayth, is no harte true or eye ſingle: ſo that we are compelled to confeſſe that the workes make not a mā righteous or good, but that the hart muſt firſt be righteous & good, ereany good worke proceede thence.
author: Tyndale, William, d. 1536.
title: The vvhole workes of W. Tyndall, Iohn Frith, and Doct. Barnes, three worthy martyrs, and principall teachers of this Churche of England collected and compiled in one tome togither, beyng before scatte

text: They looke on the miracles which God did by the Saintes to moue the vnbeleuyng vnto the fayth and to confirme the trouth of his promiſes in Chriſt, whereby all that beleue are made Saintes: as thou ſeeſt in the laſt Chapter of Marke.
author: Tyndale, William, d. 1536.
title: The vvhole workes of W. Tyndall, Iohn Frith, and Doct. Barnes, three worthy martyrs, and principall teachers of this Churche of England collected and compiled in one tome togither, beyng before scatte

text: He muſt truſt God to ſende hym good ſpeede, good lucke, fauour, helpe, a good mayſter, a good neyghbour, a good ſeruaunt, a good wyfe, a good chapman marchaunt, to ſend hys marchaundice ſafe to land, and a thouſand like.
author: Tyndale, William, d. 1536.
title: The vvhole workes of W. Tyndall, Iohn Frith, and Doct. Barnes, three worthy martyrs, and principall teachers of this Churche of England collected and compiled in one tome togither, beyng before scatte

text: And this concluſion hath he halfe a doſē tymes in his boke, that the will may compell the witte and captiuate it, to beleue what a mā luſteth.

text: Now the ſonne knoweth his fathers will, and the ſeruaūt that hath not the ſpirite of Chriſt (ſayth Paule) is none of his.

text: Remember I commend vnto you Don Chriſtofer for the moſt faithfull ſeruant which I euer had, and ſo haue care of al the reſt, which I commende vnto you.

text: This anſwere lyking the King very wel, he willed them to looke in the cofer for an other paper, and giuing it to the Prince, he tolde him, that therein he ſhould ſee the forme how to gouerne his kingdome.

text: Then the Prince asked Don Chriſtofer de Mora for the Royall Key, commaunding him to deliuer it to him, who craued pardon of his Highnes, becauſe it was the Key of all truſt and confidence, which hee could in no wiſe deliuer without the leaue of his Lord the King.
title: A briefe and true declaration of the sicknesse, last wordes, and death of the King of Spaine Philip the second of that name who died in his Abbey of S. Laurence at Escuriall seuen miles from Madrill t

text: My body ſhall be borne by eight of my chiefeſt ſeruants all in mourning weedes, with burning torches in their handes.

text: To conclude let vs confeſſ the goſpell entierlie in yt fullnes / and to the deathe ſtand to / that Chriſt hathe the ſubſtans of God and the ſubſtans of man / of hym ſelfe from above / and of David here beneathe / yet ſpottleſſ of our gilte.
author: Payne, John, fl. 1597.

text: Wherein we ſe that the fleſhe of Chriſt dothe ſhew vs his devinitie as hidden vnder a vayle / wch otherwiſe we could not indure to behowld that ſplendor and glorie / by the wch vaile we are directed and ledd vnto God / as he ſayeth in Iohn xij.

author: Payne, John, fl. 1597.

author: Payne, John, fl. 1597.

author: Payne, John, fl. 1597.

text: Certes it is grete pyte for to here her ſpeke / there they abode lōge beholdȳg thē yt retorned wt theyr purſes empty.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: In makynge theſe complayntes & many other he enbraced her bytwene his armes wt ſo feruent affeccyō yt he fel ouerth warte her in a ſwoune more thā halfe an houre / & whan he came agayne to hymſelf he made ye pyteouſt cō playntes yt ony mā myght here.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: Than the damoyſell toke the rolles of Appolyn and began for to rede them / and whan ſhe had redde theym ſhe ſtode ſtyll and ſayd no worde / and than ſhe behelde Appolyn in caſtynge a grete ſygh and after ſhe ſayd vnto hym.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: And whan the ruffyen vnderſtode the tydynges of the ſeruaūt it greued hym moche for to haue Tarcye thyder / but force it was ſo to do for to obey vnto his ſouerayne.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: Wherfore I wyll that for to appeaſe all his ſorowes and perſuacyons ye gyue hym of myn all that it pleaſeth you.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: And I make a vowe vnto god that I ſhal neuer ſhaue my berde vnto the tyme that my doughter be maryed.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: The kynge your mooſt wel beloued fader greteth your ladyſhip by me ſymple and vnworthy ſeruaunt ſendynge you theſe rolles for to certyfye whiche of the two prynces ye ſeme beſt vnto your honour and preemynence.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: Knowe thou that I haue payed and aſſoyled a queſtyon vnto the kynge of Anthyoche and demaunded his doughter in maryage (the whiche he entreteyneth for his paramours) and therfore he maketh me to be purſued for to make medye.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: And than ye nouryſſe began for to appeaſe ye lady ſhewynge her yt the kynge bare the culpe & ſynne.
author: Steinhöwel, Heinrich, 1412-1482?
title: Kynge Appolyn of Thyre.

text: We now abyde with patience the tauntes and checkes of Antichriſt and his mēbers, but yet we ſee by faith, that Babylon the mother of all abominations, ſhal ſodainly fall and come to nought, for that her ſinnes are in remembrance with God.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: The former is contayned in theſe words, By faith Noe being warned of God, of the things which were as yet not ſeene, moued with reuerence, prepared the arke.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: For euen as water floweth frō the fountaine, ſo doth this his obediēce ſpring from faith, whereby he had apprehended the promiſe of ſaluation.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: I neither (ſayeth he) care for things nowe ſeene, nor thinges which are not ſeene, ſo that I may laye holde of Ieſus Chriſt.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: In ſteade of holines of life, we deck our ſelues with pride, and in ſteade of iudgement & righteouſnes, we bring forth oppreſſion and crying of the poore, and bloud toucheth bloud.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: For finiſhing wherof, in the gathering together of the ſaintes, he charged the Apoſtles ſtraitly, but to ſpeake, what he had taught them.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: The godly king Dauid deſcribing the gouernement of his wel diſpoſed family, ſpeaketh in this wiſe: I will (ſaith he) walke in the vprightneſſe of my heart, in the middeſt of my houſe.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: Albeit Abraham had the Lorde to bee his buckler and exceeding great rewarde, vnder whoſe defence hee was ſafely garded, yet was hee tryed by famine and other daungers many, for the better exerciſe of his faith.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: It is not without good conſideration, that the Arke was for the ſafetie of Noe his houſholde: for it doth expreſſe the right gouernement of his well diſpoſed family, wherein the feare of God did floriſh and continue.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: A verie godlie and necessary sermon preached before the yong countesse of Cumberland in the North, the 14 of Nouember, 1577. By Christopher Shutt.

text: But yf one dyſſeaſour enfeoffe twoo in fee, and the diſſeyſy releaſe to one of them thys ſhall enure to bothe the ſayd feoffees.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: Alſo if ther be. 3. brethrē, & the yōgeſt brother purchaſeth lād in fee ſimple & dieth without iſſue the elder brother ſhal haue the lād by diſcēt, & not the middle brother, for that that the elder brother is more worthy of bloud.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: And he that ſhal haue the land ſhall take the ſame lande in the court, and his takyng ſhalbe entred in ye rolle And the ſtewarde or the baylife according to to the cuſtome ſhall deliuer vnto hym that taketh the land the ſame yarde or another yarde in the name of ſeiſin.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.

text: And for that cauſe the demaundaunt after that, that iudgement is geuen that the tenaunt ſhall goe without daye, maye enter into the tenementes demaunded, the whiche ſhall bee as great aduauntage to hī in the law as yf he had iudgement to recouer agaynſt the tenaunt.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: In theſame maner it is if he ſue agaynſt hys vyllayn an accion of Dette, or of accoumpte, or of couenaunt, or of treſpas, or ſuche other, thys is an enfraunchiſyng. &c. for hys that he may enpriſon hys vyllayn, & take his goodes without ſuch ſuite.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: In thys caſe the wyfe after the death of her houſbande ſhall entre into the ſaid quā titie of lande, of which her houſband endowed her without the aſſignement of any manne.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: But in thys caſe after the yere & the day that ſuch clayme was made if none other claym be made, if the father then dye ſeiſed, the morowe after the yere and the day, or at another day after. &c. than may not he that made the clayme enter.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: But the grauntours in their liues, and the heyre of the patron, and ſucceſſour of the ordinary after their deceaſes, and after ſuche charge if the parſon dye, his ſucceſſour maye not come to the ſayde churche to be parſon of the ſame churche by the lawe.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: Alſo a mā may hold of his lord only by fealte, & ſuch tenure is tenure in ſocage, for euery tenure yt is not tenure in chiualry, is tenure in ſocage.
author: Littleton, Thomas, Sir, d. 1481.
title: Littleton tenures in Englishe

text: Secondly I beleeue that al my ſins, & the puniſhmēt therof be takē away by Chriſts death, and I made partaker of his rightuouſnes.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: Firſt, hereby he declareth how that his Image in me, is corrupted with ſin, for nothing is here required, which I could not haue done before my fal in Adam.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: Secondly, that my ſaluatiō commeth onely of the free mercy of God, without my merites or good deedes.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: It is the doctrine of faith, conteynyng the promiſes of God vnto ſaluation, to all whiche truely repent, and lay hold of Chriſtes merites by a ſure truſt in the ſame.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: We pray to God in the firſt petition, that his glory may appeare, and that our liues & conuerſation may ſet forth the ſame.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: And thus is the death of Chriſt, the onely and full raunſome for my ſins, by vertue whereof, ſin alſo dyeth, and is killed in me.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: There be three ſpeciall parts therof. the firſt is to know God and my ſelfe: the ſecond is, the meanes wherby my ſaluation is wrought: the third, what helpes God doth further mee withall vnto lyfe euerlaſting.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: Prayer is the lifting vp of my hart to God, and the aſking in Chriſts name, of things needfull to me and the whole church, with thankes geuing for his benefits, and goodnes.
author: Shutte, Christopher, d. 1626.
title: The testimonie of a true fayth conteyned in a short catechisme necessary to all families, for the more knowledge of God, and better bryngyng vp of chyldren in his fayth and feare. Gathered and written

text: Concernyng the wicked, which be voyde of fayth, & of the mercy of God, the curſe of the law hangeth vpon them.

author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.

text: And this becauſe it pleaſed Chriſt Gods eternall wiſedome, graciouſlie to paſſe ouer with ſo gentle ſilence, let not vs be too ſtreight in our animaduerſions.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.

text: O holy one of Iſrael, let thy holy teſtimonies not work in vs that bitter fruit of death, but nouriſh vs through thy bleſsing, to grace & life, let it ſo diſtil into our harts, as deaw vpō the hils, that it may make thē fruitful vnto al obediēce.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.
title: Christs checke to S. Peter for his curious question out of those words in Saint Iohn: Quid ad te? Begun in Paules Church on S. Iohns day the Euangelist. 1597. out of part of the Gospel appointed for t

text: Wherefore if hee will needes bee boltinge out Gods hidden miſteries, and prye into his future determined accidents, it is fit hee ſhould bee ſifted for his vnlawful curioſitie & for his Quid hic of S. Iohn, heare Quid ad te? from his Maſter.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.

text: He ſinned in impatience, when (but a word and a blow) he cutte off Malchas eare: hee ſinned in negligence, when being commanded to watch & pray, hee ſlept, and could not wake ſo much as one howre.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.

text: Indeede I cannot boaſt much of my father and my ancetours, I ſtand not greatly vpon my ſtocke and pedigree, but I haue vertues of mine owne, which ſufficiently may commend me, I haue graces in me, for which the world admires mee.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.

text: It is an eaſie thing to bee a Cenſor, it is ſoone ſayde, why diddeſt thou it; but tu ſihic eſses aliter ſentires, not one amongſt a thouſande of vs, but would do as ſaint Peter did.
author: Barker, Lawrence, d. 1603.
title: Christs checke to S. Peter for his curious question out of those words in Saint Iohn: Quid ad te? Begun in Paules Church on S. Iohns day the Euangelist. 1597. out of part of the Gospel appointed for t

text: If hee hate Eſau, yea in his mothers wombe, why may he not with his own do that which is his pleaſure?

text: Wherfore bleſſed & beloued Citizens, praiſe God which hath protected this church & common-wealth, from ſuch vnlearned, yet contentious Spirits: and magnifie him which hath ſtill placed amongſt vs ſome graue & holy churchmē, admirable for their knowledge, & inculpable for their liues.

text: But I am, of late, more in loue wyth my Englishe Uersifying, than with Ryming: whyche I should haue done long since, if I would thē haue followed your councell.

text: Youre selfe remember, I was wonte to haue some preiudice of the man: and I still remaine a fauourer of his deserued, and iust commendation.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: And with that turning to me, and smiling a little at the first: Nowe I pray you, Master H. what say you Philosophers, quoth he, to this suddayne Earthquake?
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: That which I eate, did I ioy, and that which I greedily gorged, As for those many goodly matters leaft I for others.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: For life Magnificoes, not a beck but glorious in shew, In deede most friuolous, not a looke but Tuscanish alwayes.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: O bonny Laurell: Needes to thy bowes will I bow this knee, and vayle my bonetto: Who, but thou, the renowne of Prince, and Princely Poeta: Th'one for Crowne, for Garland th'other thanketh Apollo.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: And to saye trueth, partely too, to requite your gentle courtesie in beginning to me, and noting I knowe not what breache in your gorbellyed Maisters Rules: which Rules go for good, I perceiue, and kéepe a Rule, where there be no better in presence.
author: Spenser, Edmund, 1552?-1599.

text: As we rede through oute the Bible: and Chriſte in the newe Teſtamente confirmeth it, ſayinge: geue to Cefar that is his.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.

text: And in oure hiſtories whiche we haue before cited: wee maye ſee manye common welthes by women enlarged, or at the leaſte well preſerued, but fewe ey ther muche weakened, or vtterlye deſtroyed.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.

text: The hart (I ſay) muſt be framed and brought into the circle of obediēce: and then wyll all the reaſte followe.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.
title: An harborovve for faithfull and trevve subiectes agaynst the late blowne blaste, concerninge the gouernme[n]t of vvemen. wherin be confuted all such reasons as a straunger of late made in that behalfe

text: And if your enemies come againſt you, I will ſound ſo terrible againſt them, that their hartes ſhall fayle them to come of the Seas and treade vpon me.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.
title: An harborovve for faithfull and trevve subiectes agaynst the late blowne blaste, concerninge the gouernme[n]t of vvemen. wherin be confuted all such reasons as a straunger of late made in that behalfe

text: But that wee ſhould not in ſuche pointes, grate vpon the woordes to ſore, as though in no reſpecte a woman may opē hir mouth to edifie.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.
title: An harborovve for faithfull and trevve subiectes agaynst the late blowne blaste, concerninge the gouernme[n]t of vvemen. wherin be confuted all such reasons as a straunger of late made in that behalfe

text: And vvhen they came to encoūter vvith their enemies, if ſhe had not bene: both Barake, and al his ſouldiors, lyke vvite lyuered warriars had geuen backe ānd marred all.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.
title: An harborovve for faithfull and trevve subiectes agaynst the late blowne blaste, concerninge the gouernme[n]t of vvemen. wherin be confuted all such reasons as a straunger of late made in that behalfe

text: If we obey, and do our dutie: all the bleſſinges of God ſhal be poured vpon vs. VVe ſhall lyue in peace bothe of bodie and mynde, with leyſure and libertie to ſerue God freely, without feare of thennemie to encombre vs in our poſſeſſions, ordrede of Antechriſte to vexe our conſcience.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.
title: An harborovve for faithfull and trevve subiectes agaynst the late blowne blaste, concerninge the gouernme[n]t of vvemen. wherin be confuted all such reasons as a straunger of late made in that behalfe

text: VVherfor, let no man diſdain hiſtories, or find fault with vs, though we trauaile in hiſtories about this cōtrouerſy, for nothinge better openeth it, nothing more cōfirmeth it, nor nothing ſoner bringeth out of doubte, that is nowe broughte into queſtion.
author: Aylmer, John, 1521-1594.

text: Alſo it is as nothynge to kepe the bodye chaſte, yf man refrayne not his eyes from concupiſcence & wanton lokes.

title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: O good ſyſter ſaye thus vnto the handemaydes of GOD, vnderſet me with floures, vnderbolſter me with appelles, for why, I conſume away in the loue of my ſpouſe Chryſt Ieſu.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: He that beareth the croſſe, ought to be as ded in this world, for why to beare the croſſe, is nothyng elles but to mortifye himſelfe.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: Therfore my welbeloued ſiſter take this boke and ſet it as a glas before youre eyes, and beholde it well, & contynually, for the cōmaundementes of God be as it were glaſſes, in the which mans ſoule ſhulde euermore be lokynge.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: For he that lerneth dyſcypline loueth wiſdome, & therefore yf you will loue diſcipline you wyl become wiſe & prudent, if you wil paciētly endure chyding, you wyl become patiente, if you endure correctiō humbly.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: Yf ye can not auoyde anger, or ſwage it, yet let it not caſte you in to a furye, or in to moch haſtineſſe or iudyngnatyon, let not the ſonne goo downe vpō your anger, that is, be not longe angrye nor contynewe not in anger.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: Loke therfore that youre wordes be ful of grauyte, of ſadneſſe, and of good lernynge and that theybe irreprehenſyble.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: We loue god for he hath fyrſt loued vs, he ye loueth god ſhall pray for the forgyueneſſe of his ſynnes, and take hede he fal no more.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.
title: A compe[n]dius [and] a moche fruytefull treatyse of well liuynge co[n]taynyng the hole su[m]me and effect of al vertue. Wrytten by S. Bernard [and] translated by Thomas Paynell.

text: The wycked ſpirytes do oftentymes by nyght trouble mens myndes & vnderſtandynges with dyuers viſyons and oftētymes they do manifeſtly beate mens bodyes.
author: Bernard, of Clairvaux, Saint, 1090 or 91-1153.

text: But thus much to him which learneth to diue, let him neuer swimme further then he can see the bottome, for it is either very déepe, or els he is vnder some baucke, or in some such daunger.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: He must by stirring of his feete vp and downe in the water keepe vp his bodie, and keeping his hands vnderneath the water, pull the water towards him, that way which he would turne, and so also incline the motion of his feete, as thus.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: This is nothing els, but in diuing to lift his head aboue the water, & when he hath breathed, presently diue down againe, as afore.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: Lying vpon his backe straight as afore, his hands with their palmes downwards, pressing the water the better to keepe him vp, he must cast both his legges out of the water at once, and caper with them vpward as men vse to doe downward in dauncing, as thus.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: The windes that are most vnwholsome and daungerous to swimme in, is the East and North, for that blowing from cold and drie places, they bring diuers and sundrie discommodities.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: This is the same vpon the backe, which the other was vpon the belly, to lye vpon your backe, and behinde you take your left legge in your right hand, and forceably moue your other leg, as when you swimme vpon your backe, thus.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: And then vsing some small motion to put him forwards, kéeping onely his brest and head aboue the water, the streame will easily kéepe him vp, by reason of the concauitie in the backe.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.
title: A short introduction for to learne to swimme. Gathered out of Master Digbies Booke of the Art of Swimming. And translated into English for the better instruction of those who vnderstand not the Latine

text: Lying vpon his barke, he must drawe in his feete towards his hippes, and vse some motion with his hands vnder the water, to sustaine him till hee hath gotten hys legges in his hands, thus.
author: Digby, Everard, Sir, 1578-1606.

text: No man hath power to areſt. attache, or make diſtreſſe of anye goods forfitable, or offēces, except the Conſtable or Sargaunte of the Maſe.

text: No Butcher ſhall caſte the inwardes of beaſtes into the ſtreates, cleaues of beaſtes feete, bones, hornes of ſhepe, or other ſuch lyke, vnder payne of. ii. s.

text: No man within this Citie may make any Quyll, and breake anye Pype of the Condytte, commynge throughe hys houſe, or nighe hys ground, vnder payne of the Pyllorye, or take any water pryuely vnto hys howſe.

text: No man ſhal haue any kine, gotes, Hogges, Pigges, Hennes, Cockes, Capons, Duckes, in the open ſtreate, vnder payne of forfayture of the ſame.

text: Alſo euery freman maye finde any offence, but he hathe no power to bryng the partye before anye Iudge of thys cytye, wythout an offycer, except the party wil come to his aunſwere by frewyll.
author: City of London (England).

text: No manne ſhall encomber the Streates with Timber, Stones, Cartes, or ſuch like, vnder payne of forfayture of the ſame thinge, that ſo encombreth the Streates, whiis twentye ſhyllynges fyne: Yf he amoue it not at the warnynge of the Sargaunt of the Markette.

text: No man ſhall caſt or ley in the Streates, Dogges, Cattes, or other carrin, or any noyſome thing, contagious of ayer, nor no Inholder ſhall ley out dounge out of his howſe, but yf the carte be redy to carry the ſame away incontinentlye, vnder payne of. xl. s.

text: To hir they doe commend themſelues, and all their familie, That get themſelues beyond the ſeas for feare of ieopardie.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: But with their handes they cannot all come néere it now by much, Therefore with ropes they hale and hoyſe, and ſo farre of doe touch: And thinke they haue done ſufficiently, then giftes they offer all, Vnto their chriſten daughter, golde, and ſiluer therewithall.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: Some ſort there are that mourning go, with lantarnes in their hande, While in the day time Titan bright, amid the ſkies doth ſtande: And ſéeke their ſhroftide Bachanals, ſtill crying euery where, Where are our feaſtes become? alas the cruell faſtes appere.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: Beſides he teacheth that the Maſſe, doth profit equallye, Aſwell the men aliue, as thoſe that long ago did dye.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: All things are lawfull vnto them, and are diſpenſt withall, So thou beléeueſt not on Chriſt, nor on his name doſt call.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: There be ſuch as their orders doth continually conſtraine, To begge abrode: and ſuch as ſtill in pouertie remaine.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: If bound vnto their treble vowe, they kéepe their faſting dayes, And prayers long appoynted them, and other fooliſh playes, And all their life long from the vſe of tender bathes they flie, And in their ſeuerall Sels, as do the Monkes Carthuſian lie.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: Then furious rage begins to ſpring, and hurlyburly riſe, On pewes and deſkes and ſeates they bounce, & beate in dredfullwiſe: Thou wouldſt ſuppoſe they were poſſeſt, with ſprightes and deuills all, Or fury ſuch as forceth them, that vpon Baccus call.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.
title: The popish kingdome, or reigne of Antichrist, written in Latine verse by Thomas Naogeorgus, and englyshed by Barnabe Googe

text: Being Chriſtians calde, and both in life, and fayth doe diſagree, As in this popiſhe kingdome here thou perfitly mayſt ſée.
author: Naogeorg, Thomas, 1511-1563.

title: 14.Ayres in tabletorie to the lute expressed with two voyces and the base violl or the voice lute only. 6.more to 4.voyces and in tabletorie. And 8.madrigalles to 5.voyces By Michaell Cavendish Gentle

text: Or yf a man bete a childe afore her / or smote an hors / or an other beste wt a whype / yf she myght se it or here it. she thought she sawe our lorde beten or woūded lyke as she sawe in the man or in the beste.

text: For I tell the doughter / they that be grete fasters / & grete doers of penaūce. they wolde that it shold be holde the beste lyf / And they that gyue them to many deuocyons / they wolde haue that ye best lyfe.
author: Kempe, Margery, b. ca. 1373.
title: Here begynneth a shorte treatyse of contemplacyon taught by our lorde Jhesu cryste, or taken out of the boke of Margerie kempe of lyn[n].

text: And than wt grete wepȳge she asked our lorde Ihū how she myghte beste please hȳ. & he answered to her soule saynge doughter haue mynde of thy wyckednes & thynke on my goodnes / than she prayed many tymes & often these wordes.

title: Here begynneth a shorte treatyse of contemplacyon taught by our lorde Jhesu cryste, or taken out of the boke of Margerie kempe of lyn[n].

text: So that yf she sawe ony creature be punysshed / or sharpely chastysed / she wolde thynke that she had ben more worthy to be chastysed than yt creature was for her vnkyndnes ayenst god.

title: Here begynneth a shorte treatyse of contemplacyon taught by our lorde Jhesu cryste, or taken out of the boke of Margerie kempe of lyn[n].

text: And therfore doughter / for all these good wylles and desyres thou shalt haue ful mede & rewarde in heuen byleue it ryght wel & doute neuer a dele.

title: Here begynneth a shorte treatyse of contemplacyon taught by our lorde Jhesu cryste, or taken out of the boke of Margerie kempe of lyn[n].

text: I thanke the doughter that thou woldest dye for my loue / for as often as thou thȳkest so thou shalt staue the same mede in heuen / as yf thou suffredest the same dethe / & yet there shall no man slee the.

text: DOughter bycauſe I dyd ſaye to the that I had made a brydge of my ſone I wyl that it be vn knowen to you / ye the waye of my be loued ſone is broken / by the inobedyence & treſpas of Adam / in ſomoche ye no mā myght come to euerlaſtȳge lyfe.

text: And agayne: Dearlye beloued, let vs loue one another, for loue cōmeth of God: and euery one that loueth is born of god and knoweth God.
author: Coverdale, Miles, 1488-1568.
title: A goodly treatise of faith, hope, and charite necessary for all Christe[n] me[n] to know and to exercyse themselues therein tra[n]slated into englyshe

text: As the ſoule is noble, and heauenly, euen ſo can ſhe fynde nothynge amonge theſe earthlye creatures wherein ſhe myghte vſe true glorye, and ioye.
author: Coverdale, Miles, 1488-1568.
title: A goodly treatise of faith, hope, and charite necessary for all Christe[n] me[n] to know and to exercyse themselues therein tra[n]slated into englyshe

text: Hereby is it euident vnto man, ye gods loue is vnto hym a ſure fundament a ſtrong hold, a rock & an hard ground, wherevpon he may buylderightwel.

title: A goodly treatise of faith, hope, and charite necessary for all Christe[n] me[n] to know and to exercyse themselues therein tra[n]slated into englyshe

text: He that loketh ſtedfaſtly vpō the LORD, ſhall not be broughte to cōfuſyon: for the loue that he knowlegeth in God ſhal cauſe him to walke confidently and aſſuredly.
author: Coverdale, Miles, 1488-1568.
title: A goodly treatise of faith, hope, and charite necessary for all Christe[n] me[n] to know and to exercyse themselues therein tra[n]slated into englyshe

text: I haue treſpaſſed, I praye the remembre thy word that thou haſte promyſed vnto the ſynners which turne agayne from theyr ſynnes, namely, that thou wilt receaue a ſorowfull ſprete vnto thy mercy.

text: But they are all gone out of the waye, they are altogether become vnprofitable, ther is none that doth good: no not one.
