text: This newe Cytye was ſone repleniſhed wyth a great multitude, for commandiment was giuen to all the Cyties theraboutes to ſend inhabiters vnto Alexandrey.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: The Lacedemoniās made no other requeſt, but that they might ſend Embaſſadours vnto Alexander, whiche vpon their repaire to him and their ſuite made, obtained pardon to all men. ſauing to ſuche as were the authores of the rebellion.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: The kinges of Macedon in purifiyng of their ſouldiers, were wonte to vſe a kind of ceremony, in deuiding the bowelles of a dogge in two partes, & caſt the ſame in the vttermoſte boūdes of the field, wheron they purpoſed to bring furth the army.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: For whyles euery manne coueted vp the ladders, they were ſo ſore laden that they brake aſunder, and ſuche as were mounted vpon theim fell downe agayne, deceyuynge Alexander of hys onelye hope.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: Which enterpryſe though it were left, they had not for all yt ended the warre neuer the more, but rather made an exchaunge of a newe labour, beyng put furthe amonges theſe wylde nacions, to make the Occean ſea open to hym with their bloud and to be drawen beyonde the ſonne and ſterres.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: It was ordeined alſo that ſuche as ſhould be preſidentes amonges the Indians, Bactrians, Sogdians, and other naciōs lieng vpon the Occean, and read ſeas, ſhould in matters of iuſtice vſe regall iuriſdictiō.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: He toke ordre there amonges them that the horſemē, and ſuch as were of the ſquare battaill of footemen ſhould be caried ouer in boates, & that the light armed ſhuld ſwimme vpon bottels.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: But he that neuer doubted any perill, and muche leſſe the multitude of men, after the eleuēth encāping came to the riuer of Euphrates, ouer the whiche he made brudges and paſſed ouer his horſemen and afterwardes his footemen.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: The king then meruayling at there magnauymitye: I enquere of you (qd he) if you can be content to liue, & become frendes to him, by whoſe benifite you ſhal receiue your life.
author: Curtius Rufus, Quintus.
title: The history of Quintus Curcius conteyning the actes of the greate Alexander translated out of Latine into Englishe by Iohn Brende.

text: Go to Moyses, who hadde the guydynge of Goddes people, se howe he vsed prayer, as an instrumente to be delyuered oute of aduersytye, when he hadde greate roughe mountaynes on euerye syde of hym, and before hym the redde sea, Pharaos hoste behynde hym, peryll of death rounde about hym.

text: Paule was taken vp into the third heauen, aske lykewyse what he sawe when we was caryed thyther, you shall not fynde in scripture what he sawe or what he dyd there, shall we not therfore beleue that he was ther.
author: Latimer, Hugh, 1485?-1555.
title: The seconde [seventh] sermon of Maister Hughe Latimer which he preached before the Kynges Maiestie [with?]in his graces palayce at Westminster, ye xv. day of Marche [-xix daye of Apryll], M.ccccc.xlix

text: But I feare one thynge, and it is: lest for a salfety of a lytle money, you wyll put in chauntrye Pryestes, to saue theyr pentions.

title: The seconde [seventh] sermon of Maister Hughe Latimer which he preached before the Kynges Maiestie [with?]in his graces palayce at Westminster, ye xv. day of Marche [-xix daye of Apryll], M.ccccc.xlix

text: And I made answer, yt I would rather folowe Paule in vsyng hys termes, then them, though, they hadde all the doctours on theyr syde.

text: Syr suche a man hathe sente you a dyshe of frute, and desyreth you to be good vnto hym for such a benefice.

text: PRayer after the cōmon diffinicion of the Doctors, is a lyftinge vp of a pure mynde to God, wherein we aske somewhat of hym.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: For the place hyndereth nothynge, neyther dothe the tyme let, but though thou doste not bowe thy knees, nor knocke thy brest, nor stretche out thy handes to heauen, yet mayst thou pray aright & make thy prayer perfecte, so that thou only shewest & bryngest forth a feruēt mynde.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: Therfore whatsoeuer we do we must haue a respect to the wyll of God, & make ours conformable vnto it, vnlesse we hepe vp dānacion vnto our selues in all our peticions, prayers & requestes.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: What other thynge do the examples of all these holye men teach vs, than that it is lawfull for a faythfull man to praye wythoute ony differency in euery place.

title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: And in asmuche as this word Prayer doth contayne in it not only Peticion, but also thankes gyuyng for the benefyte that is receyued, therfore haue I also declared my mynde concernynge gyuing of thanckes to God the Father thorow Iesus Christ.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: ANd bycause no man shoulde be offended wt the obseruaunce & appoyntmēt of certayne houres vnto prayer, as a thynge supersticious & repugnant to the christen liberte: I wyll shewe that dyuers holye men had theyr certayn houres also, wherin they vsed custumably to pray.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: Yf thou be a Bysshop or spirituall ouersear, thā hast thou a great occasion to flye vnto God wt thy prayers, that thou mayst fayth fully gyue attendaūce on the flocke, ouer whome the holye Ghoste hathe made the an ouersear to gouerne ye congregacion of God, whom he hath purchased wt his bloud.
author: Becon, Thomas, 1512-1567.
title: A newe pathway vnto praier ful of much godly frute and christe[n] knowledge, lately made by Theodore Basille.

text: For we read yt Enos ye sonne of Seth dyd fyrst begynne to call on the name of the LORDE, before ony temple was buylded.

text: For it bringeth a mā to the knowledge of hym selfe, & makethe hym desyrous for to praye, that he maye be deliuered frō this great enormite.

text: But it can not be proued therby, that like rewardes are not promiſſed vnto the other, ſith that oure ſauioure Ieſus Chriſte doeth expreſſely affirme, that the righteous ſhal ſhine as ye ſunne in the kingdom of god.
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.

text: Becauſe that aboue all other, they be ſubiecte to perſequution and trouble, and therfore they haue moſt nede of coumforte, that they may with a good corage take vpon them, this moſte parilous, and troubleſome office, and perſeuere in it to the ende.
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.
title: The ouerthrow of the iustification of workes and of the vain doctrin of the merits of men with the true affection of the iustification of faith and of the good workes that procead or come of the same,

text: Not by the workes of righteouſneſſe, whiche we had done, but according to his merci he ſaued vs, by the waſſhinge of the new byrthe, & the renewing of the holy ghoſt, which he ſhed on vs aboundātli, through Ieſu Chriſt our ſauiour.
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.
title: The ouerthrow of the iustification of workes and of the vain doctrin of the merits of men with the true affection of the iustification of faith and of the good workes that procead or come of the same,

text: For, as fyer by caſtinge in of woodde, is augmented and made bygger: ſo in the Chriſtians, bothe Godlines and faythe, is by doynge of good workes, nouriſhed and made liuely.
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.
title: The ouerthrow of the iustification of workes and of the vain doctrin of the merits of men with the true affection of the iustification of faith and of the good workes that procead or come of the same,

text: Why do they not rather feare the vnquencheable fyer of hell, that oure ſauioure Ieſus Chriſte doeth ſpeake of, ſayinge: Departe ye frome me, ye curſed in to the fyer euerlaſtinge, whyche is prepared for the Deuyll and hys Aungelles?
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.
title: The ouerthrow of the iustification of workes and of the vain doctrin of the merits of men with the true affection of the iustification of faith and of the good workes that procead or come of the same,

text: Becauſe, that they do by theyr vnbeliefe and frutes of the ſame, deſerue thoſe puniſhementes of hell fyer: but it can not be truly ſayed, that the electe and choſen doe by theyr workes merit or deſerue the endeleſſe ioye and felicitye of heauen.
author: Véron, John, d. 1563.

text: No, for he made him good, and vnto the likeneſſe of his owne ſelfe, that is, endued with true righteouſnes and holineſſe, that he ſhoulde rightly know God his maker, and hartely loue him, and liue for euer with him, to that end that he might loue & prayſe him.

text: Come forth you daughters Iuda doth infold, And your great King, ritch Salomon behold, Crownd with that Diadem of sacred sway; VVherewith his Mother in his nuptiall feast, Adornd his shyning temples glorious crest, And in his harts tryumphant Holy day.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: Then did I rise, for no repose could please, And search the Citty, Streets, and open wayes, All to finde out my soules long lacking blisse, Incessant suite, endles my quest remaynd, And of my Loues losse mightely complaynd, Yet found I not whom my desires did misse.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: Earth boasts hir flowers, birds brag their singing time, And in our land the Turtles voice doth chime.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: Thy belly as faire heapes of wheate abound, So is the rysing and the downe release, VVhilst pale-facst Lillies it impalleth round.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: But when I came, nothing to me was knowne, Discording vnagreements raind therein, Then did my soule with wings that wel had flowne, Adresse me like the Charriots that within Swiftly to hale thy noble troupes begin.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: The Foxes take which makes our vines to bleede Thou mine, I thine, thou dost on Lyllies feede.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: Thether delight inticst my feruent zeale, And in my rest, thy fruite to wonder at, Vnto my mouth all honie-sweets reueale.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.
title: The poem of poems. Or, Sions muse contayning the diuine song of King Salomon, deuided into eight eclogues.

text: And those bright flames which from her being haue, Are vehement, raging mad, & will no object saue.

text: Then shall my ioy in thee be compleat fram'd, And thine eternall happy-making loue, Then iuice of swelling grapes; or what is nam'd By sweeter stile; I will record aboue All reach; because the iust in thee doe moue.
author: Markham, Gervase, 1568?-1637.

title: Ane shorte and generall confession of the trewe Christiane fayth and religion, according to Godis Word and actis of our Parliamentis subscriued be the Kingis Maiestie and his housholde, with sindrie v

text: So that we are not moued for any worldlye reſpect, but are perſwaded onely in our conſcience, through the knowledge and loue of Gods trew Religion, prented in our hearts by the holie Spirite, as we ſhall anſwer to him in the day when the ſecretes of all heartis ſhalbe diſcloſed.

text: If any man may not weare womens apparel for lightnesse, may hee weare the diuells apparell, and cloath himselfe with pride, with coueteousnes, with enuy, with hipocrisie, with vncleannes, and when he is like the diuell sit at Gods table?
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: So that to put on Christ, is to put on the new man with all his vertues, vntill wee be renued to the image of Christ, which is like a new man amongst men.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: Some put on Christ as a gloue, which coueteth but the hand, so they put on the face of Christ, or the tong of Christ, but their hands worke, and their feete walke as they did before.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: First (saith Paul) you must cast away the workes of darkenes, und then put on the Armour of light.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: He putteth on Christ as Iesus which beleeueth in none but him, and hee putteth on Christ as Christ which worshippeth none but him, beleeueth in none but him and heareth none but him.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: God forbad his people to weare linsey wolsey, because it was a sign of inconstancy, but this is inconstancy it selfe.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: This garmēt is called an Armour, because it defendeth vs from all the assalts of the diuel, the flesh the world, the heate of persecution, and the cold of defection.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: For God saith not, This is my beloued Sonne which pleaseth mee, but In whome I am pleased: meaning that not onely Christ pleaseth God, but we please God in Christ, For Christ is our head.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.
title: The vvedding garment

text: Much lesse will God agree that the diuel shuld haue part of the soule, which would not yeeld him part of the body.
author: Smith, Henry, 1550?-1591.

text: As for the Prince of Parma he commeth not into the field, but keepeth himſelfe cloſe for feare of daunger that might thereby inſue vnto his perſon.

text: Beſides thoſe aforeſaid which were ſlaine, there was alſo about the number of foure hundred more, who beeing ſore hurt, wcre carried into Nimweghen.

text: The reaſon is, becauſe ſome of his chiefeſt Townes are reuolted, and his greateſt ſtrength of horſes and horſemen lately by Gods prouidence ſcattered, ſlaine, and taken priſoners, beſides ſundry of his footmen maymed, diſcomfited, & put to the ſword, as appeareth by this hiſtorie particularly enſuing.

text: It was a great incouragement and comfort vnto all the common ſoldiers, to ſee his excellencie continually in the field all the time of the battell, who promiſed vnto them all, that they ſhould not goe one foote further than he would hazard his owne perſon.

author: T. R.

text: And though our God be mercifull, yet is he iuſte and true: And muſt of iuſtice puniſhe ſinne, with plagues by iuſtice due: Whiche none is able to endure, and ſaue hymſelf at length, If he be but a creature, and haue no greater ſtrength.
author: T. R.
title: The Catechisme in meter for the easier learnyng, and better remembryng of those prinples [sic] of our faithe, whiche wee ought moste familiarly to be acquainted withall / for the proofe of those thyng

text: And therefore I beleeue at length, that Chriſt as Iudge ſhall come: To quit his choſen Sheepe, and damne, the reſte by righteous doome.

text: I take not vppon me to directe you, but I tell you what I wiſhe, that the ſame benefite whiche I myſelf and other yoùr hearers, haue receiued by your preaching, might alſo by other your trauailes, redounde to the comforte of them, who neuer heard you.
author: T. R.
title: The Catechisme in meter for the easier learnyng, and better remembryng of those prinples [sic] of our faithe, whiche wee ought moste familiarly to be acquainted withall / for the proofe of those thyng

text: The bread and wine doe teache, that as without the naturall food Our thirſt and hunger none can ſwage: ſo nought but Chriſt his blood, And ſuffryngs can refre ſhe the ſettle, with ſinne oppreſt and pinde: Whiche ſtill doeth runne into diſpaire, till Chriſt doe come to minde.
author: T. R.
title: The Catechisme in meter for the easier learnyng, and better remembryng of those prinples [sic] of our faithe, whiche wee ought moste familiarly to be acquainted withall / for the proofe of those thyng

text: And I doubte not but that the good acceptyng of theſe firſtlynges of your labours, and the greate profite whiche this ſmall booke ſhall bryng to the Churche of GOD, will enbolden and animate you to proceede to the publiſhyng of greater matters.
author: T. R.

text: Againe, this God Almightie is, 'creatyng all of none: And he in heauen in yearth and hell, doeth gouerne all alone.

text: BEtonia is an herbe called Betayne or byſchoppes worte, this herde hathe hole leues, but they be endēted by the ſydes without, & it hath a red flower in the croppe of the ſtalke.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Alſo it is good to make a man to haue a harde wombe, & this herbe is hote and drye.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: MOther worte or mogworte, this herbe is called in latyn Artemeſia, and it is hote and drye in the thyrde degre, this herbe helpeth a woman to conceyue a chylde, clēſeth the mother, and maketh a woman to haue her flowers, and it dyſtroyeth the emerawdes on this maner.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Alſo yf a man haue venym within hym, take this herbe and drye it & make powder therof, and do the powder in good wyne, and lette hym drynke it, & it wyll caſt vp all the venym, this herbe is hote and drye.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: For the ſtrangury and flux, alſo a ſtewe made with boylynge of it in water or wyne, is good for ye foreſayd yf it be boyled in oyle, and playſter it to the ſame aforeſayd, it is better.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Alſo Pyeny ſede whan it is blacke, it maketh delyueraunce of the bed of the chylde in her wōbe, and at euery tyme when ſhe ſhal vſe to drynke it, ſhe muſt drynke.xv. ſedes at one tyme.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Alſo therof is made ſayrope for the Dropſy that cōmeth of colde called ypoſarco, and it conſumeth watery humours.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Alſo ye water ye lycoryſe is ſoden in, is good agaynſt all ſyckenes of ye breſt and for the poſtume of the rybbes called Pleuereſy, it is colde and moyſte.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: Take the tymbre therof, and brene it to cooles, and make powdre therof, and then put it in a lynen cloth and rubbe thy teth therwith, and yf there be any wormes therin it ſhal ſlee them, and kepe thy teth from all euyls.
author: Macer, Floridus, attributed name.
title: A newe herball of Macer, translated out of Laten in to Englysshe

text: And so well she kepte her place there that to saye shortely anone she put her in batayle agaynst these men of Perse & dyscomfyted them.

text: And thus she conty nued tyl she came to her parfyte age in whiche she founde herselfe of a meruayllous strengthe & har dynesse / and then she was enfourmed of her fader of the wronge that he had of his subgectes.

text: J would not therefore imitate them, but onely ſpeake plainly according to all the wordes that haue fallen into my mouth whereby God hath holpen me to bring the ſame to paſſe.
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.

text: See wee not that they ſeeke to deliuer and abandon, as it were in praye, this poore kingdome, to the Spaniſh nation?
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: How many holy and iuſt edicts haue we had, and eſpecially the Edict of Ianuary made in the yere of grace. 1561. vnder King Charles the ninth, which was both good and lawfully made, to the benefite as well of the one as other religion.
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: For likewiſe God hath vſed me in this worke, whome I doe beſeech to open the heartes of Kinges and Princes, and to deliuer them from blindneſſe which ſtoppeth their ſights, and to make them partakers of his cleare light which is the knowledge of his will.
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: See wee not many times the whole body periſh through ſome wound, not onely in the Arme or Thigh, but alſo ſome times through ſome ſmale inconuenience happened to the litle finger?
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: This ſufficiently ſheweth their peruerſe and miſchieuous mindes, as alſo that they haue no other deſire, but to deſtroy or vſurpe this Crowne of the Flowerdeluce: But what neede I ſo largely deſcribe a matter which all the world knoweth better then my ſelfe?
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: I we ſee a thiefe or robber take a pooremans purse in the wood, and doe not our endeuours to deliuor him from the ſaid oppreſſion, ſhall not we be guiltie of the treſpaſſe?
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: Marke the Serpent or any other venemous beaſt, when it ſtingeth any body, it ſeeketh not the head or any other principall member of the body, but onely or for the moſt part, the foot, and yet ye ſee the parſon ſo hurt dye of ſuch a ſtinging.
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: But nowe we ſee ſome that are willing to withſtand them, but doe feare to be ouer weake: Let vs not feare my frends, but conſider for what we fight.
author: Erondelle, Pierre, fl. 1586-1609.
title: A declaration and catholick exhortation to all Christian princes to succour the Church of God and realme of France. Written by Peter Erondelle, natife of Normandie. Faithfully translated out of the Fr

text: This commandement did God command to ye higher powers in the commō wealth of the Iſraelites, and that they ſhoulde not lift vp their hearts aboue their brothers, but to vſe indifferencie & iuſtice, with all indifferently, without exception of perſōs: as ye may read in the holy ſcripture.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: VVhat the ſinnes of the people be vvhere vvithall God is thus offended, you that haue the ouerſight of them, knovv or yee ought to know.

title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: And for a helpe vnto you, and alſo to the people in this behalfe, I haue ſet forth here the 13.

title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: The night is called the time of falſe doctrine and ignorancie, in which men liue naughtily vnpuniſhed, wher as the trew light, Chriſt and his word is not preached, there ye greteſt vertue is acompted vice, & vice accompted for vertue, & ſinnes rebuked, are excuſed & extenuated.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: By this rule men may know whither they haue charity, or not: for in caſe we deminiſh ye goods of our neighbors, whether they be of his bodye or his ſoule, or els of his poſſeſſions, honour, place, or dignitie.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: The ſecond part of S. Paules words commendeth the Magiſtrats for their vtilitie and commoditie in the common wealth becauſe that by their authoritie euill doers among the people are puniſhed and corrected: that honeſt and true men maye liue in reſt and quietneſſe.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: Where ſuch cōtentions & ſtrifs be, there is no charitie, S. Paule after theſe euils returneth againe to that we ſhoulde doe, ſaying.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: Saint Paul breketh his diſputation of duetyes, and will tary no longer in the enumeration and numbring of the partes and particulars of duetyes, but prefereth altogether ſo charitie in this wiſe.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: The firſt thing that he exhorteth vs to do, is to put on the armour of light, that is to ſay, to worke good works, of the which we ſhould not be aſhamed, neither before God, neither man: but boldly & honeſtly to walke in them.
author: Hooper, John, d. 1555.
title: Certaine godly, and most necessarie annotations vpon the thirteenth chapter to the Romanes: set forth by the right vigilant pastor: Iohn Hoper, by Gods calling, Bishop of Gloucester.

text: In quiet state you also lyude And wrong hath nere supprest, Your wyshed wealth, in carelesse ease You myght haue toke your rest.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: As lykewise viewe what madnes seemes Your trauels to possesse, For to pretende, who subiectes be, Your Princes to suppresse, Or to correct, as though yf that She error shoulde mayntayne, It were your duetie with the rod To worke your Princes payne.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: You wote your selues the yll successe That rebelles styll obtayne, You know the proofe was alwayes founde To worke their proper payne.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: And further, way the great reproche You reape to Englyshe soyle, And what an entraunce you haue made For foes to worke our spoyle.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: And thynke that yf it ambition is That hath deceaude your wyttes, How you are moylde in Plutoes lake Amongst a thousande fyttes.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: And why accursed, be not you By their deserued spoyle Aduysde to leaue your rashe deuise And shunne your shamefull foyle?
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: As lykewise thynke howe you disturbe The cause of common wealth, When as you ought imploy your payne For to deuise the health Therof, as also howe you seme Your countrey for to hate, With such contention which disdaynes Your countreys quiet state.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: And yet your owne indeuours all, Do interrupt the peace, The very meanes and redy wayes Misorder to increase.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: For he by ryght may happy hyght, Who happy can eschewe By others payne the care that would Through want of care ensue.
author: Elviden, Edmund, poet.
title: A neweyeres gift to the rebellious persons in the north partes of England Primo Ianuar. 1570. Seene and alowed, accordyng to the order appoynted.

text: It happened after, that Hercules amid his great victories, with fame of which he filled the world, chaunced to beholde the admirable Iole, the fairest and most goodly virgin that the world in that age affoorded: Her he honored and loued, and at length obteined.

text: Mee-thinkes I ſee old Abraham, vnbracing of his breſt: Saving bleſſed Branch come here and ſleepe, and take thy quiet reſt.

text: Thou haſt not hid my Talents, nor my bleſſings in the ground: Thou haſt not bene a wauering reed, but faithfull, ſtrong, and ſound.

text: This world is full of ſnares and trappes, temptations vnto ſinne, As well in generations paſt, as this that we liue in.
author: S. P.

text: The Lambe ſhall wipe away thy teares, his blood hath waſht away, All worldly cares and blemiſhes, and here is perfect day.

text: And imagenyng (saith he) we leade our lifes, meanyng, that we imagine it possible for vs to be happie in this darkenesse, and in these vanitees, whiche in vaine we busie and trauaile our selfes to gette.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: And wheather it be in peace or in warre, openly or priuilie, speakyng or doyng, alwaies it shalbe necessarie for hym to folowe the lawes, and not to departe from theim, but to be an executour of them.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: It is written in the epistle to the Hebrews, that we haue no stedfast abidyng here: but that we seke one, whiche shall be our habitacion.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: And the emperour Adrian caused those to be slayne, that he myght here shoulde excell him in any thyng, to the entent he myght remayne as most excellent of his tyme.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: Some other kepe open shoppes of ghostly thinges, sellyng not onely the thynges that ought not to be solde: but also those that are impossible to be bought.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: Wherfore nowe syns our propretee is suche, lette vs awake from our longe drowsie slepe, and beatyng our whynges together mount on the tippe toe, Appliyng wel our eies towardes that twyndyng lewre, That our celestiall kynge hath made for vs so pure.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: And this made Artaxerxes vnto.ccclx. women that he kepte, to ioygne in the noumbre of his concubines.ii. of his owne daughters.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: And in his hunger had stones presented vnto him, went seekyng fruite on the trees, and founde none, for thirste demaunded water of a straunge woman, and in his last thyrst was fedde with a most bitter drinke.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: For wheras our vnderstanding hath no cleere knowlage of thynges, and therfore can not be quiete, it foloweth, that not quietyng it selfe, it is impossible it shoulde feele the true felicitee.
author: Thomas, William, Clerk of the Council to Edward VI.
title: The vanitee of this world

text: God vseth the diuels by his prouidence to accomplish the woorke which he determineth, eyther in wrath vpon the wicked, or for chastisement and tryall of his Children.

text: For they hold that witches should bee put to death, and not onely that, but are inflamed with a wonderfull rage and fury to haue it accomplished.

text: Ye ſhal know no foreine to buy or ſell any marchaundiſe with any other foreine within ye Citie or the Fraūchiſe therof, but ye ſhall warne the Chamberlaine therof, or ſome miniſter of the Chāber.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: YE ſhall ſweare that ye ſhall be good and true to our Soueraigne Lady Queene Elizabeth, &c. and to the heyres of our ſayd ſoueraigne Lady the Queene.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: Ye ſhall impleade or ſue no free man out of this Citie, whiles ye may haue right & law within the ſame Citie.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: All theſe pointes and Articles ye ſhall well and truely keepe accordyng to the lawes & cuſtome of this Citie to your power.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: Ye ſhall alſo keepe the Queenes peace in your owne perſons, ye ſhall know no gatheryngs, conuenticles nor cōſpiracies made agaynſt the Queenes peace, but ye ſhall warne the Maior therof, or let it to your power.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: The Fraunchiſes & cuſtomes therof ye ſhall maintaine, and this Citie keepe harmeles in that that in you is.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: Ye ſhall be contributorie to all manner of charges within this Citie, as ſummons, Watches, contributions, taſkes, tallages, lot, and ſcot, and all other charges, bearyng your part as a free man ought to doe.
title: The othe of euery free man of the Citie of London.

text: Hence it is that in this booke of iudges there is no mention made of their ciuil iudgements or that they did cal together the Senate or the people, vnlesse it were to warre, or of any edictes which they made or of faults which they did redresse or punish.

text: Yea they haue the full and absolute authority of the land in their owne handes, and inherēt in their own persons, insomuch that al others within their dominions ioyntly and seuerally considered, are in respect of them priuate men.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: Salomon or A treatise declaring the state of the kingdome of Israel, as it was in the daies of Salomon Whereunto is annexed another treatise, of the Church: or more particularly, of the right constitu

text: Yea it is a greate signe, that they who doe not yeelde obedience at the first, wilbe afterwards more and more hardned as the Apostle writeth, 2.

text: If it be obiected that in so smal a number as are three or foure persons, there cannot be al the officers, much lesse the bodie of a Church, we confesse that they cannot make a perfect Church, yet a true Church.

text: To take one example of many and so to conclude this point, and specially the first edict which the first king made, and that by the immediate motion of the spirit of God, because this is most for the purpose of the matter in hand.

text: Yea this is agreeable to the word of God, which teacheth that we ought not to doe that which is good, but by good, lawful and ordinarie meanes: but to resist the ciuill power, is euill, and greatly displeasing in the eyes of God.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.
title: Salomon or A treatise declaring the state of the kingdome of Israel, as it was in the daies of Salomon Whereunto is annexed another treatise, of the Church: or more particularly, of the right constitu

text: For howsoeuer some kindes of gouernment and magistracy are conuenient or inconuenient, safe or dangerous, yet this and all other kindes are to be accounted lawfull.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.

text: Yea also in time by this hereditarie succession, the kingdome became of great antiquitie, which addeth much to the maiestie of meane thinges, much more to those which in many other respectes are excellent.
author: Morton, Thomas, of Berwick.

text: We confesse indeede that so many of them as liued in those times wherein poperie did corrupt the worshippe of God, had iust cause of separation, and that they might more commodiously and lawfully serue God in the vastest desert then in the most populous Church being in that case.

text: Howe do they that calle women quenes and Empreſſis / do they make them ſo / bycauſe they calle them?
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: I ſpeke nat onely of fleſſhe / where of the veſſel of election ſaint Paule ſpeketh this ſentēce / ſayeng: Hit is good to eate no fleſſhe nor drinke no wyne: but alſo of pulſe / all thoſe that be full of wynde & heuye ſhulde be eſchewed.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: For ſuche a one deſerued to ſe Chriſte fyrſte in the temple / and to propheſie of hym to them that were preſēt.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: And ſhe that anſwered ſuche as came to aſke any thyng of Apollo in Delphis / was euer a virgine: of whom the fyrſte was Phemone / whiche fyrſte foūde verſe royal.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: Nor Mary Magdalene / whiche ſate at the fote of our lorde and herde his worde / dyd nat only vſe the contemplation of heuenly thynges / but ſhe dyd that whether ſhe redde / or herde / or prayde.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: You wyues / whanne you put of your ſmokkes / put vpon chamefaſtnes / and kepe alway both day and night both in cōpany of other men and of your huſbandes / bothe in the lyght & in the darke / that mooſte honeſte vayle of nature.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: But they call them ſelfe louers / and I beleue they be ſo in dede / ye and blinde & madde to withall.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: Howe be it / if ſhe haue a great houſe / yt requireth moche mannes ſeruice / let her make ſome wel aged man ruler / that is ſadde and diſcrete / and of good conditions / whoſe honeſtie ſhalbe his maiſtres worſhip.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.
title: A very frutefull and pleasant boke called the Instructio[n] of a Christen woma[n]/ made fyrst in Laten/ and dedicated vnto the quenes good grace/ by the right famous clerke mayster Lewes Uiues/ ; and

text: Nor I wyll nat do ſuche a diſpleaſure vnto that mooſte auncient and holy man / as either to paſſe as ſuperfluous that he hath tolde / or to reherſe hit vnder other maner / but by & by wryte here as he hath put in his boke.
author: Vives, Juan Luis, 1492-1540.

text: Haue not many had, full sorrowfull hartes, By losing of that which they did spare: Had they not better haue taken their partes, Then so for others, them selues to make bare.

text: But ebbing and flowing, Comming and going, It neuer doth rest: Therefore when you may, Make no delay, For that is the best.

text: But better doe so, then as they liue, by thée uery, Catching and snatching, all that euer they can, Because that (say they) Tyde taryeth no Man.

text: So we accoumpt those countreyes but ill, Which vicious persons doth mainteine and norish, Although they haue all thinges at their will, And although in treasure they aboundauntly florish.

text: Because that no man from his pleasure will rest, But ech man doth take the time of his gayne, Although the same be to others great payne.

text: Therfore wyl I make the ſicke, ſtryking the and makyng the deſolate for thy ſinnes, Thou ſhalt eate and not be ſatiſfyed for miſerye ſhall go thorowe thee, thou ſhalte go vnto thy wyfe, but ſhee ſhal he barren, and that whyche ſhe doth brynge foorthe, ſhall I geue vnto the ſwerd.
author: Gilby, Anthony, ca. 1510-1585.

text: How be it to the almyghty power of the euerlyuyng Lord, vnto whom al godlye Prophetes and preachers alway prouoketh al thinges that he pleaſeth are mooſte eaſye to be fulfylled.
author: Gilby, Anthony, ca. 1510-1585.
title: A commentarye vpon the prophet Mycha. Wrytten by Antony Gilby. Anno Domi. M.D.Li

text: Let vs therfore tremble and diligently gyue eare when the Lord ſpeaketh, and wyth feare and reuerence humble oure ſelues to his name.

text: For the ſpyryte of God ſeeth from time to time contynuallye oure iniquytyes, and ſtryueth euermore there agaynſte, No hyll is ſo hyghe, no valleye ſo low, that he ſeeth not.
author: Gilby, Anthony, ca. 1510-1585.
title: A commentarye vpon the prophet Mycha. Wrytten by Antony Gilby. Anno Domi. M.D.Li

text: O brethren and children of Abraham and thei amonges you which feareth God, vnto you is the woord of ſaluacion ſent, & in ye Pſaſ. ciii.

text: So that God whyche in hys ſubſtaunce is vnſearcheable by mercy, pytye and truthe, ſheweth hym ſelfe vnto men.

text: Great sumptuous Feasts the stomacke doth dislike, Which oft in bodie dangerous surfets breed: Where dishes few reuiue our sense and spright, And Nature's pleasd on little for to feed.
author: Tofte, Robert, 1561-1620.

text: Then with thine eyes into my brest doo peere, (VVhich for the nonce I leaue to open sight) And that which now thou doubtst, see shalt thou cleere Ah, marke it then; and view what showes so bright.

text: The haplesse Argus (happie in this same) The glorie of the Sunnes surpassing light, The brightnes of the Starres (the fire which staine) VVith hundred eyes behold them alwayes might.

text: Thou (pretie Soule) hast both the colours rare Of these sweet flowers, which others all exceed; Thy Brest's a bed of beauteous Lillies faire, Thy daintie cheekes pure damask Roses breed.

title: Laura The toyes of a traueller. Or The feast of fancie. Diuided into three parts. By R.T. Gentleman.

text: FOrtune (cros frend to euer-cōquring Loue) Our bodies (Ladie) hath deuided farre, But yet our cōstant minds she cannot moue, Which ouer strong for her deuises are: Woe's me, in England thou dost bide, & I (Scarse shadow of my selfe) in Italy.
author: Tofte, Robert, 1561-1620.
title: Laura The toyes of a traueller. Or The feast of fancie. Diuided into three parts. By R.T. Gentleman.

text: Then is she cruell lesse than thou art now, Since blood her pleasd, and thee harts cannot bow.
author: Tofte, Robert, 1561-1620.
title: Laura The toyes of a traueller. Or The feast of fancie. Diuided into three parts. By R.T. Gentleman.

text: Of both our harts, make but one louing hart, And giue it vnto which thou please of twaine: Giue it to her, to her doo it impart, Or vnto mee: it skills not much the same.
author: Tofte, Robert, 1561-1620.
title: Laura The toyes of a traueller. Or The feast of fancie. Diuided into three parts. By R.T. Gentleman.

text: In vastie Sea, faine would my slender Muse VVade in thy praise, to praise thy beautie right: But (Ladie) I for pardon craue excuse, To breake such waues too brittle is her might: Meane time with lowly Verse, in humble show, A long the shallow shoare Ile wading goe.
author: Tofte, Robert, 1561-1620.
title: Laura The toyes of a traueller. Or The feast of fancie. Diuided into three parts. By R.T. Gentleman.

text: For it is not enough to doe that which he commandeth except we doe it as he commaundeth the ſame to bee done.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: So muſt wee deale in the practiſe of thinges indifferent to cut of occaſion from them that ſeeke occaſion, that God in al things may bee glorified, the prince obeyed, ſuperſtion baniſhed, the people edified and the peace of the church preſerved.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: For to him that iudgeth any thing to be vncleane, to him it is vncleane, Rom. 14.14.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: The reaſonable creatures that behold vs on this earth, are devided by S. Paul into 2. ſortes. 1.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: As if a man vſe this meate & refuſe that, vſe this garment, and refuſe that, thinking therby to pleaſe God, he indeede ſinneth againſt him.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: The ſecond part contayneth the reaſons to mooue men to bee circumſpect in the cariage of themſelues in the matter of things indifferent.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: For often it commeth to paſſe, that with whom wee converſe familiarly in worldely thinges, by him wee are drawne, either from our profeſſion, or from the former zeale, wee were wont to haue there in, beſides the corruption of our maners.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: The vnreaſonable creaturs, that behold vs, ought to affray vs, leſt, as Balaams Aſſe had a mans voice givē him to reprooue the fooliſhnes of his maiſter: ſo theſe ſhould bee produced againſt vs as witneſſes of our actions which wee haue donne in their preſence.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: Frō hence we learne, that ſuch as make conſcience of every thing which they do, muſt circumſpectly bee dealt with, leſt they bee led out of the way, or bee driven to diſpaire by a matter of it ſelfe of ſmall importance.
author: Presse, Symon, b. 1558 or 9.
title: A sermon preached at Eggington in the county of Darby concerning the right vse of things indifferent, the 3. day of August, 1596. By Symon Presse minister there.

text: I thanke you good Maistres K. for your letter and for your medicine, and for your good will to him to whom you before did owe ſo little.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: But theſe temptations Christ hath ouercome in vs, and giuen vs his ſpirite, in which we knowe aſſuredlie that the Lord reigneth: neyther ſlacketh he his comminge, as many accounte ſlacknes, but he will come, and his glorie ſhalbe knowen.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: If we will not leaue ſonne, daughter, and our own life for his ſake, can one heare fall from your ſonnes heade but at Christes commaundement?
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: Nowe that this ioye may be yours, and this gladnes your inheritāce, prepare your ſelfe, not in your own wiſdō, for that hath alredie deceiued you, but in the wiſdome of god, that your hope may be ſure.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: Haue you not bene tempted with opinions of creatures, as though ſome were more holy, ſome more prophane?
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: You knowe what is the comfort of houſes and landes: you haue weighed them well and found them light.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: And as touching the iſſue of all my buſineſſe, looke for the worst, hope for the best, and beare whatſoeuer ſhall fall.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: This boldnes you haue through him who hath made manifest his grace vnto you, that you denying impietie & worldly concupiſcence, ſhould liue ſoberly, purely, and godly in this preſent life, and looke for the bleſſed hope that ſhall be reuealed, when all ſecretes ſhall be opened.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: Learne therefore first the worde of God, this is the ſeede of regeneration, by which wee are made newe creatures, this is the bread of ſpiritual nouriſhment, by which we are growne vp into eternall life.
author: Dering, Edward, 1540?-1576.
title: Certaine godly and verie comfortable letters, full of christian consolation. Written by M. Ed Dering vnto sondry of his friends. And nowe published, for the proffite of the Church of God

text: The wife did ioy to heare the ioyfull huſband ſay, How happy hap, how meete a match, he had found out that day.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: Know ſyr that yeſterday my lady and your wyfe, I wot not by what ſodain grefe, hath made exchaunge of life: And for becauſe on earth, ſhe found nought but vnreſt, In heauen hath ſhe ſought to fynde a place of quiet reſt.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: Of Counte Paris ſute, and how my lord my ſyre, By my vngrate and ſtubborne ſtryft, I ſtyrred vnto yre.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: Thapothecary, high is hanged by the throte, And for the paynes he tooke with him, the hangman had his cote.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: But though her grieuous paynes diſtraind her tender hart, Yet with an outward ſhewe of ioye ſhe cloked inward ſmart.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: And now the wedding weedes for mourning weedes they chaunge, And Hymene into a Dyrge, alas it ſeemeth ſtraunge.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: Wherfore repreſſe at once, the paſſions of thy hart, And where there is no cauſe of greefe, cauſe hope to heale thy ſmart.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: All meanes ſhe ſought of her, and howſhold folke, to know The certaine roote, whereon her greefe, and booteles mone doth growe.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: For as her happy ſtate, no long whyle ſtandeth ſure, Euen ſo the heauy plight ſhe brings, not alwayes doth endure.
author: Brooke, Arthur, d. 1563.
title: The tragicall historye of Romeus and Iuliet written first in Italian by Bandell, and nowe in Englishe by Ar. Br.

text: Then ſhall he geue rayne to yo wer ſede whiche ye ſhall committe vnto the grounde / and it ſhall bringe forth fode from the erthe: and there ſhalbe plentye and grete aboundaunce.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: That in no maner of wyſe ſhall he enter into this cyte / no not ſo myche as an arowc ſhal he ſhote hither / there ſhal no ſhylde or buckler be bente vp agenſte hyr.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: Then ſhal the Aſſyrions be a frayde at the voyce of the lorde which ſhal ſmyte thē with a rodde / and the rodde that the Lorde ſhal bende agenſt them ſhal go thorow euery foundacion.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: I turne the drye deſerte into a ponde of wutr / & the thirſtye erthe I watr with moyſt vaynes.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: Be not ſo ſore angrye (Lorde I beſeche the) nether remember owr iniquites alwayes / but rathr (I praye the) conſyder al vs to be thy people.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: Beholde / I ſhall bringe backe the ſhadue of the dyall which ſhadne is now deſcended withe the ſonne aryſinge in Ahazdy all and ſhall turne it vp agene.x. howers: then turned backe the ſonne the ſame.x. degrees aſcending agene by the which the ſhadue had deſcended before.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: But contrarywiſe: wo be to the vngodly ād wykedman which ſhalbe rewarded accordī ge to the workes of his owne handes.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: It is Ialone that tolde you theſe thinges before / & I only ſhal call & brīge him fort & make proſperouſe his iourneye.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.
title: The prophete Isaye, translated into englysshe, by George Ioye

text: This nacion roreth lyke a lyon / and grenneth lyke the lyons whelpes / they ſhal grenne and ſnatche vp their proye / nether ſhal there be one that maye eſcape / nor yet eny that maye delyuer them Thei ſhal grenne vpon the people of Iſrael at yt tyme like a fyerce ſea.
author: Joye, George, d. 1553.

text: No man denieth that the people that came of Sem the ſonne of Noe, is the moſt ancient: among theſe remained the Church of God and the Hebrue toong.

text: To giue the better gloſſe to the former picture, another cleane contrarie, and maruellous fearfull to behold, he ſetteth here before our eyes the picture of a Tyrant that liueth in miſtruſt of the whole world, as did Dionyſius the elder tyrant of Sicilie, of whom we reade among the liues of Plutarch.
author: Du Bartas, Guillaume de Salluste, seigneur, 1544-1590.
title: Babilon, a part of the Seconde vveeke of Guillaume de Saluste seigneur du Bartas, with the commentarie, and marginall notes of S.G.S. Englished by William L'Isle

text: More than this, a Tyrant defileth himſelf with inceſts, whooredomes, adulteries, and the ſinne of Sodom, and therewith infecteth his whole court and countrie: as that filthie Nero did, whoſe life is written by Suetonius, Tacitus, and others, reciting therein many horrible and ſhamefull caſes.
author: Du Bartas, Guillaume de Salluste, seigneur, 1544-1590.

text: Adam liued 930. yéeres, his poſteritie kept his language, and although they poſſeſſed with their tents and dwellings a large péece of ground, yet is there no place of Scripture to be found, whereout may be gathered any proofe of the diuerſitie of toongs before the flood.
author: Du Bartas, Guillaume de Salluste, seigneur, 1544-1590.
title: Babilon, a part of the Seconde vveeke of Guillaume de Saluste seigneur du Bartas, with the commentarie, and marginall notes of S.G.S. Englished by William L'Isle

text: There being then but one, it muſt néedes be the ſame that Adam taught his children: as may alſo appéere by this, that all proper names vntill the flood are Hebrue.
author: Du Bartas, Guillaume de Salluste, seigneur, 1544-1590.
