title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: The ryghteous mouth: is traynd in south, in wisdom (godly) all inured: Hys tonge wyll talke: all wysdomes walke, in sentence ryght (alway) assured.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: If any take counsaile against thée, as Achitophell dyd against Dauid, if thou be admonished thereof, sing.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: His déede is worthy prayse: most worshipfull I say, It Glory is: and comlynes: his iustice lasts for aye.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: Yea euen my frendes: familiar, at me (in scorne) they lyft theyr héeles: Euen they that farde: as I dyd fare, yet me (to trap) they markt at meales.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: But when I sayd: my foote doth réele, to note the worldes disdayne: Then helpe O Lord: thou didst me deale, thy grace dyd me sustayne.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: Gods law is iust: a law to trust, as spotlesse turnyng hartes: His wytnes pure: record is sure, to babe it wyt impartes.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: And last he gaue them whole: the gentils landes by met: They all possest: for heritage: for which the people swet.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: O bring my soule: from prison bound Thy name to celebrate: So iust men wil: me glad surround, whan thou shalt quite my state.
author: Parker, Matthew, 1504-1575.
title: The vvhole Psalter translated into English metre, which contayneth an hundreth and fifty Psalmes. The first quinquagene

text: Manie times was she about to satisfie the spite of her minde, and tell Basilius, how she knewe Zelmane to bee farre otherwise then the outwarde appearance.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: Alas, better had it bene thou hadst ended nobly thy noble daies: what death is so euil as vnworthy seruitude?
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: True it is, that Amphialus was the sooner vp; but Argalus had his sworde out the sooner: and then fell they to the cruellest combate, that any present eye had seene.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: Betwixt these two a way doth lie, Away more worthie beauties fame, Then that which beares the Milkie name.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: O, would he say, all you that affect the title of wisdome, by vngratefull scorning the ornaments of Nature, am I now piping in a shaddow? or doo slouthfull feathers now enwrap me?
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: If once thou maist that fancie glosse destroy Within thy selfe, thou soone wilt be ashamed To be a player of thine owne annoy.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: What is to be thought passed betwixt two such vertuous creatures, whereof the one hath confessed murder, and the other rape, I leaue to your wise cōsideration.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: Hold for certaine most worthy Musidorus, it is your selfe I loue, which can no more be diminished by these showers of euill hap, then flowers are marred with the timely raynes of Aprill.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: Ah where was first that cruell cunning found, To frame of Earth a vessell of the minde, Where it should be to selfe-destruction bound?
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia. Written by Sir Philip Sidney Knight. Now since the first edition augmented and ended

text: Hauilah hath not onelie good golde: but it hath alſo Bdelium, and the Onix ſtone, and wiſedome comprehendeth many good things.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: That ſinne hath ſo many & ſo mightie patrones to ſooth it vp: as the high prieſtes harted the Souldiers with we will ſaue you harmeleſſe.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: Or vſe it as ſalt (for you muſt haue ſalt in your ſelues) as if you were either ſhaped out of the pillar that was Lots wife: or Elizeus had ſprinkled ſome of that ſalt vpon you which hee caſt into the ſpring of Ierico.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: When talents were deliuered, the owner ſaid, Occupie till I come: ſofte and faire ſaith the Papiſt, for we may do works of ſupererogation, and ſo you may ſoone haue your owne with aduauntage: as though none of them were vnprofitable ſeruantes, but could performe their duties and more too.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: And the ſpirit ſpake not in ſport that ſaide: Beholde I ſende vnto you wiſe men: but mēt that the neglecting of Gods mercie, is the next way to plucke downe his iuſtice.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: As the meane is directed to the ende: ſo God ſanctified the ſeuenth daie vnto vs, that wee might ſtill keepe it holie vnto him.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: I tell you the ſmall care and great eaſe that a number haue, is a great cauſe why Gods building goeth forward ſo ſlackly.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: If Sion woulde not heare for her owne good, yet Eſay muſt open his mouth for the churches ſake: and Ezechiell muſt ſpeake in the name of the Lorde, that they may knowe that there hath beene a Prophet among them: for his ſure diſcharge, and their certaine confuſion.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: He whoſe wiſedome is pregnant, whoſe learning is competent, and whoſe bodie is healthful, & yet is in al points helples in his calling, that is an Idoll.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The good sheepheardes dutie by George Phillips.

text: Whereof we haue now (God be thanked) a faire example, of the glorious victory, which we through Gods helpe, had at the ſtrong Towne of Raab.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: And raiſe vp ſuch valiant Souldiers, and giue them ſuch harts and courage: that with the comfort of Gods helpe, dare goe vnder the very noſes of their Enemies.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: For looke what could not rearh to the Towne: The ſame did the Lord Palſi, lay hold on, and ſlew.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: The Lorde Adolph of Swartzburg, with certaine great Ordinance, went before the Caſtle, and with ſhooting opened the ſame, wherein he found about 600.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: Eſpecially becauſe God heard the harty ſighing and earneſt prayers of his faithfull, himſelfe ſtanding by, and helping our Chriſtian Souldiers.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: It was alſo well furniſhed with victuals and other prouiſions, and almoſt in euery houſe, was great ſtore found.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: That they with great multitudes ſhould ouer-runne, harry, and ſpoyle Chriſtendome, and all through his wrath, by reaſon of our ſinne.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: Which winde did driue the noyſe of our Souldiers and theyr furniture backe from the Enemy, and theyr comming ſo vnlooked for, that they could not perceiue any thing at all.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: From thence hes preſently ſent about midnight, a hundred choſen men on horſebacke and on foote, before to Raab, with certaine wagons, laden with Boate-bridges, Skaling-ladders, and inſtruments of fire-workes.
author: W. S. R.
title: True newes of a notable victorie obtayned against the Turkes, by the right honourable Lorde, Adolph Baron of Swartzburg, the 18. day of March last past, anno 1598 vvhen as he and his armie three houre

text: So manie vvere the misfortunes, (most renoumed and beavvtifull Princesse) of the desolate knight my master, as neither the shortnes of the time vvil suffer me to repeat, nor the greatnes af the misterie to remember?
author: Goldwel, Henry.

text: Which speech being done, the defendants came in, in such order as they came in the day before, therefore I shal not need to make a newe repetition of the same, sith al hath bene touched already.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: Yeelde yeelde O yeelde, trust not on beauties pride, fayrenesse though fayer, is but a feeble shielde, VVhen strong Desire, which vertues loue doth guide, claymes but to gaine his due, O yeelde O yeelde.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: But if (alasse but let not that be needful) BEAVTIR be accompanied vvith disdainfull pride, and pride vvaighted on by refusing crueltie.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: At which day abouesaid for certain vrgent occasions, the saide Challenge and Triumph by her Maiesties commādement, was deferted till the first day of May.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: That if Desire did not banish dispaire as a traytor out of his kingdome, it vvoulde haue already vndermined their best grounded determination: but no invvard nor outvvarde vvounde, no vveakenesse, no vvearinesse, can daunt Desire, nor take avvay the natural effects that follovve it.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: Therefore I refer you to the reeding of them hereafter, But thus the desendaunts, entred the title yarde, one after an other as followeth.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: Nay rather Vew with what vnresistable determination themselues approch, And howe not onely the heauens send their inuisible Instrument to ayde them.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: So passing on one after another, when sir Thomas Parat and M. Cooke came to the end of the Tilt, ouer against the Queens Maiestie, one of their pages arraied like an Angel, vttred these speches vnto her.
author: Goldwel, Henry.
title: A briefe declaratio[n] of the shews, deuices, speeches, and inuentions, done performed before the Queenes Maiestie, the French ambassadours, at the most valiaunt and worthye triumph, attempted and exe

text: Alſo the holy Prophet Dauid hath theſe warrants throughout all his Pſalmes, to feare God, as firſt in the 2.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: All they are thoſe which binde themſelues to the obſeruation of Gods lawes and the popiſh ceremonies, and thinke except they obſerue and kéepe them, they are damned for euer.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: And therefore this laſte péece of Scripture that you recited in the third Chapter of Saint Iohns Epiſtle, is written, for a iuſt condemnation vnto all theſe wiſe worldly wiſardes, the Atheiſtes, and bellie gods, whoſe Ritchin is their Church, and bellie their God, and glory ende with ſhame.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: And the Papiſts belefe is, becauſe they haue left in them ſome féede of grace to doo good workes by it, they deſerue ſaluation, & becauſe they are Baptiſed, and ſo they ſhall with the vnbeléeuing Iewes that were circumciſed, & therfore (good children) of all people beware the Papiſts.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: Oh horrible, execrable, damnable, vile, preſumptuous curſed wretch, that dare preſume to violate and breake Gods holy precept, forbidden expreſſely in the firſt table and the ſeconde verſe.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: Therefore to conclude he that will raigne with Chriſt, muſt ſuffer with Chriſt, for by and through many tribulations, wee muſt enter into the kingdome of heauen.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: Yes verily, and ſo we now confeſſe, and are fully reſolued, but nowe we praye you, let vs vnderſtand the ſence or meaning of a Sacrament, and what it is.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: I pray you ſir, how muſt we frame our ſelues for to receyue this holy ſacrament faithfully and worthily.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: And the ſecond is to loue our neighbours & brethren as our ſelues, which is the fulfilling of the ſixe laſt precepts in the ſecond Table, that is to liue in righteouſnes all the dayes of our life, which power the Lorde God graunt vs for Chriſtes ſake.
author: Cotes, William, b. ca. 1560.
title: [A dialogue of diuerse quections [sic] demanded of the children to their father very necessary, and profitable both for children, and parents, masters and seruants.]

text: And laſt of al, for a final concluſion, what, & wher is the ful felicitie of the iuſt, which haue their part in the firſt reſurrection.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: Againſt this the papiſtes alſo ſay, that after life there is forgiueneſſe of ſinnes, to this mixed companye, which is obtained by their friendes, and merites of the Church, for them.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: Cicero hath ſaide, that true beatitude or bleſſedneſſe conſiſteth of two partes: Namely, to be frée from al kinde of want and miſerie: and ſo to abound in all goodneſſe, that on no parte he néedeth to aſke further.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: The firſt, neither féeling death or life in god, runneth headlong to his luſte, in infidelitie and gréedineſſe to ſinne: as though that onely were his chiefe beatitude.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: Praiſe and glorie, and wiſdome and thankes, and honour and power, and might be vnto God, for euer more, Amen.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: And nowe of theſe places we are to obſerue: Firſt, that there is a death, that goeth before this reſurrection.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: This is the nature of euery ſinne, and therefore they are rightly ſaide to bée deade, which be poſſeſſed of it: as wholly cut off from God, eſtraunged from his life, and deade to godlyneſſe.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: But others more lewde, haue ſonke themſelues to hell: with gaping after earthly treaſure, haue theſaured to themſelues in déede, the malediction of God, againſt the day of wrath.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: And at one worde to ſpeake it, herein conſiſteth the firſt reſurrection: To caſt away the works of darkeneſſe, and to put on, Chriſt the armour of light.
author: Anderson, Anthony, d. 1593.
title: A sermon of sure comfort preached at the funerall of Master Robert Keylwey Esquire, at Exton in Rutland, the 18. of Marche 1580. By Anthonie Anderson preacher, and Parson of Medburne in Leicestershier

text: I haue alſo (of hyghe & proude harte or mynde) bene diſobediēt and not done due honoure and reuerence vnto my fathers and mothers ſpirituall & carnall, ghoſtly & bodyly, nor vnto myne elders and betters, but haue ben many tymes full obſtynate and frowarde vnto them.

text: And ſo in the ſame maner / (after he had with greate contricion and open cōfeſſion of that ſwerynge) receyued the ſacramentes of the churche / he departed this lyfe vnto our lorde.
author: Whitford, Richard, fl. 1495-1555?
title: A dialoge or co[m]municacion bytwene the curate or ghostly father, the parochiane or ghostly chyld, for a due preparacion vnto howselynge ; The werke for housholders w[ith] the golden pystle and alpha

text: For many that fayne wolde haue and vſe the meditacyon and exercyſe of deth: haue nat the way, ne knowe any fourme or faſſyon therof.
author: Whitford, Richard, fl. 1495-1555?
title: A dialoge or co[m]municacion bytwene the curate or ghostly father, the parochiane or ghostly chyld, for a due preparacion vnto howselynge ; The werke for housholders w[ith] the golden pystle and alpha

text: How moche more than ſhuld it become or byſeme vs that ben frayle perſones: to be dredefull / and euer in fere to offend our lord in the leſt neglygēcy / offence or defaut / and neuer to preſume vpō any good dede: ne yet to deſpeyre for any euyll or ſynfull dede.

text: For prayer (ſaythe he) is nothyng els but a deuociō of mynd / and conuerſion and tournynge of the hart & mynde inwardely, and perfectely vnto god by a deuoute religiouſe and meke affection, cō forted & holden vp (ſayth the ſayd ſaynt Hugh with fayth / hope / and charity.
author: Whitford, Richard, fl. 1495-1555?

author: Whitford, Richard, fl. 1495-1555?

text: My sure beliefe, that God baith may and will saue me in the bloud of Iesus Christ, because he is almightie, and hes promised sa to do.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: TRy your selues, if ye be in the faith, proue your selues: do yee not acknowledge your selues that Christ Iesus is in you, and if not, that year reprobates.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: Therefore hes hell enlarged her selfe, and opened her mouth without al measure, and the stoute, high, and glorious of the people sal discend thereinto.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: If thou hes found in thy hart the loue of God and Christ, and of the things that he loues, and the hatred of the Deuill and his warkes.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: Ouer true, but striuing to mende, and preassing to the best, God will accept thereof, for Christs sake.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: Behald thou hes, in weichtie, wise, discreit And pleasant style, a schort and reddie way.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: And being thus redeemed from the deuill & the seruitude of sin, be my greate and strong Sauiour, to be the free Citiziner, and heir of his kingdome of justice & life.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: That he is verie God and man, Prophete, Priest, and King, conceiued, borne, suffered, to perfite the office of the true and onelie Mediatour and Saviour, for all the elect and faithfull, and for me in speciall.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: I couet to come to thee, wha before hated thee, & followed after Sathan, I cum to thee putting no doubte, but now I sall be acceptable, not hauing my awin righteousnesse, but whilk is through faith of my Lorde Iesus Christ.
author: Melville, James, 1556-1614.
title: A spirituall propine of a pastour to his people

text: Vnder which name of Paſtours, be compriſed Biſhops, Prieſtes, and other like, hauing the cure of Churches.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: For to ſpeake truely, the beginning is not only the halfe of the whole, but it hath beſide that, a reſpect to the end.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: And as touching the domination of many, likewiſe well ruled, that whiche ſhall be made by the voyce, and approbation of many, be it by lotte, or by them bothe ioyned together, as Ariſtotle rehearſeth treating of the election of Magiſtrates.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: For though we reſpect ye Eccleſiaſticall as an actiue, vndoubtedly there is no action ſo excellent, as that which inſtructeth and informeth the interior, which is the principall part of man, where hence all the good or euill of ye exterior procéedeth.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: And that therefore, to beginne with the greateſt, to the meaneſt, it were ſaide to the king, Thou arte king, be attentiue therevnto: And to the Churcheman, Thou art Gods Miniſter, and diſpoſer of his worde: And ſo of other.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: In the whiche Ciuil gouernment ſo framed of the thrée, we will ſay likewiſe, that the moſt perfecte, and beſt eſtabliſhed manner of calling vnto vocations, ſhall be by thoſe thrée wayes alſo aboue ſaide, conioyned together.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: And as for ſpeculations and the contemplatiue life: knowledge and contemplation onely (as we will ſhewe hereafter) is a lame and vnperfecte thing, vnleſſe the ſame be ſo accompanied with the action, vſe, and handling of affaires to the Common profite and ſeruice of men.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: We will adde vnto the Gréeke by vs here alledged, an other Romane example, which is neither leſſe excellent, or leſſe worthie of memorie.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: And it ſufficeth not to ſay, that neceſſitie, and the want of good Preachers moued thée thervnto: for God is the Lorde of the harueſt, (ſaith Ieſus Chriſt,) who will ſende harueſt folke, when it ſhall pleaſe him.
author: La Place, Pierre de, 1520-1572.
title: Politique discourses, treating of the differences and inequalities of vocations, as well publique, as priuate with the scopes or endes wherevnto they are directed. Translated out of French, by Ægremon

text: Thus farre after my accuſtomed maner I haue entreated generallytees, and yet ſuch as my harte is ful of, and where myght I better diſcharge my ſorowe then wyth one, which wyll take parte thereof, I coulde not tell?
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: And ſo euery varlet (abounded in hys owne ſenſe) At the laſte, they concluded vpon theſe Articles, and ſet to their names as ye ſhal ſee in the copie therof.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: Of the whych I receyued ſyxe Copies in printe from you, by M. Mohan, at his laſt comming frō the Court to my Lord pryuey ſeale.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: I thinke they kepe hym ſtyl, becauſe they can not fynde hys match, a Captaine wel choſen by the deuil at the firſt.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: And for the ſame I thanke you, prayng you, yf any ſuche lyke thynges come fourth in printe, I may haue ſome ſent me wyth the fyrſt, & yf you wyll ſpeake to the Kynges Prynter in my name, I dare ſay, he wyll not denye you.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: For with you, the kinges people which deſerued death, be by mercy preſerued, & the thynges euell vſed (as in dede diſceaſes there be in the cōmō wealth) ſhalbe now wel ordered by Parliamēt.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: It was maruell to ſe the newe deuyſes and inuencyons of the pryeſtes and vagabunde Captaynes, for the furtheraunce of theyr firſt purpoſes.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: Theyr boldenes beyng nowe of theyr owne ſtoore, without hope of partakynge, more deſperate then myghtye and leſſe for theyr purpoſe, then for theyr nombre, very many beynge there aſſembled with them, by force againſt theyr wyll, and manye dayle by repentaunce, reacknoweledgīge theyr dutyes and Subieccyon.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: And euery euil mā (I thinke) is ſory: he was no more wretched, & yet no euilnes nor wretchednes, alloweth any mā (yf he wyl not be a ranck traytour) onelye that profeſſion maketh rulers.
author: R. L.
title: A Copye of a letter contayning certayne newes, the articles or requestes of the Deuonshyre Cornyshe rebelles

text: The herbe it ſelf and the ſéede thereof drunken, abate carnall concupiſcence: But if Letuſe be eaten verie often, it hurteth the iye ſight it cauſeth ſlepe.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: The herbe roote & ſéede, hath vertue to heate, it is of like qualities to Smallache, and perſely, and therefore it prouoketh vrine & menſtruis, ſpecially the ſeede of it.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: But alſo it teacheth, to preſerue & kepe the ſame bodie in health, ſo long as the courſe of nature will ſuffer á man to liue.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: By whiche wordes it is euident, that Phiſike is ordained of God, for the profite and commoditie of all mākind, whiche although perchaunce it hath been, and is abuſed, ought neuer the more to bee hated or diſpiſed.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: Theſe humours, maie bee called the ſecond elementes, or the elementes of mā, for thei are equalle with the elementes, and thei haue alſo the qualities of Elementes.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: The herbe being ſoddē in water while it is grene and ſo dronke, is good againſt conuuitions, coughes, hardenes of the ſplene, difficultie in piſſinge, and againſt dropſies in the beginning of thē, it prouoketh vrine and menſtrues, and taketh awaye obſtructions.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: SInce herbes are ſo diuerſly & often vſed of all kinde of people in pottage, brothes, Sallettes, and ſauſes.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: As vndoubtedly not onely Adam and Eue were nouriſhed by herbes & fruites, but alſo great multitudes of people in diuerſe ages, haue béen, and at this preſent be nouriſhed & fedde onely with herbes, rootes, & fruites.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: And by that meanes he maie miniſter amete medicine for it, whereby the ſicke ſhall ſone finde eaſe, and hymſelf great good fame.
author: Moore, Philip, fl. 1564-1573.
title: The hope of health wherin is conteined a goodlie regimente of life: as medicine, good diet and the goodlie vertues of sonderie herbes, doen by Philip Moore.

text: In this bleſſed life all kind of maladies, griefes, ſorrowes and euils, be ſarre away, and all full of all kind of myrth, ioy and pleaſure.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: The puniſhment whereof, although God oftentimes deferreth in this life: yet after the general reſurrection, when our ſoules and bodies ſhall ariſe againe to immortalitie, they ſhall be damned to vnqueachable ſire, and then we, which haue forſaken all mans wiſdome, to cleaue vnto Chriſt, ſhall heare that ioyfull voyce.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: Graunt me alſo that I may humbly reuerence, and faithfully loue mine Huſband, and be obedient to all his honeſt, lawfull, and godly requeſts.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: Although lothſomnes be wont to followe fulneſſe, yet our fulneſſe in the contemplation of thy pleaſures, ſhall bring with it, now kynd at all of lothſomneſſe.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: Therefore, wheſoeuer reſerueth or worſhippeth theſe Sacraments, or contrarywiſe contemneth them in time and place, procureth to himſelfe damnation.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: The Lorde bleſſe vs and ſaue vs: the Lord make his face to ſhine vpon vs: and be mercifull vnto vs: the Lord turne his fauourable countenance towards vs, and grant vs his peace.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: For our conſciences doe accuſe vs, and our ſinnes witneſſe againſt vs, and we know that thou art an vpright Iudge, which doeſt not iuſtifie the ſinnerse & wicked men, but puniſheſt the faults of all ſuch as tranſgreſſe thy commandements.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: Defend me from the counſailes and curſings of euill tongues, let thy mightie arme be my ſhield againſt all the malignitie of the wicked world.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: That it may pleaſe thee to bring into the way of truth, all ſuch as haue erred and are deceiued.
author: R., James (James Rowbotham), attributed name. aut
title: [The perfect pathway to salvation]

text: A heauie caſe deſerues a dolefull place Since bale and bleſſe are aduerſe Complements: And yet the Glowe-worme in the darkeſt night Though blacke it be, ſhines foorth a ſtarry bright.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: Of latter dayes a Bourbon in diſgrace I arm'd againſt his Lieges injurie, And gaue him victorie at Pauia-chace Where he beheld him in captiuitie: What though he were a Traitor in ſo doing, Tis ſtatelie done to ouer-top a King.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: No longer will I wander vp and downe The deſart of Reuenge, and dread Diſpaire, But heer will ſtint me againſt miſ-fortunes frowne A land-man of this ſoyle and happy aire: From hence I will reuine to priſtin bleſſe Or els die heer with Ieſu in diſtreſſe.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: He then out-ſtepping from his ſiluer-cloud Made toward me with a reuerend peacefull pace, And as he march'd euer and anon he bow'd Vnto the Crucifixe was there in place, Whereto at laſt downe humbled, he kiſt it, And gaue it me in hand, and thus inſpeecht it.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: There on the Temple-pinacle ſhe reſted Gracing, and doubling our ſollempne feaſt With her in-heauen; And all the while ſhe atteſted Both with her glee-full countenance and geſt Gods euerlaſting loue vnto the place And eke her owne againſt Dobleſſas race.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: Hold heer (Elizian-man) thy Sauiours image The typick Trophee of thy ſoules redeeme, Be it thy lifes eternall Appennage Thy hearts deere daintie, and thy choice-eſteeme, Inconſcience it within thy in-moſt heſt For In hoc ſigne vinces is expreſt.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: Then gaue he me in hand a Shield of Golde All ouer-grauen with Chriſtes Paſsion, And round about in-amill'd I might behold Death-heads, and latter Reſurrection To heauen or hell: The Croſſe in th'other hand Was all my Spear againſt whatſoere withſtand.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: And laſtly he thus embracingly beſpake me, Welcome (Elizian-man) a thouſand-fold More deere and ſhone to Catechryſius eye Then all the pleaſant pride of Pearle or Gold: Rare, yea all too rare are now adayes Elizas ſubjectes ſeen to paſſe this wayes.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: A Pigeon whiter then the whiteſt Pigion Solie ſubſiſtant of his owne pure Eſſe, His Poſſe was Sanctification, And Graces bounteous liberalitie; What Ieſus erſt had planted with his blood This Pigion gaue it grace-full liuelihood.
author: Copley, Anthony, 1567-1607?
title: A fig for fortune. A.C.

text: Then if we ſin willingly after we haue had the knowledge of ye troth, there remaineth no more ſacrifice for ſinnes: but a fearful looking for iudgement, and violent fire which ſhall deuoure the aduerſaries.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: If it be impoſſible yt they can be conuerted, and the end of our prayers is that ſinners may amend, it ſeemeth ſuperfluous to pray for their conuerſion.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: But the ſame ſpirit which enforced them to craue pardon for the people, prouoked them to aſke vengeance on the rebells and murmurers which withſtood not onely Moſes and Aaron, but the Lord, vnder whom they exerciſed the charge, which they had receiued of him.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: And again: Let their table be a ſnare before them, and let their proſperitie be made their ouerthrowe.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: For I count that the afflictions of this preſēt time are not worthy of the glory whiche ſhalbe ſhewed vnto vs.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: And render vnto our neighours ſeuen folde into their boſom their reproch, wherwith they haue reproched thée O Lord.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: S. Paule ſaith, that he is perſwaded that he that hath begun, a good woork in the Phillippians, wil performe it vntil ye day of Ieſus Chriſt: and addeth that it becōmeth him ſo to iudge of them all.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: And alſo: My little children of whom I trauail in birth again, vntil Chriſt be foūd again in you.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: Alſo: Let them be confounded and put to ſhame togither that ſéek my ſoule to deſtroy it, let them be driuen backward and put to rebuke that deſire mine hurt.
author: Marlorat, Augustin, 1506-1562.
title: A treatise of the sin against the holy ghost made by M. Augustine Marlorate. Translated out of French to the great consolation of all such as repent them of their sinnes, and to the astonying of of [s

text: And alſo of theſe pots they may throwe into the place of the chiefeſt fights of the ſhippes, to amaze the men, and ſo by that meanes they may the eaſilier enter the ſhip. &c.
author: Bourne, William, d. 1583.
title: Inuentions or deuises Very necessary for all generalles and captaines, or leaders of men, as wel be sea as by land: written by William Bourne. An. 1578.

text: And then when that you haue placed the powder in the vaut that is ſufficient for to ſerue your turne, and the more in quantitie, the greater ſhall bee the effect of the raiſing of the thing.

author: Woodes, Nathaniel, fl. 1580.

text: Yea ſurely: all were I deade, it lyeth in you to rayſe me vp againe to life, and that with a light thing.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.

text: For I ſée that ſome parentes are more troubled wyth their childrens euill manners, than with their naturall deathes.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.

text: If mine eyes be witches, how hapneth it then that other alſo do not conſume awaye, whome I looke vpon as ofte as you, therfore I feare me much, yt bewitching is in your owne eyes, not in mine.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: Then ſuffer mee I pray thee to reſt with thy quiet and thankfull iudgement: whereby thou ſhalt vrge me to attempt farther enterpriſe (perchance to thy delight.)
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: No verily not a flie (my ioy) why doubt you? why go you not about your purpoſe?
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: Laſtly that which in friendſhip is the chiefe thing, your maners ſéemeth not the worſte to ſquare vnto my minde and liking, for it maye bee that a thing is ſimply and of it ſelfe right excellent and yet not apt and méete for ſome vſe.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: No ſuch thing, but I haue knowne for the ſpace of certaine yeares the verteous and honeſt behauiour of your parents, that is a birde not leaſt to be regarded (I think) to be come of a good ſtock.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: Verie well, conſider now, conſider I ſaye whither ought thou mayeſt doe to them more pleaſaunt and better lyked, then to let them ſée thée leade this maner of lyfe, ſo ſhamefull and wretched.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A modest meane to mariage, pleasauntly set foorth by that famous clarke Erasmus Roterodamus, and translated into Englishe by N.L. Anno. 1568

text: And firſt beléeue mee this (my Lucres) ſhee that hath ſo many louers, hath no loue at all.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.

text: AND now being ready to close vp, freshe aduises are come by this last post of Paris, of the betraying and apprehension of Maister Campion and others through the filthy treason of one Eliot, who they say after certain other infamous treacheries towardes his best Maisters and frendes, plaied Iudas part herein egregioussy.

text: But if you communicate the case to M. Fox, perhaps he can make something of it, as he hath done of the martyr in Portugal, and of other as stincking stuff as this, cōmēd me to him I pray you as vnacquainted.

text: The more learned (quoth he) the more damnation that you liue not accordingly, but are of ill life as the protestants, and puritans be: & that this booke is gods word & well translated I am warrāted by the spirit.
author: Parsons, Robert, 1546-1610.

text: Quid vultis mihi dare & ego tradam vobis eum, God graunt we heare not shortly that he hange him self after his wages be paied.

text: I promes yow I pray not for him, following the knowen rule of S. Augustine hat we should not pray for such, but rather sesire them to pray for me. tract. 9. in Ioan.
author: Parsons, Robert, 1546-1610.

text: But of the sequel of these things, as of his racking & other durāce, whereof there is already likewise an vncertain rumor, I trust you will aduertise vs from time to time, and so I pray you hartely doe.
author: Parsons, Robert, 1546-1610.

text: Is it not a greater matter, that one should kill him self, then offer him self, to be killed by an other? but that we haue seene the Diuel driue diuers to haue hanged or drowned thē selues.
author: Parsons, Robert, 1546-1610.

text: Bee thou as carefull as thy freend will be conſtaunt, and as faithfull, as ſhe will be firme, and no doubt but good fortune in thyne owne houſe ſhall preſent thee with the greateſt pleaſure thou deſireſt, and ſo till then farewell.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

text: But why is he not liked of with the Religious, becauſe he can not finde in his harte to colour an errour: and wherefore is he diſcommodious to the Lawyer, for that he abridgeth hym of conuenient tyme, to practiſe his corruption.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

text: Frier Fredericke hauing giuen him the Baſeles manes (after the faſhion of our Napolitan Courtiers) aunſwered hym thus.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

text: Truely ſir (aunſwered Simonides) neither will I let ſlippe your proffered courteſie, nor be vnthankfull for your courtlike affabilitie: If therefore it ſhall pleaſe you to accompanie a ſtraunger, to ouerſee the Monumentes of this Citie, I ſhall in this courteſie be greatly beholdyng vnto you.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.
title: The second tome of the trauailes and aduentures of Don Simonides enterlaced with/ varietie of historie, wherein the curteous and not curious reader, maie finde matters so leueled, as maie suffice to p

text: The Euenſong beeyng finiſhed, he was driuen out of his dumpes with the returne of our religious Votiue, who queſtioning with Simonides, how he alowed of the brauerie of Naples, was ſatiſfied with this aunſwere.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.
title: The second tome of the trauailes and aduentures of Don Simonides enterlaced with/ varietie of historie, wherein the curteous and not curious reader, maie finde matters so leueled, as maie suffice to p

text: Theſe breefly are the cauſes of my trauaile, ſomewhat I haue ſeene els where, and now what I looke for here, if by your meanes I might, (good Countrey man) I would gladly accompliſhe.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.
title: The second tome of the trauailes and aduentures of Don Simonides enterlaced with/ varietie of historie, wherein the curteous and not curious reader, maie finde matters so leueled, as maie suffice to p

text: And blinde you maie be if a Louer (ſaied Ladie Fraunces) or els Loue ſtaines in other colours in Spaine then in England.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

text: ALthough I haue no Schoole Rethoricke (Gentlemen) or fine phraſes to make my cauſe more commendable, yet as the naked truth leadeth me, & myne owne experience hath taught me, I will make you priuie to my little ſkill.
author: Rich, Barnabe, 1540?-1617.

text: A noble king durſt Nature race, The guerdon of thy right, To chaunge a king to be an Aſſe: VVhich did appeare ſo bright?
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: After the ende of the buryall of Hellepatrus: Hellvdorus the kinges ſonne, after his dayes of morning were ended, was happely crowned to ſucceede his Imperiall Crowne.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: The King with all the aforeſayd royaltie marched towardes the holy Alſephon: which when the King had taken his place, in the preſence of all the Elders and Commons of the Lande, began to ſpeake after this manner.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: Wherefore this deuiſe was prouided, that all the people, which although they were of two ſeuerall opinions in minde: notwithſtanding, they ſhoulde be gathered all in one, in this holye Alſephon.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: Doo you not ſee, the people, thorowe this lyttle ſtryfe, are readie to holde vp the ſworde one againſt another? vvhiche if this your enterpriſe doo enſue, preſently looke for vtter deſtruction, in short tyme after to followe.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: A Garlande gaie on thistles sharpe, on which your fate shall lye: VVhich shall be greene and nouer warpe, for moiſte or yet for drie.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: After theſe ſore troubles, the Elders of the lande proclaymed a faſte, thorowout the countrey, for the ſpace of twentie dayes.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: But hauinge much diſpleaſure of the Greacians, for that ſo precious a iewell was brought into commen: I could not thinke my ſelfe in any ſaufetye, to returne any more among them.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: And thus he dealt with all of them. one after another, vntyll he had apprehended euerie one of them, when theſe deuiſes were accompliſhed: the king vppon very prudent pollycie, ſent for all the neareſt kindred and friends of theſe murtherers, and talked vnto them after this ſort.
author: Glaucus, James.
title: A knowledge for kings, and a warning for subiects conteyning the moste excellent and worthy history of the Raellyans peruerted state, and gouernment of their common wealth: no lesse rare, then strange

text: As Pleuriſie, the hoaſt and rheume Do ſeeldome make repaire, But couered with the whiteſt flocks Of heauenlie fethers fair, And Souldiers ſweirlie keeping home Into the houſe do hold Of gelded ſonne to aigit yeir, Thair garniſon full cold.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: And in caſe thou finde aſwel in this work, as in my LEPANTO following, many incorrect errours, both in the dytement and orthography, I muſt pray thee to accept this my reaſonable excuſe, which is this.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: With all thy ſpeed from Fame thou canſt not flee, But more thou flees, the more it followes thee.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: For man he is inuaded with A thouſand langors ſore, And euery other liuing thing It gets a proofe no more But of a verie few of euils: The falln-ill onlie aſſailes, The Squadres gatherers of the hoat And the Venerian Quailes.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: IF ALEXANDER ſighed vvhen he came, Vnto the Tomb vvhere fierce ACHILLES lay: If he had cauſe, that bleſſed age to blame, Since HOMER lacks his merites to diſplay.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: No more ſhall now theſe Chriſtians be With Infidels oppreſt, So of my holie hallowed name The force is great and bleſt, Deſiſt ô tempter.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: O ſhall I neuer ſee The Spiders long and threadie feet Full buſie for to weaue, Within the holloweſt of a healme Deckt with a pennage braue?
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: Then though the Antichriſtian ſect Againſt you do conjure, He doth the bodie better loue Then ſhadow be ye ſure: Do ye reſiſt with confidence, That God ſhall be your ſtay And turne it to your comfort, and His glorie now and ay.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: The bloodie fluxis, Peſts, and als The watrie ſwelling great, Are nuriſhed with vs when weake Autumnus brookes his ſeat.
author: James I, King of England, 1566-1625.
title: His Maiesties poeticall exercises at vacant houres

text: This done take it out circumſpectly and diligently, and ſpreade it abrode vpon the Porphire ſtone, and lette it ſo drie thorowly: Then putte it among the paſte for to incorporate it in this maner following.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: TAke an olde Cocke and cut of his combe, and take of the blood that commeth of it and rubbe their gommes with it, & they ſhall neuer feele paine.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: Alſo the decoction or pouder of the floures of a Pomegranate tree, beyng put in your mouth and betwene your gommes faſteneth the teeth.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: Whan it is almoſt ſodden and that it make a gelley, giue it a little of the ſecond or of the third, according as it ſhall haue neede by your Iudgement.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: TAke of the roote of Symphiton petreon, in Engliſh Bugle or Camfrey, and put of it into the bread that he eateth euery daie, and let him eate euery day of the ſaid roote either rawe or roſte, and it ſhal be a very healthfull thing for his diſeaſe.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: Take alſo oile and put into it ſeuen times ſome molten Leade, and then quenche the yron in it at the ende of foure or fiue times.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: Then waſhe what ſpotte you will with it refreſhing it diuers times with colde water and it will take it awaie.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: And whan you haue taken vp a littel, and haue lette it coole and ſo cut it, and than if it be ferme and faſte on the ſides, and in ſetting it vp it tarry vpright, than it is ſodden.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: Menne make the like with Soda, as they do vſe at veniſe, the ſalt muſt be groſſely beaten, and ten pound of it for the hundreth, and mixe it with it all about, and put in but a little at ones.
author: Ruscelli, Girolamo, d. ca. 1565.
title: The seconde part of the Secretes of Master Alexis of Piemont by hym collected out of diuers excellent authours, and newly translated out of Frenche into Englishe, with a generall table, of all the mat

text: In what vice ſoeuer they are takē, be it adulterie, mā ſlaughter, theft. &c. they aunſwere.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
title: A confutation of certaine articles deliuered vnto the Familye of Loue with the exposition of Theophilus, a supposed elder in the sayd Familye vpon the same articles. By William Wilkinson Maister of Ar

text: But the Elder ſinneth not, therefore the young mynded ones ought not to confeſſe vnto thē, for that ſuch confeſſion is mutuall and from either to other, but this place is likewiſe taken from the Romiſh Cleargie.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
title: A confutation of certaine articles deliuered vnto the Familye of Loue with the exposition of Theophilus, a supposed elder in the sayd Familye vpon the same articles. By William Wilkinson Maister of Ar

text: Howbeit yet I ſée not how hereupō HN. would conclud his Reuelation cōcernyng the Reſurrection, for that this place hath not any ſuch meanyng.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
title: A confutation of certaine articles deliuered vnto the Familye of Loue with the exposition of Theophilus, a supposed elder in the sayd Familye vpon the same articles. By William Wilkinson Maister of Ar

text: Whereas the ſpirit of God in the Scriptures doth not onely commend a generall, but alſo commaund a particular knowledge of the miſteries of ſaluation.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
title: A confutation of certaine articles deliuered vnto the Familye of Loue with the exposition of Theophilus, a supposed elder in the sayd Familye vpon the same articles. By William Wilkinson Maister of Ar

text: THerefore it is all (aſſuredly) falſe lyes and ſeducing and deceauing whatſoeuer the vngodded, or vnilluminated man.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
title: A confutation of certaine articles deliuered vnto the Familye of Loue with the exposition of Theophilus, a supposed elder in the sayd Familye vpon the same articles. By William Wilkinson Maister of Ar

text: Who ſoeuer is not Baptiſed accordyng to the forme or maner of Iohn: that is with the water of repentaunce confeſſing their ſinne, he is no Chriſtian.
author: Wilkinson, William, d. 1613.
