text: BAlſaminta is an herbe that men cal horſemynt, this herbe hath leues lyke vnto other myntes, and ſome men calleth it water mynt, it groweth moche by the water, but it hath a ſtrōger ſauer then hath another mynt.
author: Wyer, Robert, fl. 1530-1556, printer.
title: Hereafter foloweth the knowledge, properties, and the vertues of herbes.

text: HErba crucita is an herbe called Croys worte or Exean, this hath lytell leues and a ſmall ſtalke, and alſo a whyte flower.
author: Wyer, Robert, fl. 1530-1556, printer.
title: Hereafter foloweth the knowledge, properties, and the vertues of herbes.

text: Alſo yf thou haue any venym within the, take and pune this herbe and tempre it with Ayſell and drynke it and you ſhall caſt vp all the venym, & it groweth in drye places.
author: Wyer, Robert, fl. 1530-1556, printer.
title: Hereafter foloweth the knowledge, properties, and the vertues of herbes.

text: Not withſtanding the woords of the ſayde Princeſſe, and the promiſes of the Earle of Manſfeeld: Our Regiment and Foncres menne, will not be content without they haue eight Monethes paie altogether, there are but thrée offered vnto them.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: Further, declaring vnto me that ſince the death of the Emperour Maximilian, he was not ſo farre bound to the Emperour that now is, but that it was lawfull for him to accept this ſeruice.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: The report goeth, that theſe were ſolliceted by the Duke of Alanſon, and ouercome by promiſes to attempt the enterpriſe, by the counſell of the Prince of Orenge.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: But the neceſſity that they ſuffer through want of money, ſuffreth not that they can execute their good intencions.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: Howbeit, the twenty of the moneth paſt, I receyued Letters from my Lord the Prince of Parma: whereby he aduertiſed me, that it had pleaſed your Maieſtie, to name me of his Counſell of Eſtate.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: Praying the ſame therfore, to vouchſafe to ground him ſelfe rather vpō a ſmall Campe well payde: then vpon a great one not payde, ſo much ye rather.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: They of Cambray, Tournay, and Bonchaim, continue theyr excurſions vpon theyr neyghbours, deſtroying the Countrey, ſo that euery where is nothing to be ſéen but myſerie and pouertie.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: But for that I deſire principally before all other thinges, to be releaſed and fréeed from this trouble and tediouſneſſe.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: Yea, they will not forget to place amongſt his firſt quarters, and for the fayreſt parte of his Armes, that he hath brought in and maynteyned, the new Religiō, whereof they are ſo deſirous, and farre in loue with all.
author: Fredericke, abbot of Marolles.
title: Newes from Antvverp, the .10. day of August. 1580 Contayning, a speciall view of the present affayres of the lowe countreyes: revuealed and brought to lyght, by sundrie late intercepted letters, of ce

text: William Tooly ſeruingmā was hanged, buried, and then taken vp and burnt, becauſe at his death he praied thus, From the tyrannie of the biſſhop of Rome, requiring the people to ſay wt him, Good Lord deliuer vs.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: For at your handes (onles that ſpedely and vnfaynedly ye repent) ſhal God require all the blood, not onely whiche lately hathe bene ſhed by your moſte wicked permiſsion, but alſo of all thoſe, that for the ſame cauſe haue ſuffred from the beginnyng.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: And be you aſſured that by mainteyning of Idolatrie you ſhal neuer attein to that quietnes, which ye ſeke in this earthe, but contrarywiſe God ſhal plage you, euē by thoſe whome ye ſtudie to pleaſe.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: For the fathers dyd fele in a ſtraunge countrie the heauie yoke of bondage the ſpace of 70. yeres, after that the bodies of many thow ſandes had fallen vpon the edge of the ſworde, and the eies of the children dyd ſee the force and vehemencie of Gods wrathe once kyndled.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: For then be you moſt aſſured, that ye ſhal not eſcape yt irreuocable ſentēce of God, once pronounced by the mouthe of Ieremie in theſe wordes: Euery natiō like vnto this ſhal I iudge ſaithe the eternal.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: Againſt theſe and other vices from tyme to tyme dyd God ſend his prophetes to call them to repentance and did alſo rayſe vp ſome tymes good and godly Kings to make publique reformation as towching the religion.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: It ſhal not proſperouſly ſuccede vnto you, but euē as you haue left ye Lorde, ſo ſhal he leaue you.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: Abſolue and flatter you who ſo liſt, God the father, his ſōne Chriſt Ieſus, his holy angels the creatures ſenſible and inſenſible in heauen and in earth ſhal ariſe in iudgement and ſhal condem you, if in tyme ye repent not.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: Let not the King and his proceadinges (what ſoeuer they be) not agreable to his worde be a ſnare to thy conſcience.
author: Knox, John, ca. 1514-1572.
title: The copie of an epistle sent by Iohn Knox one of the ministers of the Englishe Church at Geneua vnto the inhabitants of Newcastle, Barwike. In the end wherof is added a briefe exhortation to England f

text: For whye complayne they not also of this, that Lot went quitte his way out of Sodome, Abraham out of Calde, the Israelites out of Egypte, Christ frō the Iewes, and Paule from the Pharisees?
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: Paule the fourthe not many monethes since, hadde at Rome in prison certaine Augustine fryers, manye Bysshops, and a greate numbre of other deuout men, for Religion sake, hee racked them and tormented them: to make them confesse, hee lefte no meanes vnassayed.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: But I put case, an Idol be set vp in the Churche of God, and the same desolation which Christe prophecied to comme, stoude openly in the holy place? what yf som theefe or pirat inuade and possesse Noes arke?
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: But say they, ye haue ben once of our felowship, but now ye are become forsakers of your profession, and haue departed from vs. It is trew we haue departed from them, and for so doing we both giue thankes to almightie God, & great lye reioyce on our owne behalfe.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: If we be scismatiques bycause we haue lefte them, by what name shall they be called themselues which haue forsaken the Grekes, frō whom they first receiued their faith, forsaken the primatiue Church, forsaken Christ hymselfe and the Apostls, euen as Children should forsake their parentes?
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: Ebion though he agreed in opinion with ye Samaritanes, yet as saith Epiphanius, he would be called a Christian.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: I saye not, as maye become a Byshopp, but as may become euen a Christian man, Is it so great a mater to haue a vaine title, and by chaunging a garment onely to haue the name of a Byshop?
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: Celsus likewise when he of set purpose wrote against Christ, to thende he might more scornefully scoffe out the Gospel by the name of noueltye, What saith he, hath God after so many ages nowe at last, and so late bethought himselfe?
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: And Origene saith: Christ is the preest; the propitiation and sacrifice, which propitiatiō cōmeth to euerie one by meane of faith.
author: Jewel, John, 1522-1571.
title: An apologie or answere in defence of the Churche of Englande with a briefe and plaine declaration of the true religion professed and vsed in the same.

text: Into this worlde naked we entered And so we must agayne out of it fare Deth By no man can Be defended.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: Nor there is none that can of ryghte thynke hym selfe to be called forthe before his day / cō siderynge that there is no man that hath a day certayne to hym appoynted: but that only is his laufull day / whiche so euer he our souerayne capitayne wolde shulde be his last day.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: No doubt he lyueth / beleue me he lyueth / and perauenture is present with vs / and hereth / and perceiueth this our communication / and laugheth and damneth this our lamētation.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: But nowe if a man wolde consider the matter a ryghte / doth it nat seme a poynt of madnes / wyllyngly of one harme to make twayne / and whan ye can nat by no maner reason recouer your predestinate losse / yet wilfullye to annoye and hurte your owne selfe?
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: But I prey you for the loue of god tell me / what ye call before his day: as though euery day of a mans lyfe coude nat be his laste daye?
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: Fyrst and formost / if it were so / that deth were a thynge moste miserable: yet it behoueth vs to take it in good worth / seinge that ther is none other remedye.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: No doubte we se very often tymes / that the latter age dothe bothe infecte the clene conuersation of yonge age with more greuous vices / and spottethe and defileth the felicitie of youthe / with manyfolde myserable grefes.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: For he is nother ignorant of mortall folkes busines / nor hath nat forgone with the bodye the lowlye reuerence and tender loue / whiche he was wōte to bere to you his father.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: And there is no violence / no space of tyme / nor no distaunce of places / that can seuer or diuide the couplyng of myndes.
author: Erasmus, Desiderius, d. 1536.
title: A treatise perswadynge a man patientlye to suffre the deth of his frende

text: I beſeech you marke aduiſedly that the author of the epiſtle calleth vpon you to goe, and to goe boldely.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Praier is not a common gift, common to all, but a ſpeciall gift, proper onlie to the elect, as faith and repentance.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Some yeares an occupier gaynes a hundred pound by his trade: Hee gaynes not ſo much euery yeare: Therfore he gains nothing.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Again you reade in Saint Lukes Goſpel, the ſeuenteenth chapter and fift verſe, of the holie Apoſtles, whom our Sauiour Chriſt had choſen to preach, and by their preaching to beget faith in others: yet euen theſe men doe in like maner find and feele great want and weakneſſe in their owne faith.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Bind them all and euerie one of them in one bundle, caſt them into the one end of the ballance: when you haue ſo done, take vp the ſinnes of this people, put them into the other ende and weigh them together without ante deceit.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Firſt you feele no profit by the word preſentlie ſo ſoone as you heare it preached: therefore you doe not profit at all.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Againe the Lord himſelfe ſaith, That all the imaginations of the thoughts of mans heart, be euill, onelie euill, and that continuallie.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: What the offer is you heare, and how great it is, your ſelfe is able to iudge: euen ſo large an offer of mercy as none can be greater.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: Perfection is no where to bee found but in heauen, that that we may long to be there, and ſo bee fully perfect.
author: Linaker, Robert, 1550 or 51-1618.
title: [A comfortable treatise for the reliefe of such as are afflicted in conscience]

text: NO sooner loue intirely me possest, But see how iealousie doth me assaile, She seekes with deepe distrust my faith to quaile, And to remoue from conscience quiet guest.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: Stretch forth hād lord, smite thou my hart of stone, With rod of true repentance, griefe and mone.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: The more in view of all thy works I wade, The more I finde my sence confound indeed, But yet insteed of Eccho to thy fame, I will giue thanks and laud vnto thy name.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: I cast my count by Christ, my debt to paie, And frutes of faith from hell my soule shall staie.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: Then is it time my thoughts at length to waine, For laying vp my treasure for my need, Where mothes and canker do so common breed.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: Of force my faults for shame confesse I must, My lauish vsage of thy graces sent: My soules consent to action so vniust, As death of Prophets teaching to repent.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: If in matter they iumpe not to thy passions in all points, thinke among the great Arsenall of Satans armour, he hath choyce of weapons for sundry assaults, and disposeth of them diuersly according to the strength or weaknesse of the partie he besiegeth.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: Thus comfort to the patient alwaies growes, If they attend the time God hath assignde, Our strength to beare, our maker best he knowes, And at a need is readie for to finde.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: Amidst my wandring course by thee am staide, And haue a promise not to die but liue, Thy couenant Lord abundantly is paide, If grace to seed by faith thou doest me giue.
author: Lok, Henry.
title: Sundry Christian passions contained in two hundred sonnets Diuided into two equall parts: the first consisting chiefly of meditations, humiliations, and praiers. The second of comfort, ioy, and thanke

text: That they might oppresse in iudgemente the poore, and might doe violence to the cause of the humble of my people.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: Other also in theyre greate and hyghe solemnities, when the presse & throng of people is moste, vse to lye flatt in the thresholdes of the dores of the Temples, and suffer them selues, to be trampled to death, & are therby accoūted as Sainctes.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: This is the water at which our heauenlye Gedeon, trieth who are fitt soldiers to assist him agaynst the Madianites, and he seuereth such as fall on theire knees for greedines and thirst of worldly vanityes, from those that reach with their hande, so much onlye as their necessity requireth.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: As long as the lyon hath the praye in his pawes, he can dallye and playe with it, but if he see any offer of escaping frō him, he forthwith fixeth his clawes in the fleshe.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: We must not now seeke Christ as our Ladye did inter cognatos & notos, amongest her kinsefolke and acquaintance: nor as the spouse did, that sayed, In lcctulo meo per noctes, quaesiui quem diligit anima mea: In my bed haue I in the nights, sought whom my hart best loued.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: The Priestes or namentes agaynst Pelagius, Purgatorye agaynst the Armenians, Reliques, chastitie of Priestes, voluntarie pouertye, aud prayer for the deade agaynst Vigilantius and Aerius.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: The fearfull and palpable darcknesse, the kylling all the first begotten, both of man & best, and finally the drowning of Pharao, and his innumerable armye in the redd sea.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: They knew that who will keepe the feast in heauen, must first keepe the vigill and the fast here.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: Loue the loue of him, that for the loue of thy loue, descended into the wombe of a Virgine, and afterward ascēded to the ignominy of the Crosse, that there he mighte couple his loue, and thy loue together.
author: Southwell, Robert, Saint, 1561?-1595.
title: An epistle of comfort to the reuerend priestes, to the honorable, worshipful, other of the laye sort restrayned in durance for the Catholicke fayth.

text: ANd ſuynge after on the next night Whyle they ſlepte at her lodgynge place Came an Angell apperynge with greate light And warned hem / that they nouht ne trace By Herodes / but that they ſholde pace Withouten taryenge / in all the haſte they maye To her kyngdome by another waye.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: Certes quod he / I may not voyde oute My fantaſye to aſſent in any wyſe: It ſhulde be lyke / as ye nowe deuyſe.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?

text: Of good and euyll / to haue entendement And for my ſyſter / trouth was abſent And ye your ſelfe / alſo rightwyſnes He was betrayed / ſleyghtly by falſenes.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: ALſo this day of Ioſeph the canele Amyd the felde / that dothe vertue floure Was gadered vp by clennes euery dele Whome all that other / gan worſhippe & honoure For in chaſtite / clene choſen bowre Of may denhede / this canell grewe by kynde That whan the bretherne of Ioſeph dyd bynde.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: ANd whā the Angels / with this heuēly ſonge The byrth of Chriſt / had magnefyed With parfyte gladneſſe / that was hem amonge To heuen anone / agayne they haue hem hyed And the herdes by one accorde a lyed Ben haſtely vnto Bethleem gone Where they founden / whan they came anone.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: TOuchynge this thinge / playnly yf I conne Howe worde by worde / ſothely in ſentence Of this thynge / the rumour is yronne And reported / that thorow necligence Of this Ioſeph: or by vyolence Howe that Marie / goth with chylde greate Wherfore they haue / in a ſodeyn heate.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: O Blynde man / thorowe thyne iniquyte Why haſt thou loſt / thy reaſon & thy ſight That thou of malyce / liſt not for to ſee Howe Chriſt Ieſu / thorowe his greate myght To his diſciples / helde the waye right Thorowe the yates / yſhette by greate deffence Without brekyng / or any vyolence.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: O Thoughtfull herte / plonged in diſtreſſe With ſlōbre of ſlouth / this long wynters night Out of ye ſlepe of mortal heuyneſſe Awake anoue / and loke vpon the lyght Of thylke ſterre / that with her bemys bryght And with the ſhynynge / of his ſtremes merye Is wonte to glade / all our emiſperye.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?
title: This boke is compyled by Dan Iohn Lydgate monke of Burye, at the excitacion [and] styrynge of the noble and victorious prynce, Kynge Henry the fyfthe, i[n] the honoure glorie [and] reuerence of the by

text: O Howe the bawme of heuenly lycoure Of thy ſwetenes / with ſouerayne ſuffeſaūce Lyke Paradyſe / ſhe dyth his vapoure Erly a morowe / auoydinge all greuaunce Lyke the frute / that is of ſuche pleſaunce The garnet appell / of colour golden hewed Thorowe whoſe odoure / the corage is renewed.
author: Lydgate, John, 1370?-1451?

text: When Moiſes had declared gods threatnynges in Egipt, kinge Pharao and hys people were plaged vpon the lād, and drouned in the red ſea.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: This is euen he whom Moiſes, the law, & the prophetes do teache, to be the fully & only ſufficient ſauiour of ye world.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: Yea, and herke all ye that be godlye Rulers: there was much graſſe in the place, god had prouided muche graſſe for theym that loked for no carpets: geuyng all godly gouernours example to prouyde thynges neceſſarye for thoſe people that loketh for no ſuperfluities.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: Thys was the peoples confeſſion of Chryſt, after that they were by ſo great a miracle; ſo plentyfullye fed.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: The lawe, as a tutour, leadeth & bryngeth al men to thys ſauyour, to receyue of hym that perfeccion, which the law it ſelfe lacketh.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: For what could ſeme better counſel then yt a litle ointmēt, the ſwete ſmel of the whyche continued but a while among a few, ſhould haue ben ſould for thre hundreth pence, the greate price of the whyche beſtowed amongeſte manye poore, ſhould haue done them good for a great ſeaſon?
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: But although ye do ſo imagin, yet the people do feel and perceiue that he doeth meane no other thing but pay your duty, pay your dutye.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: Yea, although he be not a labourer, a paſtor or an offycer in dede, but onlye by a pretenced name, vnto whome theſe for the moſt part be paied.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: A great ſin and no les ſhame is it for him that ſayeth he is a Chriſtē mā to ſe Chryſt lack things neceſſary, & to beſtowe vpon the deuil ſuperfluouſli.
author: Lever, Thomas, 1521-1577.
title: A sermon preached ye fourth Su[n]daye in Lente before the Kynges Maiestie. and his honorable Counsell, by Thomas Leauer

text: A man is good ere he do good workes and euel ere he do euel workes / for the tre is good ere he bere good frute / and euel ere it here euel frute.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: This I wryt vnto you that beleue on the name of the son of god that ye may know how that ye haue eternall lyfe Them as because thou hast free me / therfore hast thou beleued / happy are they that haue not sene / and yet haue beleued in me.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: For if we beleue to get the inherytaunce of heuen thorowe good workes, then we beleue not to get it thorow the ꝓmyse of god: if we thynke to get remyssyō of our syn then we beleue not that they are forgeuen vs / and so we counte god a lyar.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: Uvith out grace / it is impossible to kepe any of the commaundementes of god / and grace is not in our power: ergo it is not ī our power to kepe any of the commaundementes of god euen so may you reason cōcerning the holy goste and fayth.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: A good man is knowne by his workes for a good man doth good workes and an euel euel workes / ye shal knowe thē by theyr frute / for a good tre bereth good frute / and an euel tre euel frute.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: Go ye in to all the worlde and p̄ache the gospell vnto euery creature / he that beleueth and is baptysed shalbe saued but he that beleueth not shalbe comdempned.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: For the gospell sayeth / you shal be saued for Christes sake / youre synnes are forgeuē for Christes sake.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: For without faythe it is impossible to kepe any of the commaundemētes of god / and he that hath the fayth kepeth al the commaundementes of god ergo he that kepeth one commaundement of god kepeth them all.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: And we beleue in Iesu Christ / that we may be iustifyed by the fayth of Christ and not by the dedes of the lawe.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: Dyuers frutful gatherynges of scripture and declarynge of fayth and workes of the lawe

text: Neuertheleſſe if thou warn the wicked of his way, to turn from it, if he doo not turn from his way he ſhall dye for his iniquitie, but thou haſt de liuered thy ſoule.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: O how do men reioyce when it pleaſeth the prīce or gouernor of the countrey to cōe vnto them, to giue them good countenance, and to ſpeake cherefully vnto them?
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: It is written of Dauid that with his whole hart he did praiſe the Lord and looued God that made him.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: This heauen, this earth, this ayre, this ſea with all that is therin, bend their force to thy commoditie.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: Beſeeching therfore that by your worſhips well accepting it at my hand (though out of another mans caſke) it may be the better, lyked, accepted and followed, of them that endeuour themſelues to liue in the looue of our onely Sauiour.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: But why do not theſe cormorāts ſay to thēſelues for whom doo I prepare theſe buildings lāds and farmes, with ye loſſe of mine own ſoul.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: Will God think you ſuffer theſe vices long vnpuniſhed? no, let vs thinke therfore that God ſpeaketh vnto vs after this manner and faith.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: Firſt I minde (God permitting) to entreat of that loue which the children of God dutifully owe vnto Jeſus Chriſte, their alone God and Sauiour.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: When I ſhall ſay vnto the wicked, O wicked man thou ſhalt dye ye death if thou dooſt not ſpeak and admoniſh the wicked of his way, that wicked man ſhal dye for his iniquitie, but his blood wil I require at thy hands.
author: D. S., fl. 1584.
title: A godly learned and fruitfull sermon Made vpon the fourteenth of Iohn in which is plainely set foorth the true looue of Christ, the markes whereby the children of God are knovven and the commodities v

text: Of Infans yonge, agone not longe, With calues and pigges which were: The tookens loo, miſhappen ſoo, Whiche cryeth to vs great feare.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: That doth ſtill ſyn, and neuer lyn, As men heapyng vp treaſure: Agaynſt the day, of wrath for aye, Of Gods heauy diſpleaſure.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: Within the raſe, of fyue yeres ſpace Moche monſterous ſights hath byn: Of ſundry kynde, man bare in mynde, And ſone turne from thy ſyn.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: ALl ye that dothe beholde and ſee, this monſtrous ſight ſo ſtraunge, Let it to you a preachyng be, from ſynfull lyfe to chaunge: For in this latter dayes trulye, the Lord ſtraunge ſyghts doth ſhowe, By tokens in the Heauens hye, and on the yearth belowe.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: Loo here you ſee, before your eye, A man childe to beholde: A babe gylties, deformyd this.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: In workyng of her ſkylle: To ſhape a right, eche lyucly wight, Beholde it is Gods wyll.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: Now this late ſyght in Ile of Wight, Straungely it is to tell: Two children borne, neuer beforne.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: The one I fynde, of Woman kynde, Hauyng her ſhape all right: The other is, tranſpoſed this, As pleaſeth the Lorde of myght.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: Nowe praye wee all, bothe great and ſmall, Unto the Lorde of might: To gyue vs grace in Heauen a place, There to attayne his ſight.
author: Barker, John, ballad writer.
title: The true description of a monsterous chylde, borne in the Ile of Wight, in this present yeare of oure Lord God, M. D. LXIIII. the month of October after this forme with a cluster of longe heare about

text: FIrſt whether hipocriſie / fayned relygion called / and wicked lawes called Cacanomia, myght be put out of this Realme without counſell of Auaricia.
title: Questions worthy to be consulted on for the weale publyque

text: Also as longe as a man is withouten wemme or rottynge yf he be wasshed therin it helpeth greatly agaynst achys in the bones pockes / & suche other.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: COmunely it is vsed to take.ii. partes of Fenell & the thyrde parte of Hony & sethe thē togyder tyll they be thycke as a lectuary & let the seke vse therof fyrst and last & he shalbe hole / but gyue hym a purgacyon.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: Also take a poūde of Sall gemme & wynde it in Coll leues & do it in the hote asshes & let it there sethe in it owne kynde tyll it be turned to whytnes.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: Fyrst it destroyeth meselry and dose away all maner of sekenesse of the eyes / ye perle / the skomme of the teres and the quyters / and draweth agayne into theyr owne kynde the eye lyddes that ben blered.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: TAke a hanfull of Percely / & a poūde of Comyn &.v quartes of wyne and sethe all to gether tyll the halfe dele and then gyue hym to drynke that is seke at morne colde and at euen hote & it wyll hell hym.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: TAke Otmell and Mylke of a cowe and put therto the iuse of Syngren and shepes talowe and lette them al boyle to gether tyll it be thyke / & make a playster therof & laye it aboute the sore and that shall sece the akyng and put a waye the swellynge of the same.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: And whan these waters be made yche by hym selfe / putte a droppe of the water to the other water & it wyll be as it were fayre crudded mylke.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: And to hym that is cureable / gyue hym to drynke.iii. dayes Pympernell Bugle & Sanycle to purge the wounde.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: This water of lyfe draweth out the swetenesse & sauour of all maner of spyces and of all rotes that ben therin netted or layde.
title: Here begynneth a newe boke of medecynes intytulyd or callyd the Treasure of pore men whiche sheweth many dyuerse good medecines for dyuerse certayn dysseases as in the table of this present boke more

text: The ſacraments alſo, like as the word, are an inſtrument, or exerciſe to ſtirre vp and maintaine faith and godlyneſſe in vs. They are alſo a publike profeſſion of our faith and thankfulneſſe vnto God, and a part of the publike worſhip of God in the church.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: Againſt the teaching of doctrine is ſet the leauing or forſlowing of the duetie of teaching, either priuatelie or publiklie.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: Verie earlie the firſt daie of the Sabboths, that is, of the wéeke, they came vnto the Sepulchre.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: So the Lord hath ordeined, that they which preach the Goſpell, ſhould liue of the Goſpell. 1.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: From the daie in which ye offer a Gomer of lifting vp, there ſhall be ſeuen full weekes, Math. 28.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: For ſo all the figures of the olde lawe are euerlaſting, yea, & the kingdome of Dauid it ſelfe, the which notwithſtanding was to be deſtroied before the comming of the Meſſias.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: And again, there are two parts of the cōmandement, of the which the one is morall or euerlaſting, namelie, that the Sabboth be hallowed, that is to ſaie, that ſome certaine time be appointed for the miniſterie of the Church, or publike worſhippe of God.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: Euerie firſt daye of the weeke, let euerie one of you laye a ſide with himſelfe, laying vp that, which thorough the gentleneſſe of GOD he maye.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.
title: A verie profitable and necessarie discourse concerning the obseruation and keeping of the Sabboth day seruing as well to confute the superstition of the Iewes, which obstinately vrge the strict keepin

text: God himſelfe alſo doth witneſſe Deut. 5. that he will haue the Sabboth kept, that reſt maye be giuen to ſeruaunts and to our familie: leaſt that with the continuaunce of laboures they ſhould be too much brought downe.
author: Ursinus, Zacharias, 1534-1583.

text: DO not dispyse Thys myne Aduyse / Yee that bee wyse / And lust for to eate than, Of the lyuinge Wood / Or heauenlye Food / So pure and good / In the Supper of the Lamb / For Hee is now blest. &c.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: NEGLECT Mee not / As they dyd Lot Longe past / yee wot / And perryshed all than: My Loue pervse / Make no excuse / Lest yee refuse The Supper of the Lamb.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: For Hee is now blest / / in verye deede / That's found a Gest / / in ye Mariage-weede.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: MAKE haste and speede / I am indeede That Maryage-weede, That Those must putt-on, than / Which shall bee fitt / Or-els permitt Downe for to sitt / At the Supper of the Lamb.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: THEN must I go To the Hye-wayes, so / And Hedges, tho / And seeke them-vp all than: All Those by name That's Blynde or Lame / And compell thesame, To the Supper of the Lamb.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: THEN runne apace / Whylst there is Grace / Or Tyme and space / So fast as euer yee can / To Syons Hyll: Wheare All that wyll May eate their fyll / In the Supper of the Lamb.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: FOR that all Kynges / Vnder Loues Wynges (Without Grudgynges) In Peace mought gouerne, than / Praye All: that trust Amonge the Iust / Or haue a Lust To the Supper of the Lamb.
author: W. S., veritatis amator.
title: A new balade or songe, of the Lambes feast Another, out of goodwill.

text: Al those things which be mine I take with me: inferring therby, that vertue is the onlye ornament and possession of a wise man: all other things being but snarles to intangle honestie, and to cast vs head-long inso much miserie.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: With mindes inflamde, alwayes to domage of your selues, What profite ist? so many countryes to subdue, And nations diuers tributaries make vnknown, And after enterprices perillous and vaine, With blood to conquer walled Townes, and treasure get?
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: I forget not how vnpleasant this later councell séemeth to them, who haue with so much blood mainteyned their liberties: yet would I haue them estéeme that sweete, which gaineth their safety, ye either is by the two former means obteyned, or purchased by alteration of times, or surely established by nothing.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: How vnprofitable mouldes the world and nature are to cast the forme of a godly perfection, he hath drawne with quicke coullors in the person of the ritch man, who is not by ye sacred rule made perfite, vnlesse he sell all that he hath, and giueth the same to them that haue nothing.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: Our soueraign gouernes, applieth the easiest remedies of godly surgerie, for preseruation of the whole bodye: but in this, they be no otherwise deceiued, then in those actions which be squared with the rule of error.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: To this are the testimonies of the scriptures answerable: which witnes the bountious liberality of God, to the needy, naked, miserable, and possessors of nothing, and his indignation to the mighty, and rich, whom he pulleth from their seates, and sendeth emptie from his presence.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: The consideration hereof, ministred Heraclitus large floodes of teares, and clowdes of sighes, as vnfained witnesses of his continuall mourning, for those miseries wyth which he beheld our liues filled and made lamentable.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: The charitable looking vpon the torne leaues and poore afflicted members of Christ, greatly profiteth no doubt the dulnes of our bodily sight: which being séene and not relieued, argueth vs of incrudelitie towards the head, whose parts they are.
author: Dyer, Edward, Sir, 1543-1607, attributed name.
title: The prayse of nothing. By E. D.

text: Compaire the ioyes and sorrowes, which grow of corruptable things, & there wil be sufficient reason minstred, to confirme this argument.

text: And therefore wee muſt looke that that which hath been maturely deliberated and thought vpon, be ſpeedily put in execution: and let vs not accuſtome our ſelues to poſt that ouer to the morrow, which may be as well done the ſame day.

text: For if it be a true good which hath happened vnto him, we ſhould rather reioyce and bee glad with him for it: for euery mā ſhould deſire the good one of an other; and to reioyce at the good of another is the way to encreaſe a mans owne.

text: For as a ſober grauitie maketh a man to be reuerenced of all: ſo a kinde of portlike and conſtrained auſteritie, makes him to appeare ridiculous and odious vnto all.

text: The vſe of words whē occaſion bids vs ſpeake, ought to bee this: to ayde the trueth, and to carrie the candle before her that ſhe may be ſeene: & contrariwiſe to diſcouer and reiect lyes and vntruth: to praiſe that which is good, and blame that which is otherwiſe.

text: Thē examine whether that which he ſaith be true, either in whole or in part, and correct that fault in your ſelfe, leaſt happily another man take occaſion to ſpeake as much, or more of you.

text: Enuie ſtirreth vp within vs a kind of ſorrow at the good which other men enioy, which ſtill lieth gnawing at our hearts, and tormenteth vs moſt cruelly.

author: Gurney, Arthur.

text: If Fortune, fie on her harlot, that would be ſo freendly vnto you, who neuer did her good, and ſo froward to the reſt, that neuer wiſht her harme.

text: WHo markes the ſteps of this vnſtayed ſtate, And ſées the ſeas which ſink vs in our ſin, And wiſeli weies our wicked wādring gate, And floudes of filth that we lye frozen in, Maye mourne with me, our caſes are akinne.

text: And for theeues and murtherers and adulterers and falſe ſwearers and Idolaters, to come into the houſe of God, either to pray or to offer ſacrifice, without a conſtant intent to amende their ill waies, is to make the houſe of God or the houſe of prayer, a den of theeues.
author: Howson, John, 1557?-1632.

text: And though the Church of England hath no ſuch conſtitution, yet the people entertaine the practiſe of it, many of them condemning common prayer, but a greater part neglecting them, and holding it the only exerciſe of the ſeruice of God to heare a Sermon.
author: Howson, John, 1557?-1632.
title: A second sermon, preached at Paules Crosse, the 21. of May, 1598. vpon the 21. of Math. the 12. and 13. verses concluding a former sermon preached the 4. of December 1597. vpon the same text. By Iohn

text: I complaine not that our Churches are auditories, but that they are not oratories: not that you come to Sermons, but that you refuſe or neglect common prayer; not that you reſort ad porticum Solomonis, to Paules croſſe, but that your pariſh churches are naked and emptie.
author: Howson, John, 1557?-1632.
title: A second sermon, preached at Paules Crosse, the 21. of May, 1598. vpon the 21. of Math. the 12. and 13. verses concluding a former sermon preached the 4. of December 1597. vpon the same text. By Iohn

title: The displaying of the Protestantes, [and] sondry their practises, with a description of diuers their abuses of late frequented Newly imprinted agayne, and augmented, with a table in the ende, of all s

text: A very apt worde, and mete for ſuche, who in very dede were al togethers Proteſtantes, That is to ſaye diſſwaders of holſome lawes whiche touched the reformacion of mannes nature, and reformers of ſuche good orders as were conſtituted for the bridlinge thereof.
author: Huggarde, Miles.
title: The displaying of the Protestantes, [and] sondry their practises, with a description of diuers their abuses of late frequented Newly imprinted agayne, and augmented, with a table in the ende, of all s

text: In lyke maner whyle ſome were in debating the abbaie poſſeſſiōs, and ſtakinge the ſame oute to the kinges vſe, ſome remained in the middes, mete for their owne vſes.
author: Huggarde, Miles.
title: The displaying of the Protestantes, [and] sondry their practises, with a description of diuers their abuses of late frequented Newly imprinted agayne, and augmented, with a table in the ende, of all s

text: Another ſecte there is whiche denye all the forſayd opinions, & affirme that when Chriſte ſayde, this is my body: He ment onelye that the bread was his bodye.
author: Huggarde, Miles.
title: The displaying of the Protestantes, [and] sondry their practises, with a description of diuers their abuses of late frequented Newly imprinted agayne, and augmented, with a table in the ende, of all s

text: Then the lorde of the harueſt ſhall deuide thē, & ſhall put the good corne in to his barne, and caſt the cockle into the fyre.
author: Huggarde, Miles.

text: What brought Northumberlande to his deſerued ende, in going about to diſplace ye Quenes maieſtie of her iuſt tytle, but treaſon and hereſie, the inſtrumentes of his deuiliſhe attemptes?
author: Huggarde, Miles.
title: The displaying of the Protestantes, [and] sondry their practises, with a description of diuers their abuses of late frequented Newly imprinted agayne, and augmented, with a table in the ende, of all s

text: Wherein, it pleaſed the holy Ghoſt to ſerue himſelfe by them, for confuſion of the Pagane incredulity, and to giue theſe deuoute women, as theyr Iudges, being faithfull Trumpets of the comming of Chriſt Ieſus, as alſo of his death and reſurrection.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: As for my ſelfe, I neuer heard or knew, that any woman voluntarily gaue her ſelfe to a man, without his traynes and craftie ſollicitings vſed before.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: Virgill, and (before him) Appolonius and Cteſias, depainted to vs Polimneſtor of Thrace, a man ſo carried away with auarice, as he violated al the rights of hoſpitality, and wickedly murdered Polidore, ſon to King Priam his neighbour.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: THis teſtimonie of my true hearts zeale, Faire, and (for euer honord) vertuous maide: To your kinde fauour humbly dooth appeale, That in conſtruction nothing be miſ-ſaide.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: So that ſhe is no way to bee diſſolued, but may well chaunge into a forme more conuenable, and agreeing with the quality of her Demon.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: See to what kindes of excellencie, the mindes of men are dayly addicted, and yet they will be Lordes and controullers ouer women, when baſeſt infamie dooth thus commaund ouer themſelues.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: In lyke manner, your high and ſoueraigne Courtes, are nothing elſe but filled with mens continuall tumults, whence enſue iniurious offences to theyr betters: and that in matters of ſo meane reckoning, as womens modeſtie are aſhamed thereof, and theyr height of ſpirit holdes it in moſt deepe diſdaine.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: Nature on Bulles did hornes beſtow, And tallents to the Birdes ſhe gaue, Hoofes to the horſe, and well we know Swiftnes to Hares their liues to ſaue.
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: There browne and faire are both as one, When two ſweet ſoules are ſo alone: Tell me then (Loue) in ſuch a night, Wouldſt thou not thinke the browneſt white?
author: Pontaymeri, Alexandre de, d. 1618.
title: A vvomans vvoorth, defended against all the men in the world Proouing them to be more perfect, excellent, and absolute in all vertuous actions, then any man of what qualitie soeuer. Written by one tha

text: THe Iuell of our ioye is gone, the happie heauens haue wonne, The greatest gift that euer was, with vs beneth the sonne: Which makes such weepinge eyes, in Sallesbury they saye, As all the ronning streames therof, can neuer washe awaye.
author: Elderton, William, d. 1592?
title: An epytaphe vppon the death of the right reuerend and learned father in God I. Iuell, doctor of diuinitie and bishop of Sarisburie, whom God called to his marcie the 22. of September. 1571.

text: That wee haue such a Shepard gone: God helpe the selie sheepe: Meethinkes I see in heauen, triumphant truth appeare, And faythfulnes, which speake alowde let Iuell nowe come neare.
author: Elderton, William, d. 1592?
title: An epytaphe vppon the death of the right reuerend and learned father in God I. Iuell, doctor of diuinitie and bishop of Sarisburie, whom God called to his marcie the 22. of September. 1571.

text: And Abraham rendes his clothes, and bowells out his brest, And sayth to Iuell iumpe in here, and take thye quiet rest.
author: Elderton, William, d. 1592?
title: An epytaphe vppon the death of the right reuerend and learned father in God I. Iuell, doctor of diuinitie and bishop of Sarisburie, whom God called to his marcie the 22. of September. 1571.

text: Thappostelles all do prease, meethinckes to see his face: And all the Angells go about to bring him to his place: Euen Christ him selfe mee thinkes, I see begins to smile, And saith: beholde my chosen frend, I lookte for all this while.
author: Elderton, William, d. 1592?
title: An epytaphe vppon the death of the right reuerend and learned father in God I. Iuell, doctor of diuinitie and bishop of Sarisburie, whom God called to his marcie the 22. of September. 1571.

text: Whether the laſt Churchwardens were enioyned to haue repaired anye parte of the Church, or fenced the Churchyarde, and did neglect to doe the ſame.

text: And whether being not reſident, they leaue their cures to an vnlearned or lewde perſō, or do not diſtribute yerely among their pore pariſhioners, the fourteth parte of the fruites of their benefices, the ſame being of the yearely value of twentie poundes or aboue.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: Whether in any Church or Chappell, if ſinging be there vſed, ſuch partes onely of the Common prayer be ſong, as by the Booke of Common prayer are appoynted to be ſong, and the reſt reuerently ſayde and read with an audible voyce.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: And whether there be any ringing on Sundayes or Holidaies betwéene Morning prayer and the Letany, or at other times contrarie to good order or lawe.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: And whether they reade the Quéenes Maieſties Iniunctions, euery quarter of a yere once, or no. And whether they praye for the proſperous eſtate of hir Maieſtie, as is preſcribed in the ſayde Iniunctions, or no.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: And whether in any fayres or common markets falling vppon the Sunday there be anye ſhewing of any wares before the morning prayer be done.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)

text: And whether on all Saintes day after Euening prayer, there be anye more ringing in your Church or Chappell, or other ſuperſticious ceremonies vſed, tending to the maintenaunce of the Popiſh Purgatorie, or praying for the deade, and who they be that vſe or doe the ſame.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: And whether he marry any perſons, which were ſingle before, that cannot ſay the Cathechiſme, or contentes thereof.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)
title: Articles to be enquired of in the visitation of the Dioces of London, by the reuerende father in God, Edwyn Bishop of London In the thirtenth yeare of the raigne of our soueraigne ladie Elizabeth, by

text: And if any doe wilfully and ſtubburnly refuſe to come to ſuch recitall or examination, whether the Churchwardens and ſworne men, or anye of them doe aſſiſt the Miniſter therein, that ſuch ſtubburne perſons may be rebuked and repelled from the communion at that time.
author: Church of England. Diocese of London. Bishop (1570-1577 : Sandys)

text: Item whither there haue bene or be anye legacies or gyftes made for the repayrynge and mayntenaunce of your church, or of high waies, finding of the poore, maryenge of poore Maydens, or anye ſuche like, and the ſame not payde and aunſwered accordingly.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: Item whither any woman by them ſelues or by the ſmiſtre counſell of other, haue after their own fantaſies purified them ſelues or done any thing therein contrary to the law, ordenaunce, and cuſtome of the catholike church.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: Item whither the churche of your pariſhe be nowe vacante or no, who is the patrone therof, how long it hath bene vacant, who doth receiue the tythes, oblations, and other commodities thereof, during the ſayd vacation, and by what authoritie, and in what eſtate the ſayde churche as in.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: Item whether there be within the ſayde pariſhe any, that at the ſacring time of the Maſſe dothe hange downe theyr heades, or hyde them ſelues behinde pillers, or turneth away their faces, or departeth out of the church, becauſe they woulde not looke vpon the bleſſed ſacrament of the Aultare.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: Item whither any do depraue or contempne the auctoritie or iuriſdiction of the Popes holynes, or the ſea of Rome, or do let the proceſſe of anye Archbyſhoppe or Byſhoppe, or of anye of theyr deputies.
author: Church of England.

text: Item whither anye dothe take vpon hym to miniſtre the goodes of any that is deade before the Teſtament be proued, or adminiſtration to him by thordinary dulye committed, or doth let the Teſtament or laſt wyll in anye wyſe to be fulfilled.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: Item whither there be within the ſayde pariſh any priuie lectures or ſermons, or other deuiſes, or anye vnlawfull conuenticles or aſſembles.

author: Church of England.
