text: Item whither anye Minſtrels or anye other perſons do vſe to ſyng or ſay any ſonges or dities that be vncleane or vile, eſpeciallye againſt any of the.vii.
author: Church of England.
title: [Interrogatories vpon which ... churchwardens shalbe charged, for searche, of al such things as now be amysse.]

text: As touchinge their diſcourſe concerning this matter ſent by the ſaid Ladye vnto the Court of Parliament: It is moſt certeine that Monſeur de Guiſe cauſed her to putte her hande therunto.
title: The Verye trueth of the conference betvvixt the queene mother, and the prince of Conde, Iulye, 1562

text: For mauntenaūce wherof he had put him ſelf in Armure agaynſt the ſaid Guyſe, who by their priuate aucthoritie with violence had broken the ſame, as the greate number of murthers and manſlaughters by them committed dyd teſtifye.
title: The Verye trueth of the conference betvvixt the queene mother, and the prince of Conde, Iulye, 1562

text: And whereas they couered thē ſelues with thaucthoritie of the Kynge Queene and Courte of Parliamente, it was apparent inough to al the world, that thei ruled the ſame by force euen as they luſted.
title: The Verye trueth of the conference betvvixt the queene mother, and the prince of Conde, Iulye, 1562

text: All theſe thynges aboue written at true, wherof it foloweth that the ſayd Prince with hys adherentes are falſely eſtemed and called rebelles and ſeditious perſons, and that the name of rebellion, ſedition and diſobedience apperteyneth truly & properly to his aduerſaries.
title: The Verye trueth of the conference betvvixt the queene mother, and the prince of Conde, Iulye, 1562

text: And whereas ſith it was imprinted by Uaſcoſan, the ſale therof was prohibited, leſt the lyes wherewith it ſwarmeth ſhould be diſcouered and knowē.
title: The Verye trueth of the conference betvvixt the queene mother, and the prince of Conde, Iulye, 1562

text: The lorde anſwered and ſaid A ſeake man and ſore wounded hadde nede to haue a ſure leche and a trewe / knowing his cure / and therfore a man ſholde principally be ſhreuen to god / and els his confeſſion is noucht.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: And one of the biſhopes clerkes ſaid thā there / that he herde Nicoll Herforde ſay / that ſyns he forſoke and reuoked all the learning and Lolardes opiniōs / he hathe had mekell greater fauour and more delyte to holde ageinſt them / thā euer he hadde to holde with them while he helde with them.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: And whan he came to anſwer he gaue that one parte to the biſſhope / ād that other parte he kept to hymſelf.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: And whan I came in ageyne before the Archebiſſhop / a clerke badde me knele downe and aſke grace / and ſubmit me lowly / and I ſholde fynde it for the beſte.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: And I beleue that Chriſte our ſauyour was circunciſyd in the eyghte daye after hys byrthe in fulfillyng of ye lawe / and hys name was callyd Ieſu whych was callyd of ye angell before yt he was cōceiuyd in ye wōbe of Marie hys moder.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: For thy venemous doctryne is ſo knowen thorow out Englōd / yt no biſhop will admitt the for to preache by witneſſyng of their letters.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: The.ij. thing that moueth me to write this ſentence is thys / diuerſe frendes which haue herde that I haue ben examined before ye Archebiſſhop / haue comen to me in priſon and councelled me beſely / and coueted greatly that I ſhulde do the ſame thynge.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: He went downe to helles: the thirde daye he roſe ageyn fro dethe: he aſcended vp in to heuenis he ſitteth on the righte hande of god the father almightie: fro thence he is to come to iudge the quicke & dede.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: For thorow Chriſte Ieſu meane or middill perſone of the trinite / the father of heuen is pituous or mercifully ioynyd and made one to gither to mankynde.
author: Thorpe, William, d. 1407?
title: The examinacion of Master William Thorpe preste accused of heresye before Thomas Arundell, Archebishop of Ca[n]terbury, the yere of ower Lord .MCCCC. and seuen. The examinacion of the honorable knight

text: It maketh a man ferme / and ſtable in vertuous life & to ſeme vyle and deſpecte or vn worthy in his owne ſight.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: It is thou only that perfectly mayeſte helpe me for thou knoweſte what vnto me neceſſarye: and of what goodes aboue all other I haue mooſtenede.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: Gyue hede in any wiſe that thou auoide thoſe vyces in thyſelfe that thou arte moſte greued or myſcontent within other mē: and be glade to gether vertue of euery vertuoꝰ creature as the hony Be gadrethe hys hony of diuers floures ſo conſider all thoſe that thou arte cōuerſāt with.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: Speke thou to vs & we ſhall here the gladly: let nat our lorde ſpeke to vs lyſte we dye for drede.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: Tho that be roted & ꝑfitly fixed in the drede & loue of god: may nat of no wiſe be obſtynate or proude.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: The fame of ſotell phyloſophers the knowlege of poetes & reforike as aſmoke or fume vaniſſheth awey: but the truthe of god abydeth withoute ende.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: For perſyte loue hath ſure paſſage to owre lorde. who ſomeuer hath delyte to offende it is no meruayle if they drede dethe / and theyr Iugement.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.
title: A full deuoute and gostely treatyse of the imytacyon and folowynge the blessed lyfe of our moste mercyfull Sauyour cryste compyled in Laten by the right worshypful Doctor Mayster Iohn Gerson: and tran

text: Verely we deceyue our ſelfe by inordynat loue that we haue to owre ſelfe. what ſhall the fyre come to deuoure but thy ſīne.
author: Atkinson, William, d. 1509.

text: Then those Knights that a farre off with dolorous viewing, Cast their eyes hetherward: loe in an agonie All vnbrac'd, crie aloud, their heauie state ruing; Moyst cheekes with blubbering painted as Ebonie Blacke, their feltred haire torne with wrathfull hand, And whiles astonied, starke in a maze they stand.

text: Nor if I would could I iust title make That anie laud thereof to me should growe Without my Payns from others wings I take; For nothing from my wit or will doth flowe: Since all my wordes thy beautie doth indite, And Loue doth hold my hand, & makes me write.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: Syr P.S. His Astrophel and Stella Wherein the excellence of sweete poesie is concluded. To the end of which are added, sundry other rare sonnets of diuers noble men and gentlemen.

text: For I protest, mine eyes neuer thy sight enioyeth, But Im mee am chang'd, I am aliue and dead.

text: Let Venus haue the graces hir resignd, And thy sweete voyce yeeld to Hermonius spheares: But yet restore thy fierce and cruell minde To Hircan Tygers, and to ruthlesse Beares; Yeeld to the Marble thy hard heart againe: So shalt thou cease to plague, and I to paine.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: Syr P.S. His Astrophel and Stella Wherein the excellence of sweete poesie is concluded. To the end of which are added, sundry other rare sonnets of diuers noble men and gentlemen.

text: VVell Loue, since this Demurre our sute doth staie, Let Vertue haue that Stellas selfe, yet thus, That Vertue but that body graunt to vs.

text: VVhat plague is greater than the griefe of minde, The griefe of minde that eates in euerie vaine, In euerie vaine that leaues such clods behind Such clods behind as breed such bitter paine, So bitter paine that none shall euer finde, What plague is greater than the griefe of minde.
author: Sidney, Philip, Sir, 1554-1586.
title: Syr P.S. His Astrophel and Stella Wherein the excellence of sweete poesie is concluded. To the end of which are added, sundry other rare sonnets of diuers noble men and gentlemen.

text: And yet my starre, because a sugred kisse, In sport I sucke, while she a sleepe doth lye: Doth lowre, naye chide, nay threat for onely this: Sweet it was saucy loue, that prest so nye.

text: For whilst they striue which shall be Lord of all, All my poore life by them is trodden downe; They all erect their triumphs on my fall, And yeelds me nought: who gaines them there renowne.

text: Teach vs by thy holye ſpirte, that we maye rightly weigh them, and earneſtly repent for the ſame.

text: And furthermore, that the affliction and combat of this thy pore creature in moſte greeuous tormentes, maye moue vs to humble our ſelues with all reuerent feare and trembling vnder thy mighty hande, knowing that we muſte appear before thy iugement ſeat, when it ſhal pleaſe thee to appoint.

text: We praye thee alſo (good lord) that we may haue the feeling of the miſeries of our brerhren, as members of the ſame body, & thoſe that liue by the ſame ſpirite.

text: The Lorde bleſſe vs and ſaue vs, the Lorde make his face to ſhine vpon vs, and be mercifull vnto vs: the Lord tourne his fauourable countenaunce vnto vs, and grant vs his peace.

text: Furthermore that our ſleep be not exceſſiue or ouer much after the vnſatiable deſires of the fleſhe, but only ſufficiēt to cō tent oure weake nature, that we may be the better diſpoſed in all godly cōuerſation, to the glory of thy holy name, & profite of our brethren.

text: Make vs, O Lorde our God, to feele this ſame in our ſoules and conſciences, that IESVS CHRIST is ours, and all that hee hath done: that we are graffed into his body, and made one with him, and therfore fellow heires with him of euerlaſting life.

text: In whole name for theſe mercies and what ſoeuer thou knoweſt to be needefull for vs, and for the whole Church, we pray vnto thee, as he him ſelfe hath taught vs in his holye worde, ſaying: Our father. &c.

text: Than aroſe Nychodemus vp and thus he ſayde to them / ye haue herde what theſe thre men haue ſayd & ſworne vpon the lawe that they ſawe Ieſu ſytte and ſpeke to his dyſcyples vpon the mount of olyuete / and there he ſtyed vp to heuen.
title: Cayphas and asked them what was prosylyte. And

text: Oure lorde anſwered to hȳ my kyngdome is not in this worlde / for yf my kyngedome were in this worlde my mynyſters wold not be ayenſt me / nor I ſholde not haue be delyuered to the but my kyngedome is not now here.
title: Cayphas and asked them what was prosylyte. And

text: And for as moche as Ieſus ſayth that he ſhall ſyt in heuen vpon the ryght ſyde of ye deuyne mageſte / and that he ſhall come frome heuen in to ye ſkyes / for this ſclannder we wyll that he be crucyfyed.
title: Cayphas and asked them what was prosylyte. And

text: ANd as they were ī this are ruaylyng they and ne entred in to theyr ſynagoge / & amonge thē there came one of the knyghres yt kepte the ſepulcre & to them he tolde ryght ſykerly yt our lord Ieſu was not in ye monument.
title: Cayphas and asked them what was prosylyte. And

text: And they ſayd that proſelyty was paynyms chyldren / and ſo be his dyſcyples / & for that they ſay that he is borne in fornycacyon.

text: All the Gentlemen pertaining to that Cardinal attending on them, thus going al in order towards the Conclaue dreſſer, they méete firſt at the firſt doore the Conſeruours, Senatours, or ſherifs gard, then comming to the ſtayers foote, they méete the other garde of Italians and Swizers.
author: Florio, John, 1553?-1625.
title: A letter lately written from Rome, by an Italian gentleman, to a freende of his in Lyons in Fraunce Wherein is declared, the state of Rome: the suddaine death sollemne buriall of Pope Gregory the thir

text: Al other Cardinals haue their chambers, & other implementes hanged, and couered with gréene, The order how they are ſerued in the Conclaue, ſo long as the election laſteth is this.
author: Florio, John, 1553?-1625.
title: A letter lately written from Rome, by an Italian gentleman, to a freende of his in Lyons in Fraunce Wherein is declared, the state of Rome: the suddaine death sollemne buriall of Pope Gregory the thir

text: No Cardinal can bring in more then thrée men, that is to ſay, a Secretarie, a Gentleman, and a Chamberlaine, who ſo long as the election laſteth can not by any meanes come out.
author: Florio, John, 1553?-1625.
title: A letter lately written from Rome, by an Italian gentleman, to a freende of his in Lyons in Fraunce Wherein is declared, the state of Rome: the suddaine death sollemne buriall of Pope Gregory the thir

text: A little while agoe there were taken out of the Caſtle great ſummes of mony for the vſe of the Sea vacante, which now are reſigned againe.
author: Florio, John, 1553?-1625.
title: A letter lately written from Rome, by an Italian gentleman, to a freende of his in Lyons in Fraunce Wherein is declared, the state of Rome: the suddaine death sollemne buriall of Pope Gregory the thir

text: There went to méete him out of the Gates, theſe men folowing: the Duke of Sora his Nephewe, the Cardinalles San ſiſto hys ſonne, and Vaſta villani his Nephewe, with certain others, who conducted him to Cardinall San ſiſto his houſe.
author: Florio, John, 1553?-1625.

text: But of all other that euer liued, none was comparable vnto this helhound, whose tiranny and cruelty did well declare he was of his Father the deuill, who was a murderer from the beginning, whose life and death and most bloody practises the discourse following dooth make iust reporte.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: And héere is to be noted a most strange thing which setteth foorth the great power and mercifull prouidence of God to ye comfort of eache Christian hart.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: Ouer that on the top of the stake the sorcerers head it selfe was set vp, and round about the Wheele there hung as it were sixtéen peeces of wood about a parde in length which represented the sixteene persons that was perfectly knowen to be murdered by him.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: For the Deuil hauing brought the wretch to al the shame he could, left him to indure the torments which his deedes deserued.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: Likewise in the townes of Germany aforesaid continuall praier was vsed vnto god that it would please him to deliuer thē from the danger of this gréedy Woolfe.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: Moreouer he vsed many times to kill Lambes and Kiddes and such like beastes, feeding on the same most vsually raw and bloody, as if he had béene a naturall Woolfe indeed, so that all men mistrusted nothing lesse then this his diuelish Sorcerie.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: Also his Daughter and his Gossip were iudged to be burned quicke to Ashes, the same time and day with the carkasse of the aforesaid Stubbe Peeter, And on the 31. of the same moneth, they suffered death accordingly in the town of Bedbur in the presence of many péeres & princes of Germany.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: And the same ordained to stand there for a continuall monument to all insuing ages, what murders by Stub Peeter was committed, with the order of his Iudgement, as this picture doth more plainelye expresse.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: And sundry times he would goe through the Streetes of Collin, Bedbur, and Cperadt, in comely habit, and very ciuilly as one well knowen to all the inhabitants therabout, & oftentimes was he saluted of those whose fréendes and children he had buchered, though nothing suspected for the same.
title: A true discourse. Declaring the damnable life and death of one Stubbe Peeter, a most wicked sorcerer who in the likenes of a woolfe, committed many murders, continuing this diuelish practise 25. yeere

text: The laſt but yet that not of the leaſt importance, wherewith your heart is troubled, is that you cannot feele your ſelfe to be one of thoſe, whome God hath marked out to eternall life.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Our bodies to daie freſh and luſtie, and to morrowe wythered and dried vp, as a skinne bottle that hangeth in the ſmoke: and yet in time raiſed vp againe to haue naturall moiſture, and to performe with ſtrength and agilitie, as woorthy deedes as before.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: And againe: The ſtrong foundatiō of God remaineth ſure, & hath this ſeal, the lord knoweth who are his: & let euery one that calleth on the name of Chriſt depart from iniquitie.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: And in an other place biddeth euery one that is thirſtie, come ye to the waters: and ye that haue no ſiluer, come buy & eat: Come I ſay, buy wine and milke without ſiluer, and without money.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Hitherto I haue laboured, neither vnſoundly, as in regard of Gods trueth propounded, nor vnprofitably, as in reſpect of you afflicted, nor vndutifully, as inconſideration of my ſelfe trauailing, generally to deliuer generall comfortes againſt generall tranſgreſſions.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: But hitherto (I deliuer it with my griefe of heart, as a man ſenſiblie ſeeing and feeling gods hand vpon my ſelfe, both that and other waies alſo) my expectation and hope hath bene fruſtrat, and my power very ſhort and skant.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Or rather doth not God worke then moſte mightily and mercifully both when in mens eyes the way is ſtopped vp, not onely agaynſt a deed, but againſt hope or hart to conceiue it?
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Let two verie woorthy and plaine (one wherof is in the olde, and the other in the newe Teſtament) ſerue for all?
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Secondly, the verie lamentable complaintes and earneſt prayers, that Gods Children (who indeede are moſte, I had almoſt ſaid onely exerciſed that way, this I am ſure of, with fruite and profite) haue eſpeciallie in that diſtreſſed caſe, made and powred forth, doe plainlie proue it.
author: T. W. (Thomas Wilcox), 1549?-1608.
title: Large letters Three in number, containing much necessarie matter, for the intruction and comfort of such, as are distressed in conscience by feeling of sinne, and feare of Gods wrath. Written heeretof

text: Be they wanton be they wilde, Be they gentle be they milde: Be shée white be she browne, Dooth she skould or dooth she frowne, Let her doo what she shall: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: If that you bid her doo ought, If that she doo it not, And though that you be her goodman, You your selfe must doo it than, be it in kitchin or in hall: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: Be they halt be they lame, Be she Lady be she dame, If that she doo weare a pinne, Kéepe she tauerne or kéepe she Inne, Either bulke bouth or stall, please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: Be they ritch be they poore, Is she honest is she whore, Weare she cloth or Ueluet braue, Dooth she beg or dooth she craue, Weare she hat or silken call: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: Please one and please all, Be they great be they small, Be they little be they lowe, So pypeth the Crowe, sitting vpon a wall: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: Though it be some Crowes guise, Oftentimes to tell lyes, Yet this Crowes words dooth try, That her tale is no lye, For thus it is and euer shall: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: Be they sluttish be they gay, Loue they worke or loue they play, Whatsoeuer be theyr chéere, Drinke they Ale or drinke they béere, whether it be strong or small: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: BE they white be they black, Haue they a smock on their back, Or a kircher on her head, Whether they spin silke or thred, whatsoeuer they them call: please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: If the goodwife speake aloft, Sée that you then speake soft, Whether it be good or ill, Let her doo what she will: and to kéepe your selfe from thrall, please one and please all, please one and please all.
author: Tarlton, Richard, d. 1588.
title: A prettie newe ballad, intytuled: the crowe sits vpon the wall, please one and please all To the tune of, please one and please all.

text: But to retourne to the purpoſe againe: whereas M. Dorman hath here in one halfe leafe, heaped a greate number of euidente lies, as it were, in a packet together, I haue thought good to putte the reader in remembraunce of them, in order as thei lie.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: You ſée howe ſhamefully he alleageth Nazianzene his ſayinges of one God, as though they had beene ſpoken of one Pope, of whome Nazianzene neuer dreamed.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: Whiche is to ſaie: Let vs come to the leuell and marke of the holie ſcripture, whiche dooeth expounde it ſelf.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: The verie ſame thyng, although in other woordes, doeth S. Baſile in an epiſtle written by hym, to the biſhoppes of Italie and Fraunce, bewailyng therein the eſtate of his tyme, moſte plainely declare.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: For if euery Biſhop haue in ſolidum, that is to ſaie, fullie, and wholie that one Biſhoprike, or biſhoplie function and office, as S. Cyprian ſaieth, no one cā haue more, then the whole, and therefore, no one can be aboue all other.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: Thus ye ſe good readers, that I maie ſaie with ſaincte Paule, haue I proued onely by reaſons fetched from the dooynges of men, by examples of all common wealthes and ſocieties well gouerned, that in Chriſtes common weale there muſt be alſo one to rule?
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: S. Hierome ſaith: The leſſe dioceſſe or toune, or the poorer eſtate maketh not the biſhop lower, or leſſe in authoritie: the greater prouince, the greater citie, the greater riches make not a Biſhop greater in authoritie.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: And for more cautell, ſuche ſome alſo to be named for the ſaide authors, as haue not all learninge, vvit, nor diſcretion, but men of a diuers profeſſion, vvho haue yet ſome fight in Diuinitie, as ſtudientes of the ſame, for ſo they profeſſe them ſelues.
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.
title: A reproufe, written by Alexander Nowell, of a booke entituled, A proufe of certayne articles in religion denied by M. Iuell, set furth by Thomas Dorman, Bachiler of Diuinitie: and imprinted at Antvver

text: Dooe not the Papiſtes themſelues, forbiddyng the ſcriptures to be readde of the Laitie, kéepyng the ſcriptures hid in an vnknowen tongue, burnyng the ſcriptures written in knowen language, go as nere to this abominable hereſie of Suenkfeldius, as wee are moſte farre from the ſame?
author: Nowell, Alexander, 1507?-1602.

text: Than sayde ye kynge yu spekest as a proude clerke / but I shall abbate thy pryde or I leue the.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: Therfore let vs praye to thys glorious martyr / to be our aduocate / that by his peticion we may come vnto euerlastynge blysse.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: And well executed he his offyce / ī punysshynge the culpable / & cherisshynge ye good people / & dyuers tymes went to Rome to supporte & helpe holy chirche.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: And saynt Thomas wente to wynchester / & there prayed our lord deuoutly for holy churche / and to gyfe hym ayde & strength for to defende yt.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: And whan he had acomplisshed his pylgrymage / he was taken homwarde by the hethenmen / and brought in prison of a prince named Ameraūt where longe tyme he / and his felyshyp suffred moche peyne and sorowe.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: Saynt Thomas besought god of helpe & socoure / for ye bysshopps whiche ougte to be wt hym were moost ayenst hym.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: And thys perlament was holden at claryndon the.ix. yere of the kynges reygne and the yere of our lorde. xi.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: The pope wold not beleue hym but sent another cardynall whiche for more euydent toke the legge of the capon in his kerchyef / & affermed the same.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: And after thys / yet the sayd gylberde went agayne in to the holy land / and was.iii. yere or he came agayne / & thys chylde grewe forth tyll he was set to scole / and lerned well & be came vertuouse.
title: Here begynneth the lyfe of the blessed martyr Saynte Thomas

text: First you must take heed from time to time, what chaplains be put to the queene, seing they are the teachers of the whole court, namelie, that they be eloquent of toong, and good companions, not too precise in their conuersation.
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: Howe can I tell hir that all is well, when I haue bin constrained to tell diuers Preachers, that haue so sore vrged mee with the text, that I coulde wishe things were amended, but the Q. will not at any hand?
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: This is excellent, I am verie willing to do this, for it will helpe forward our owne cause: nowe go on and tell mee what is to be doone further.
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: I woulde I might see that once come to passe, we haue laboured for it hitherto, and neuer could attaine vnto it neyther will the Church euer bee in quiet vntill you all be turned out.
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: They stop the mouth of the sheepeheardes, and set at liberty the rauening wolues, and turne the foxes among the lambes.
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: You say true, but what if it shall fall out, that the aduersarie be not blameworthy, neither in matter nor manner?
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: I do not beleeue you, albeit I cannot controll you in it, because I haue not bin in England of late, but what will come of it, if it be so?
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: Me thinks this man should be an vnfit assistant, for if he be a right Papist, he will labor to erect the Popes kingdom, and so to crosse you.
author: Udall, John, 1560?-1592.
title: The state of the Church of Englande laide open in a conference betweene Diotrephes a bishop, Tertullus a papist, Demetrius an vsurer, Pandocheus an in-keeper, and Paule a preacher of the word of God.

text: Let the meanes be as good as it will, I praise God for the successe of it, howsoeuer the contrary was meant.

text: For the curious conceited fellows that liue now in the world, thogh not poſſeſt with any great ſtore of malice nor wit, but are yet of ſuch a fine ieſting humor, that they wil dry-bob any man that writes, of what ſubiect ſoeuer.

text: But ſhe that was content to be deceiued, loued him ſo well, that ſhe had wholly forgotten the maner that women ought to vſe, in refuſing men.

text: The Lord of Boniuet to find the ſecret of his heart, feined to ſhew him his, and that he loued a Gentlewoman whom hee neuer thought vpon, deſiring him to keepe his ſecret, and beſought him that their harts and mindes might be all one.

title: The queen of Nauarres tales Containing, verie pleasant discourses of fortunate louers. Now newly translated out of French into English.

text: The maid obeyed her miſtris: and when night came the Gentlewoman laide her ſelfe in hir maides bed, determining if it were true, to correct her ſonne ſo well, that neuer after he ſhould deſire to lie with maide againe.
author: Marguerite, Queen, consort of Henry II, King of Navarre, 1492-1549.

text: Of that I aſſure you ſaid ſhe, and in ſuch manner, that if he found not a good ſurgeon, I think the markes will eaſily appeere.

text: For his courage he durſt haue gone into any baudy houſe, and would haue come out againe as honeſt a man as when he went firſt in.

text: You loue a woman already in yeares, and of no great beauty, in reſpect of me, and I loue a Gentleman younger, fairer, and amiabler then you.

text: It is not then the beautie or perſon of your mayd that made you finde ſuch pleaſure at this time; but it is ſinne and filthy luſt that burneth in your heart, and makes your head ſo madde, that you had taken a goate at that time for a wench.
author: Marguerite, Queen, consort of Henry II, King of Navarre, 1492-1549.

text: Nature that ſtoode faſt by, where ſhe might both heare and ſee, and yet vnſeene her ſelfe, was wel pleaſed with this firſt ſalutation, and the Spaniard thus departed.

author: Ochino, Bernardino, 1487-1564.

author: Ochino, Bernardino, 1487-1564.

author: Ochino, Bernardino, 1487-1564.

author: Ochino, Bernardino, 1487-1564.

author: Ochino, Bernardino, 1487-1564.

text: Whan Uirginius consull sawe afar of, his ennemies racynge out all abrode, he commanded his to pitche theyr dartes in the grounde, and reste them: then with his army lusty and fresche he sette on the other nowe almost breathelesse, and put them to flyghte.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.

text: The Aeginenses, what tyme their wyues and chyldern were slayne of the Uiathotiens, chose rather to behold the turment of those their so dere pledges, than to fall from the Romayns.

title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: VUhan Philip coulde by noo power get the castel Trinassum, he began to caste vp erthe before the walles, and made as thoughe he wolde vndermyne theym.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: VUhan C. Marius had vanquyshed the Almaynes in battayle, bycause the nyghte was at hande, he enclosed the resydue, fearynge and kepynge them all nyght wakynge, by noyse and crienge of a fewe souldiours. wherby on the morow he more easily ouercame theym, disquieted all the nyght before.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: And within a whyle after, beinge soore greued with thyrst, he restored to thē the water, corrupted with the herbe Helleborus: which water, whā they had dronke, cast them into a las ke. and so deceyued, he toke them.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: He that can beste rule his lyght harneised, lette hym inuade eyther wynge of his ennemies, settynge the archers in the forefront, whiche is the fyfte maner.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: Sylla commanded the cohort and centurions, throughe whose warde their ennemies had broken, to stande before the pauilyons of the heed capitayns, helmed and vngyrded.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: He hath lyttell wylle to trauayle, lyttell loue to his countrey, that seeth before his eies, your hyghnesse thus occupied: and yet is nothynge pricked, to do that he thinketh may serue his countrey.
author: Frontinus, Sextus Julius.
title: The strategemes, sleyghtes, and policies of warre, gathered togyther, by S. Iulius Frontinus, and translated into Englyshe, by Rycharde Morysine

text: Than he ordered his foote men in thre battayles, leauynge spaces for the lyght harneysed, and for the horsemen whome he sette vttermoste of all, that whanne nede requyred, he myghte sende theym forthe.

text: After that hée had done this ſo Tragicall an act, hée finiſhed his iourney to Fes, to the intent for to thruſt his ſonne Muley Mahomet vpon the Feſſans for their Prince and ſole heir of all his kingdomes, & ſo force them to ſweare faith & obedience vnto him.

author: Polemon, John.

text: But ſéeing there was now no time at all left for to conſult, and they ſaw that our men drew towards them couragiouſly, they alſo prepared all things neceſſarie for fight.

text: The Turke with his Mahomes ſhall loſe his Scepter, and a great chaunge in his regiment thorough hunger and warrs, ſo that moſt will rather ſeek helpe of the Chriſtians, then at his hands.

title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: To the ninth, which is: There will alſo ariſe great Earthquakes, and the fruit of trees will be very ſtrange and hollow within.

text: For were hee throughly appoſed, I doubt he would hardly ſhew the cauſes Philoſophicall and Naturall of Earthquakes, and whereof the ſaide Earthquakes are cauſed and ingendred, in that his doctrine hath beene ſo groſſe and palpable in the reſt.
author: T. R.
title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: For that towarde the ende of the worlde, Chriſt hath promiſed to increaſe the nūber of his elect, as alſo that his truth ſhall perſeuer vnto the ende & in the ende.
author: T. R.
title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: Laſtly to the tenth, which is: On ſaint Bartholomews day, will be great mouinges of the earth, both on hilles and vallies, for feare whereof fewe ſhall remaine aliue.

title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: All vvhiche are manifeſt tokens of Gods heauy diſpleaſure euen at hand which partly we feele by this bitter dearth vvithout neede, through out all the land.

title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: And the ſame Flouds to exceed, eſpecially, in Calabria, where no doubt, then Calaber-furres will bee deare, for that the Calaber-ſkinns wil be moſt drowned, which may cauſe ſome lamentation in the Budge-row in the VVinter following.
author: T. R.
title: A confutation of the tenne great plagues, prognosticated by Iohn Doleta from the country of Calabria, to happen in the yeare of our Lorde, 1587

text: Either els that much fruite the ſaide yeare will proue worme-eaten, & conſequently hollow within, which thing is nothing ſtrange.

text: And concernynge the resurrectyō, it is an article of our fayth: and proued there sufficiētlye and that it shall be by the power of Chryste, is also the open scrypture.

title: Wycklyffes wycket whyche he made in Kyng Rycards daye the second in the yere of our lorde God M.CCCCCV.

text: I beleue yt my redemerlyueth & yt in ye last day I shal rise out of ye erth, & ī my flesse shall se my sauiour, this my hope is layd vp in my bosome.

title: Wycklyffes wycket whyche he made in Kyng Rycards daye the second in the yere of our lorde God M.CCCCCV.

text: And agayne he sayethe ye shall not thynke that God lyuynge is not lyke to golde, syluer, ether any grauen thynge, or paynted by crafte, eyther taughte of man, for God despisethe the tyme of the vnknowen thynges.

title: Wycklyffes wycket whyche he made in Kyng Rycards daye the second in the yere of our lorde God M.CCCCCV.

text: And by that woorde vnderstande an attonemaker, a peace maker & bringer in to grace & fauour, hauyng ful power so to do.

text: Also in another place he calleth his passyon a cuppe, Math. xx. where the mother of zebedeus sonnes came to hym, & axed of hym that her two sonnes when he came to his kyngdome myght syt one of his ryght syde & one at his left syde.
author: Wycliffe, John, d. 1384.
title: Wycklyffes wycket whyche he made in Kyng Rycards daye the second in the yere of our lorde God M.CCCCCV.

text: I Beseche ye brethren in the lorde Christ Iesu, and for the loue of hys spirite to praye with me, that we may be vessels to his laude and praise what tyme so euer it pleaseth hym to call vpon vs. Romanes.xv.

title: Wycklyffes wycket whyche he made in Kyng Rycards daye the second in the yere of our lorde God M.CCCCCV.

text: AS the Coleryke hath nature of fyre hote and drye / natually is lene and ſklender / couetous / yrefull / haſty / braynles / folyſſhe / malycyous / deceytfull / and ſubtyll / where he beſtoweth his wyt.

author: Ptolemy, 2nd cent. Tetrabiblos.

author: Ptolemy, 2nd cent. Tetrabiblos.

text: And is the exaltacion of Saturne For the wether begynneth to waxe colde in this monthe of Septembre / and Saturne is the planet and the lorde of colde that exalteth in great heyghte / whan that he entreth in to the ſygne of Libra.
author: Ptolemy, 2nd cent. Tetrabiblos.
title: Here begynneth the compost of Ptholomeus, prynce of astronomye: translated oute of Frenche in to Englysshe, for them that wolde haue knowlege of the compost

text: For the whiche it behoueth firſte to knowe that the yere is deuyded in.iiii. partyes (as it hathe ben ſayd before) that is to wyt Pryme tyme / Some / Herueſt / & wynter / that ben compared to the.iiii.
author: Ptolemy, 2nd cent. Tetrabiblos.
title: Here begynneth the compost of Ptholomeus, prynce of astronomye: translated oute of Frenche in to Englysshe, for them that wolde haue knowlege of the compost

text: And whan the nombre is fayled / he muſt begyn at the houre that he wold know what planet reygneth.

text: Vnder the whiche ſygne ryſeth another fyxed ſterre / which Aſtronomyers calle the golden cuppe / and is in the.xiii. degree of the ſayd ſygne towarde the partye merydyonall.
author: Ptolemy, 2nd cent. Tetrabiblos.
title: Here begynneth the compost of Ptholomeus, prynce of astronomye: translated oute of Frenche in to Englysshe, for them that wolde haue knowlege of the compost

text: After that a man ought to knowe that the erthe is in the myddes of the worlde / for it is the heuyeſt element.

text: And that goodly Citie Ieruſalem, for their abhomination was made deſolate, and not one ſtone left vppon an other.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: And as before the deſtructions of Sodome and Gomorra, appeared like wonders, but they would not call to God for mercy, and ſo were cōſumed with Fire and Brimſtone.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: For as before the deſtruction of the firſt World, like ſignes and tokens appeared, & yet they would not turne from their wickedneſſe, and ſo were drowned in the Flood.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: And now let vs beare in mynde the fourth Starre, that was ſeene in Calabria, which ſignifieth great alteration this yeere. 1587. and that the world will not long indure, God make vs all ready againſt the day of the Lorde.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: SEcondly, there ſhall come a marueilous great water Flood vpon our Lady day in Lent, being vpon the 25. day of March, and by reaſon of the fearfulneſſe thereof many people may dye.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: FIftly, Infidels and Hereticks through great feare and dread, will flye and gather together, and a great parte of Chriſtindome, ſhall be in daunger to be ouerthrowne, which God defend.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: SEauently, there will be throughout the world great change, and alteration in Religion, and wonderfull ſtraunge newes vnto all people as conſerning the ſame.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: EIghtly, the Turke with his God Mahomet shal loſe his Scepter, and a great change and alteratiō; in his Regement, through hunger and warres, ſo that the moſt parte of them will rather ſeeke for reliefe by the Chriſtians then at his hands.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut
title: Straunge newes out of Calabria prognosticated in the yere 1586, vpon the yere 87. and what shall happen in the said yere: Praying the Lord to be merciful vnto vs.

text: NInthly, there will alſo ariſe great Earthquakes, and the fruite of Trees will be very ſtraunge to be ſeene, and hollowe within.
author: Doleta, John, attributed name. aut

text: THe forme of the proceeding in this Court, was altogether according to the proceſſe of ſummary cauſes in the Ciuill Law.

title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THe Iudges of that Court were alwaies of the kings most honorable Councell appointed by the King to keepe his Councell bourd.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THE Court of Requeſts now ſo called, was, and is parcell of the Kings most honourable Councell, and ſo alwayes called, and eſteemed.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THat both parties, or the one of them be ſometimes commaunded to bring into the Court, all their Euidences, Writings, Miniments, Bondes, &c. concerning the cauſe.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: Matters of Annuities, extents, debt with ſpecialties, and without, deteining of euidences, rent, aſſurance of lands, &c.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THat the party Defendant attend De die, in diem on the Councell, till he haue made his aunſwere to the Plaintifs bill, and be licenced to depart vpon caution De Iudicio ſiſti, & Iudicato ſoluendo, and constitution of his Atturney and Counſell by name.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THe keeping of this Court was neuer heretofore tied to any place certeine; but onely where the Councell ſate, the ſuitors were to attend: But now of late for the eaſe of ſuitors, it hath bene kept in the White-hall in Weſtminſter, and onely in the Terme time. viz.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: THE cauſes wherewith they deale, and whereof they iudge, are of all ſorts: As Maritime, Eccleſiaſticall, Temporall, but properly of Temporall cauſes, and onely of the other ſort, as they are mixt with Temporall.
author: Caesar, Julius, Sir, 1558-1636.
title: The ancient state, authoritie, and proceedings of the Court of Requests 2 Octob. 1596.

text: But they ſhould reſt as Chriſt did, ſitting vpon Iacobs well: viz. vntill they are refreſhed, and then to it againe by Chriſts example: for my father worketh hitherto and I worke, ſaith hee.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: And as Paule commanded yt he which wil drinke wine, ſhould help to plant the vine, and him that liueth of the altar, to miniſter at the altar: and him that wil eate the milke, to feede the flock.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: Aske the ſhower of the Saints bloud els, which began with the bloud of Abell, and helde on to the bloud of Zacharias the ſonne of Barachias.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: And therefore was it a part of Paules care to ſaie to the Coloſſians, Admoniſhe Archippus to looke to his charge.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: Or as Dauid ſaid: Loe wee heard of the ſame at Ephrata, and found it in the Wood.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: But that which is here ſaid, That the chiefe prieſt came and they that were with him, giueth vs warning, how we come in companie with euill aſſociates, like Peter vvith the high prieſts ſeruants.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: Arams hoaſt labouring to get Eliſha the prophet, are led into Samaria by Eliſha himſelfe, where (of al the places of the world) they would not be.

title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: The voice which ſtroke Saule to, the ground, came not vntill hee vvas neere to Damaſcus, where hee meant to make hauocke of the church.
author: Phillips, George, fl. 1597.
title: The embassage of Gods angell. By George Phillips

text: But it is true, that thorough Gods permiſſion, the mightie often times ſurpriſe the meaner ſort: and that made the Philoſopher laughe in his ſleeue, to ſee great theeues leade little theeues to priſon.

text: More ouer they hadde leuer suffre some griefe in their bodies / than in reuoluyng what shuld be moste necessary, trauayle any thyng in theyr mindes.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: Also goodes happen to men that be of euyll disposytion / but so doth not good estimation, but cometh onely to them that endeuour them selfe with vertue to gette it.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: I haue not spoken this agayne all men but only againe them that be giltie in that which I haue rehersed.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: well gouerned, if thou perceyue them that ben vnder thy gouernaunce to be by thy dylygence welthy and more temperate in lyuynge.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: Moreouer if one shuld gader out of the said authors that which men cal sentences, wherin they perchance haue ben studiouse, in semblable wise towardes them shulde they be disposed, for they shuld with more plesure here a lyeng fable or fantasy, than the sayd preceptes made by moch connyng and diligence.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: Therfore the one and the other is to be vsed, than exchne that thyng, whiche in any of them is yll or semeth not conuenyent.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: And if a man take good hede, he shall fynde in theyr mutuall assembles and companies, that eyther they reproue other men, or els that they of other be in some thynge reproued.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: For in herynge such thynges they reioyce: but whan they perceyne to be labours and contentions in theyr affayres / than be they pensife.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: Finally this is apparraunte and certayne, who so euer wyl make or wryte any thynge pleasaunte and thankfull to the multytude, he may not seke for wordes or maters moste profitable / but for them that contayne most fables and leasynges.
author: Isocrates.
title: [The doctrinall of princis]

text: Becauſe he being God, and mā, hath ſuffered all the puniſhment due for my ſinnes, and hath fulfylled the lawe.

text: No, but two, as we haue ſayde before: for the other ſacramentes, can be no ſacraments, becauſe they want the manifeſt woordes of promiſe, which ſhoulde by a viſyble ſygne be ſealed, and becauſe there is no commaundement geuen of God, wherby we are bounde to obſerue them as ſacraments.

title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: I beleeue that as my bodye is nouriſhed with breade, and wyne, there broken, and powred for thee, that euen ſo my ſoule is nouriſhed ſpiritually by Chriſtes body, broken, and his bloodſhed; for the remiſſion of my ſynnes.
author: Cobhead, Thomas.
title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: I ſaye not ſo, Gods grace is not tyed to externe Elementes, we beleeue his promiſe, and therefore doubte not, but the chyldren of the faythfull are ſaued, although they paſſe awaye in their mothers wombe, for they are holye by vertue of the couenaunt.
author: Cobhead, Thomas.
title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: If any man be werie of the burden of ſinne, let him aſke for mercie, and he ſhall haue it.

text: No, for the Prophet Eſay ſayeth vnto the Lorde: thou art our Father, for Abraham knoweth vs not, neyther is Iſraell acquainted with vs.

title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: The cuppe naturallie, is a cuppe of wine, but ſacramentally, it is the cuppe of the Lordes blood & newe Teſtament.

title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: Thou ſhalt not make to thy ſelfe any grauen Image, nor the lykeneſſe of any thing that is in heauen aboue, or in the earth beneath, nor in the water vnder the earth, thou ſhalt not bow downe to them, nor worſhip them.
author: Cobhead, Thomas.
title: A briefe instruction, collected for the exercise of youth, and simple sort of people. / By Thomas Cobhead preacher..

text: No, but to remember my promiſe, and returne vnto God for the remiſſion of my ſinnes, and for his holy ſpirite, to leade mee into newneſſe of lyfe.
author: Cobhead, Thomas.

text: Indeed you say well, and I agree: but yet you know I am a poore man, and am a Pisoner.

text: And tell me first who thou thy selfe mayst be, That art a man, and yet doest gibe at me.

text: With that I rose, and to this poore man went, In hope to learne some nouils by his talke: Approching him, amidst his discontent, He asked me, if so I pleasd to walke?

title: The blacke dogge of Newgate both pithie and profitable for all readers.

text: Whilst thus I lay in Irons vnder ground, I heard a man that begged for releefe: And in a chaine of Iron was he bound, Whose clattering noyse filde full my heart with griefe, Begging one penny to buie a hundred bread, Hungerd and sterud, for want of food ny dead.
author: Hutton, Luke, d. 1596.
title: The blacke dogge of Newgate both pithie and profitable for all readers.

text: Honest man, you neede not doubt of his good meanyng towardes you: This is such a one as may do you pleasure, yf he please to vndertake it.

text: At first he gently tooke me by the hand, And bids we welcome, as I were his guest: You are a prisoner, I do vnderstand, And hether welcome are both bad and best.

title: The blacke dogge of Newgate both pithie and profitable for all readers.

text: Straight, of my friend I asked by and by, What it might be, who made me this reply.

text: Fayre friend, quoth I, if so thy will may be, To ease my griefe Ile giue thee any fee.

text: Preaſſe not then to ye enheritaunce of heuē thorow preſumpciō of thy good workes for if thou do / thou counteſt thy ſilfe holye and egall to him becauſe thou wilt take nothinge of him for nought: & ſo ſhalt thou falle as Lucifer felle for his pride.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: [Paitrikes places]

text: But knoweth yt he both maye ād will fulfill his worde / how can he thē diſpleaſe him? for thou canſt not do anye greater honoure to god / thē to counte him true.

text: He yt beleveth not goddes worde / beleveth not him ſelfe / & the goſpell is gods worde / ergo he yt beleueth not the goſpell beleueth not God him ſelfe / & conſequentlye they that beleue not the aboue writen and ſuch other / beleve not god.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: [Paitrikes places]

text: He that beleueth not goddes worde he coūteth hym falſe & a lyare / ād beleueth not yt he maye and will fullfyll his worde: and ſo he denyeth both the might of god ād god him ſelfe.
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: [Paitrikes places]

text: The fayth of chriſt / is to beleue in him / that ys to beleue his worde and to beleve that he wyll helpe the in all thy nede and delyuer the from al euell. thou wylt aſke me what worde?
author: Hamilton, Patrick, 1504?-1528.
title: [Paitrikes places]

text: For it biddeth vs kepe the cōmaundemētes of god / & yet is it not in our power to kepe anye off thē / ergo it biddeth vs do that is impoſſible for vs. Thou wilt ſaye where to doeth god bid vs do that is impoſſible for vs?

title: [Paitrikes places]

text: So I cōdēpne not good redis / But I codēpne ye falſe truſt in anye workes / for al ye workes yt a ma putteth cōfidēce in are therwith poyſoned & become evel.

text: Then how can it be but moſt neceſſary, to be diligent in getting, and diligent in ſtudying yt monumēts & bokes of worthy authors: out of which ſo many cōmodities, ſo many fruites, ſo many aduiſes, ſo many good coūſails, lerned leſſons, & prudent exhortatiōs may be gathered.

text: Howe then maye it bee, that the Pope maye poſſyblye denye GOD in woorke and deede, and not in woorde and doctrine.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Verily nothyng els, but that the Superioritie ouer other churches, was geuen to the pope, not by the Apoſtles, but by the fathers, and that for no greater or iuſter cauſe, then that the citie of Rome, at that tyme had dominion ouer the whole world.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Moreouer Peter was a Doctoure of all the worlde, and ſo were the reſte of the Apoſtles: for the Lorde ſayde to hym, as well as to the reſte of the Apoſtles, Go and preache the Goſpel to all nations.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Laſt of all, our aduerſaries ſay, that no decree may be made in the Church, without the Popes conſente, whyche in dede they may very well lay againſt vs, but we ſhall repaye oure aduerſaries with the ſame meaſure.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Beſydes this, they hold that the pope is byſhop of no certayne place, neither is he ſo called as other are, but ſimply without circumſcription, he is named a Biſhoppe.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Lette the olde cuſtome take place, whiche was, that the byſſhop of Alexandria ſhulde be chiefe, and haue the higheſt dignitie in Egypte, Lybia, and the.v. cities: bycauſe this is a cuſtome with the byſhop of Rome alſo.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: But yf I ſhuld pleade afore our Grekes, then myght the Latines haue iuſte cauſe to complayne of me, where as I make the Grecians, iudges ouer them, whom they thinke to be their aduerſaries, in matters Eccleſiaſticall.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.
title: A briefe treatise, conteynynge a playne and fruitfull declaration of the Popes vsurped primacye, written in Greeke aboue. vij. hundred yeres sens, by Nilus, an ancient archbyshop of Thessalonia and ne

text: Byſhoppes gathered togyther at Conſtantinople, called newe Rome, in the tyme of the moſte holye Emperour Theodoſius, the ſame alſo doo we ordeyne & decree, concernyng the honoures and prerogatiues of the ſaid church of Conſtantinople, or new Rome.
author: Cabasilas, Nicolaus, 14th cent.

author: Old, John, fl. 1545-1555.

text: No band of loue ſo ſtronge as knowledge is: Which who is he that may not learne of you, Whom learning doth with his lights throne endow?

text: Chaucer (by whom we will needes authoriſe our true engliſh) had more newe wordes for his time then any man needes to deuiſe now.

text: O had your perfect eye Organs to pierce Into that Chaos whence this ſtiffled verſe By violence breakes: where Gloweworme like doth ſhine In nights of ſorrow, this hid ſoule of mine: And how her genuine formes ſtruggle for birth, Vnder the clawes of this fowle Panther earth.
author: Homer.
title: Achilles shield Translated as the other seuen bookes of Homer, out of his eighteenth booke of Iliades. By George Chapman Gent.

text: But as ill lines new fild with incke vndryed, An empty Pen with their owne ſtuffe applied Can blot them out: ſo ſhall their wealth-burſt wombes Be made with emptie Penne their honours tombes.

title: Achilles shield Translated as the other seuen bookes of Homer, out of his eighteenth booke of Iliades. By George Chapman Gent.

text: Thus as the ſoule vpon the fleſh depends, Vertue muſt wait on wealth; we muſt make friends, Of the vnrighteous Mammon, and our ſleights, Muſt beare the formes of fooles or Paraſites.

text: Item that Ellis Mayſter Doctour Redmans ſeruaunte ſhewed me, that he dydde knowe that hys Mayſter had declared too Kynge Henrye the.viii. his Maieſtie, that faith onely iuſtifieth, but that doctryne as he thought was not to be taught the people, leaſt they ſhuld be negligent to do good workes.

author: Chedsey, Master.

text: On the other ſide, what is it to denie Ieſus Chriſt before men? is it not to do euen as you haue done?

text: It foloweth then that we muſt not ſerue the deuill therwith, polluting them with ſuperſtitions & Idolatries, but we muſt kéepe them in al purenes and holines for the ſeruice of our god.

text: But this is not al: come to that which followeth afterwarde, & conſider I praie you how many pernicious errors, & horrible blaſphemies are contained in ye ſixt and ſeuenth articles.

text: And ye which more is, this tē peſt came not at a ſodain or at vnawares as that of the Maſſacre, but lumbered a long time in the ayre before ye clap came.

text: Haue you euer read eyther in the olde or newe Teſtament, that the bloud and merites of Saintes ought to be coupled with the bloud and merit of Ieſus Chriſt thereby to race out ſinnes, and to ſatiſfie Gods iuſtice.

text: And what intertainment can you looke for at his handes at that laſt daie, and howe miſerable ſhal your eſtate bee, if hee account you ſuch?

title: A Christian and wholesom admonition directed to the Frenchmen, which are reuolted from true religion, and haue polluted themselues with the superstition and idolatrie of poperie.

text: And yet your owne conſcience telleth you that they ſuffered for righteouſnes ſake, and gaue their liues for the name of Ieſus Chriſt: and that they are therefore bleſſed, as Ieſus Chriſt pronounceth them to be.
author: Constant, Léonard, d. 1610.
title: A Christian and wholesom admonition directed to the Frenchmen, which are reuolted from true religion, and haue polluted themselues with the superstition and idolatrie of poperie.

text: He that is not with me, ſaith he, is againſt me, and hee that gathereth not with mee ſcattereth abroad.
author: Constant, Léonard, d. 1610.
title: A Christian and wholesom admonition directed to the Frenchmen, which are reuolted from true religion, and haue polluted themselues with the superstition and idolatrie of poperie.

text: Vp, courage take, And to that path full ſwiftlie runne, Which conſtant hath propoſde to you, Vp, vp, I ſay and enter now.
author: Constant, Léonard, d. 1610.
title: A Christian and wholesom admonition directed to the Frenchmen, which are reuolted from true religion, and haue polluted themselues with the superstition and idolatrie of poperie.

text: And therfore he which dwelleth not in Chriſte: & in whom Chriſt dwelleth not, doubtles eateth not Chriſtes fleſhe nor drinketh his bloud although to his iudgmēt, he eate the ſacramēt of ſo great a thing.
author: Broke, Thomas.
title: Certeyn meditations and thinges to be had in remembraunce, and well considered by euery Christia[n], before he receiue the sacrament of the body and bloude of Christ. Compiled by T. Broke.

text: For cōfirmacion wherof, thei ſay that man conſiſteth and is made of a bodie and of a ſoule, the bodi is a natural and a materiall ſubſtance, which is fed with natural and corporal ſuſtenaunce, & noryſhement.
author: Broke, Thomas.
title: Certeyn meditations and thinges to be had in remembraunce, and well considered by euery Christia[n], before he receiue the sacrament of the body and bloude of Christ. Compiled by T. Broke.

text: For Chriſt is like vnto vs his reaſonable creaturs in all thyngs (except onlie in ſyne) But our bodies after our reſurrection ſhalbe viſible: wherefore doubtles Chriſtes bodie ſhal alſo be viſible, wherſoeuer it be preſēt.
author: Broke, Thomas.
title: Certeyn meditations and thinges to be had in remembraunce, and well considered by euery Christia[n], before he receiue the sacrament of the body and bloude of Christ. Compiled by T. Broke.

text: If we be one wyth our head Chriſt, and in heauen wyth hym to whome alſo he hath geuen eternall lyfe: Howe can ſynne hell or deathe preuayle agaynſt vs, his liuely membres?
author: Broke, Thomas.
title: Certeyn meditations and thinges to be had in remembraunce, and well considered by euery Christia[n], before he receiue the sacrament of the body and bloude of Christ. Compiled by T. Broke.

text: The godlie and ye vngodlie receyuethe ſacramente ſaye they, but the thynge repreſented in and bi the ſacramēt, which is Chriſtes bodie broken and his bloude ſhed out for the remiſſion of our ſynnes: no man cā eate excepte the faytheful by fayth.
author: Broke, Thomas.
title: Certeyn meditations and thinges to be had in remembraunce, and well considered by euery Christia[n], before he receiue the sacrament of the body and bloude of Christ. Compiled by T. Broke.

text: Alſo S. Peter in the Actes ſayth, repent and turne you, that your ſynnes may be done awaye.

text: Alſo ye ſame doctour ſaint Auguſttine again ſaith, truly this bread, requireth the hongre of ye inward man.

text: They are become ſtraungers to God, for the blindeneſſe of their harte, that haue yeelded them ſelues to wantonneſſe or fleshly luſtes.

text: For with to much plentie and aboundaunce of meates and drinks our mindes become wanton, leacherous, & diſſolute.

text: And agaynſt the ſuggeſtions and inward intiſementes to cuil, of Sathan, which here is ſignified, by the worde (Diuell.)

text: For except vicious luſt and deſire, be put out of our mindes, it groweth and waxeth ſtronge by litle and litle, like ſeede ſowen, vntill it bring forth deadly ſinne: ſuch ſinne, that vnleſſe God in mercie mightely deliuer vs from it will bryng vs to euerlaſtyng death and deſtruction.
author: Hergest, William.
title: The right rule of Christian chastitie profitable to bee read of all godly and vertuous youthes of both sexe, bee they gentlemen or gentlewomen, or of inferiour state, whatsoeuer. Collected and written

text: Becauſe they gaue them ſelues to filthy and abhominable luſt, God gaue them ouer into a reprobate ſence or minde.
author: Hergest, William.
title: The right rule of Christian chastitie profitable to bee read of all godly and vertuous youthes of both sexe, bee they gentlemen or gentlewomen, or of inferiour state, whatsoeuer. Collected and written

text: What greater iniury, ſpite, or contumely then this ran wee doo to our bodyes, that were made to liue and raigne with Chriſte in bliſſe vnſpeakeable, world without ende?
author: Hergest, William.
title: The right rule of Christian chastitie profitable to bee read of all godly and vertuous youthes of both sexe, bee they gentlemen or gentlewomen, or of inferiour state, whatsoeuer. Collected and written

text: And therfore great ſhame would it be for vs, then to yelde to the Diuell, and to become his vaſſals, and bondflanes, and to ſuffer him to rule and reigue in vs by his filthie ſpirite of Fornication and whoredome.
author: Hergest, William.

text: THyrdly, leaſt wee looſe the excellent giftes, that God in merrie hath beſtowed vppon us: and that we may reteyne; and keepe the fauour of God; the holy Ghoſte, Faith, Repentance, Juſtification, and all other ſpiritual giftes.

text: If men wyll not be wyllyngly blinde, they ſhall eaſily ſee euen by a due and euident profe in reſon, though grace dothe not yet by the worde of Chriſt enter into them, howe ſmall thauctoritie of the byſhop of Rome is, by the laufull denyall of the Duke of Mantua for the place.

text: If Prynces haue gyuen hym this auctoritie, to calle a Councille, is hit not neceſſarye, that they gyue hym alſo, all thoſe thynges, withoute the whiche he canne not exercyſe that his power?

text: BBs. & parish priestes, curates, preachers & all: Neither (saith D. S.) can this euer be recouered.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: Our sauiour Christ whiles he was here emongst vs, came not into the world as thē to iudge or cōdēne the world, but that the world through him might be saued.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: But in this high Cōmission of the church of Englād is an opē cōmixture & confusiō of ciuil & ecclesiastical offices & causes; a new diuised ordināce with new officers, new proceedings, and a strange course not heard or read of in the whole word of God.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: Thus make they him a minister after an other order thē that which he hath set downe in his Testament, then that wherunto he was annointed of his Father, & that with an othe, & that for euer.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: Which whiles these learned Doctors & diep diuines (as they in their stile and banner write themselues) haue labored by the light of their owne pregnāt wittes to vnlose, they haue the further encombred themselues, & intangled their miserable followers.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: God plighteth not his fauour and protection vnto vs, longer then we vowe our obedience, and keep our faith vnto him.

title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: But we reade not that he went vp to offer or communicate with them according to the law, but rather to teach & instruct them, & to call them to repentāce & amendment of life.

text: The prophets they giue out to be vnderstood of such ministers only, as haue the gift of preaching (as they call yt) holding yt lawful for none els to speake of the scriptures by way of interpretation and prophecie, especially to expound them in the Church or Congregation.
author: Barrow, Henry, 1550?-1593.
title: A brief discouerie of the false church. 1590

text: I am loth for to rayle, as Baldwin hath begun For so betwine vs both: a fayre threde shuld be spun This miche I haue writen: that the truith shuld be knowen And that the falsite: shuld quite be ouerthro wen.
title: A Short answere to the boke called Beware the cat

text: Therfore ientyl reder: beware what credence thou ghive The truth here conteyned: thou mayst boldly belive Baldwins toyes do belong: to thee or any other As well as they do touche Stremer, his pore brother.
